children.text: gavyaṃ yavyaṃ yanto dīrghāheṣaṃ varam aruṇyo varanta ||
children.translated_text: Seeking wealth in cattle and barley, the ruddy ones chose the boon that lasts through long days.

children.text: Chapter 141
baﾱ itthā tad vapuṣe dhāyi darśataṃ devasya bhargaḥ sahaso yato jani
children.translated_text: Indeed, thus that visible beauty was set in his form, the divine radiance of the god born from strength;

children.text: yad īm upa hvarate sādhate matir ṛtasya dhenā anayanta sasrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when inspired thought calls upon him and accomplishes its aim, the flowing streams of truth have led him on.

children.text: pṛkṣo vapuḥ pitumān nitya ā śaye dvitīyam ā saptaśivāsu mātṛṣu
children.translated_text: His form is rich in nourishment, possessed of food, lying always in the first place; a second is among the seven auspicious mothers,

children.text: tṛtīyam asya vṛṣabhasya dohase daśapramatiṃ janayanta yoṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a third, for the milking of this bull, the women generated with tenfold insight.

children.text: nir yad īm budhnān mahiṣasya varpasa īśānāsaḥ śavasā kranta sūrayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the powerful lords, with might, cut forth the roots of the great buffalo's form, the inspired seers,

children.text: yad īm anu pradivo madhva ādhave guhā santam mātariśvā mathāyati ||
children.translated_text: when after the primeval one, for the pouring of honey, <s>Mātariśvan</s> churned him, hidden in the secret place.

children.text: pra yat pituḥ paramān nīyate pary ā pṛkṣudho vīrudho daṃsu rohati
children.translated_text: When he is led around from the father's highest place, he rises among the nourishing plants and shoots,

children.text: ubhā yad asya januṣaṃ yad invata ād id yaviṣṭho abhavad ghṛṇā śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: when both births of his are stirred; then the youngest became blazing and pure.

children.text: ād in mātṝr āviśad yāsv ā śucir ahiṃsyamāna urviyā vi vāvṛdhe
children.translated_text: Then he entered the mothers, among whom, pure and unharmed, he grew widely.

children.text: anu yat pūrvā aruhat sanājuvo ni navyasīṣv avarāsu dhāvate ||
children.translated_text: When he climbed up after the former ones, born together, he runs down among the newer, lower ones.

children.text: ād iddhotāraṃ vṛṇate diviṣṭiṣu bhagam iva papṛcānāsa ṛñjate
children.translated_text: Then in the heavenly contests they choose him as <s>hotar</s> (sacrificial priest); questioning him like <s>Bhaga</s>, they adorn him,

children.text: devān yat kratvā majmanā puruṣṭuto martaṃ śaṃsaṃ viśvadhā veti dhāyase ||
children.translated_text: when, much-praised, with will and greatness he goes in every way among gods and mortals for praise and support.

children.text: vi yad asthād yajato vātacodito hvāro na vakvā jaraṇā anākṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: When the worshipful one stood apart, wind-driven, like a crooked, unshaped old trunk,

children.text: tasya patman dakṣuṣaḥ kṛṣṇajaṃhasaḥ śucijanmano raja ā vyadhvanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: over the path of that skilful one, black-tracked and pure-born, the dust spread out.

children.text: ratho na yātaḥ śikvabhiḥ kṛto dyām aṅgebhir aruṣebhir īyate
children.translated_text: Like a chariot set in motion, made with strong parts, he goes to heaven with ruddy limbs.

children.text: ād asya te kṛṣṇāso dakṣi sūrayaḥ śūrasyeva tveṣathād īṣate vayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then his dark tracks, O skilful seers, hasten onward from the hero's flashing onset like birds.

children.text: tvayā hy agne varuṇo dhṛtavrato mitraḥ śāśadre aryamā sudānavaḥ
children.translated_text: Through you, O <s>Agni</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s> of firm vow, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, the good givers, have obtained strength,

children.text: yat sīm anu kratunā viśvathā vibhur arān na nemiḥ paribhūr ajāyathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when, following their will, all-pervading and encompassing like a rim around spokes, you were born.

children.text: tvam agne śaśamānāya sunvate ratnaṃ yaviṣṭha devatātim invasi
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Agni</s>, youngest one, set divine favor and treasure in motion for the praising soma-presser.

children.text: taṃ tvā nu navyaṃ sahaso yuvan vayam bhagaṃ na kāre mahiratna dhīmahi ||
children.translated_text: Now we, O youthful son of strength, think of you, the new one, like <s>Bhaga</s> for the singer, O rich in great treasure.

children.text: asme rayiṃ na svarthaṃ damūnasam bhagaṃ dakṣaṃ na papṛcāsi dharṇasim
children.translated_text: Among us you fill up wealth, like a good possession, householding, <s>Bhaga</s>-like skill, and sustaining power,

children.text: raśmīṃr iva yo yamati janmanī ubhe devānāṃ śaṃsam ṛta ā ca sukratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the wise one restrains both births like reins, and, according to truth, the praise of the gods.

children.text: uta naḥ sudyotmā jīrāśvo hotā mandraḥ śṛṇavac candrarathaḥ
children.translated_text: And may bright-shining <s>Agni</s>, the swift-horsed <s>hotar</s>, delightful and moon-bright of chariot, hear us;

children.text: sa no neṣan neṣatamair amūro 'gnir vāmaṃ suvitaṃ vasyo accha ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Agni</s>, unconfused, lead us by the best leadings toward lovely prosperity and better welfare.

children.text: astāvy agniḥ śimīvadbhir arkaiḥ sāmrājyāya prataraṃ dadhānaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> has been praised by active songs, setting forth a further course toward sovereignty.

children.text: amī ca ye maghavāno vayaṃ ca mihaṃ na sūro ati niṣ ṭatanyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Both those bountiful ones and we have stretched beyond, like the sun beyond mist.

children.text: Chapter 142
samiddho agna ā vaha devāṁ adya yatasruce
children.translated_text: Kindled, O <s>Agni</s>, bring the gods today to the one whose ladle is stretched out.

children.text: tantuṃ tanuṣva pūrvyaṃ sutasomāya dāśuṣe ||
children.translated_text: Stretch out the ancient thread for the generous worshiper whose soma has been pressed.

children.text: ghṛtavantam upa māsi madhumantaṃ tanūnapāt
children.translated_text: O <s>Tanūnapāt</s>, come near the ghee-rich, honey-sweet

children.text: yajñaṃ viprasya māvataḥ śaśamānasya dāśuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sacrifice of the inspired, bounteous worshiper who praises.

children.text: śuciḥ pāvako adbhuto madhvā yajñam mimikṣati
children.translated_text: Pure, purifying, wondrous, he mingles the sacrifice with honey;

children.text: narāśaṃsas trir ā divo devo deveṣu yajñiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>, god among the gods, worthy of sacrifice, comes three times from heaven.

children.text: īﾱito agna ā vahendraṃ citram iha priyam
children.translated_text: Praised, O <s>Agni</s>, bring here beloved, splendid <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: iyaṃ hi tvā matir mamācchā sujihva vacyate ||
children.translated_text: for this thought of mine is spoken toward you, O fair-tongued one.

children.text: stṛṇānāso yatasruco barhir yajñe svadhvare
children.translated_text: Spreading the sacrificial grass, with ladles outstretched, at the well-ordered <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice),

children.text: vṛñje devavyacastamam indrāya śarma saprathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I choose for <s>Indra</s> the shelter that extends farthest and is most spacious for the gods.

children.text: vi śrayantām ṛtāvṛdhaḥ prayai devebhyo mahīḥ
children.translated_text: Let the great doors, increasers of truth, open wide in their going forth for the gods,

children.text: pāvakāsaḥ puruspṛho dvāro devīr asaścataḥ ||
children.translated_text: pure, much-desired, divine doors, never failing.

children.text: ā bhandamāne upāke naktoṣāsā supeśasā
children.translated_text: Let <s>Night</s> and <s>Dawn</s>, drawing near, being praised, beautifully adorned,

children.text: yahvī ṛtasya mātarā sīdatām barhir ā sumat ||
children.translated_text: the two great mothers of truth, sit down willingly upon the sacrificial grass.

children.text: mandrajihvā jugurvaṇī hotārā daivyā kavī
children.translated_text: The two divine <s>hotars</s> (sacrificial priests), poets, sweet-tongued and praising,

children.text: yajñaṃ no yakṣatām imaṃ sidhram adya divispṛśam ||
children.translated_text: let them worship for us this <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), successful today and touching heaven.

children.text: śucir deveṣv arpitā hotrā marutsu bhāratī
children.translated_text: Pure, established among the gods as the priestly office, <s>Bhāratī</s> among the <s>Maruts</s>,

children.text: iﾱā sarasvatī mahī barhiḥ sīdantu yajñiyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: let <s>Iḷā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and great <s>Mahī</s>, worthy of sacrifice, sit upon the grass.

children.text: tan nas turīpam adbhutam puru vāram puru tmanā
children.translated_text: That wondrous, many-formed, much-choosing work of ours,

children.text: tvaṣṭā poṣāya vi ṣyatu rāye nābhā no asmayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: let <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> unfold for nourishment and wealth, as a kinsman who cares for us.

children.text: avasṛjann upa tmanā devān yakṣi vanaspate
children.translated_text: Releasing them from yourself, worship the gods, O <s>Vanaspati</s>;

children.text: agnir havyā suṣūdati devo deveṣu medhiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, wise god among the gods, makes the oblations well prepared.

children.text: pūṣaṇvate marutvate viśvadevāya vāyave
children.translated_text: For the one accompanied by <s>Pūṣan</s>, by the <s>Maruts</s>, for <s>Viśvadeva</s>, for <s>Vāyu</s>,

children.text: svāhā gāyatravepase havyam indrāya kartana ||
children.translated_text: make the oblation with svāhā for <s>Indra</s>, whose form is the Gāyatra chant.

children.text: svāhākṛtāny ā gahy upa havyāni vītaye
children.translated_text: Come to the oblations made with svāhā, for enjoyment;

children.text: indrā gahi śrudhī havaṃ tvāṃ havante adhvare ||
children.translated_text: come, O <s>Indra</s>; hear the call. They call you in the sacrifice.

children.text: Chapter 143
pra tavyasīṃ navyasīṃ dhītim agnaye vāco matiṃ sahasaḥ sūnave bhare
children.translated_text: I bring forward for <s>Agni</s>, the son of strength, a stronger, newer inspired thought, a voice and intention,

children.text: apāṃ napād yo vasubhiḥ saha priyo hotā pṛthivyāṃ ny asīdad ṛtviyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Apāṃ Napāt</s>, who, dear along with the <s>Vasus</s>, sat down as the seasonal <s>hotar</s> (sacrificial priest) on the earth.

children.text: sa jāyamānaḥ parame vyomany āvir agnir abhavan mātariśvane
children.translated_text: As he was being born in the highest heaven, <s>Agni</s> became manifest for <s>Mātariśvan</s>.

children.text: asya kratvā samidhānasya majmanā pra dyāvā śociḥ pṛthivī arocayat ||
children.translated_text: By the will and greatness of him as he was kindled, his flame made heaven and earth shine forth.

children.text: asya tveṣā ajarā asya bhānavaḥ susaṃdṛśaḥ supratīkasya sudyutaḥ
children.translated_text: His impetuous, undecaying rays, easy to behold, belong to the fair-faced, brightly shining one.

children.text: bhātvakṣaso aty aktur na sindhavo 'gne rejante asasanto ajarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: With shining forms, like rivers beyond the night, O <s>Agni</s>, the unaging ones tremble, not resting.

children.text: yam erire bhṛgavo viśvavedasaṃ nābhā pṛthivyā bhuvanasya majmanā
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhṛgus</s> set in motion him, the all-knowing one, at the navel of the earth, by the greatness of the world.

children.text: agniṃ taṃ gīrbhir hinuhi sva ā dame ya eko vasvo varuṇo na rājati ||
children.translated_text: Urge that <s>Agni</s> onward with songs in his own house, he who alone shines as lord of wealth like <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: na yo varāya marutām iva svanaḥ seneva sṛṣṭā divyā yathāśaniḥ
children.translated_text: There is none like his roar, as of the <s>Maruts</s>, like an army let loose, like a heavenly thunderbolt.

children.text: agnir jambhais tigitair atti bharvati yodho na śatrūn sa vanā ny ṛñjate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> devours with sharp jaws and bears down; like a warrior upon foes he assails the forests.

children.text: kuvin no agnir ucathasya vīr asad vasuṣ kuvid vasubhiḥ kāmam āvarat
children.translated_text: May <s>Agni</s> be the hero of our hymn; may the good one, with goods, fulfill our desire.

children.text: codaḥ kuvit tutujyāt sātaye dhiyaḥ śucipratīkaṃ tam ayā dhiyā gṛṇe ||
children.translated_text: May he as impeller urge our thoughts toward winning; I praise that bright-faced one with this thought.

children.text: ghṛtapratīkaṃ va ṛtasya dhūrṣadam agnim mitraṃ na samidhāna ṛñjate
children.translated_text: They adorn <s>Agni</s>, butter-faced, seated at the pole of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), like <s>Mitra</s> when he is kindled.

children.text: indhāno akro vidatheṣu dīdyacchukravarṇām ud u no yaṃsate dhiyam ||
children.translated_text: Kindled, the tireless one shines in the assemblies; may he raise up for us a bright-colored inspired thought.

children.text: aprayucchann aprayucchadbhir agne śivebhir naḥ pāyubhiḥ pāhi śagmaiḥ
children.translated_text: Without neglect, O <s>Agni</s>, protect us with your unfailing, auspicious, beneficial guardians.

children.text: adabdhebhir adṛpitebhir iṣṭe 'nimiṣadbhiḥ pari pāhi no jāḥ ||
children.translated_text: With uninjured, unproud guardians, O desired one, with unwinking ones, guard our people all around.

children.text: Chapter 144
eti pra hotā vratam asya māyayordhvāṃ dadhānaḥ śucipeśasaṃ dhiyam
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) goes forward to his rite by his wondrous power, holding upward his bright-formed thought.

children.text: abhi srucaḥ kramate dakṣiṇāvṛto yā asya dhāma prathamaṃ ha niṃsate ||
children.translated_text: Turned to the right, he steps toward the ladles, which at once touch his foremost seat.

children.text: abhīm ṛtasya dohanā anūṣata yonau devasya sadane parīvṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The milkings of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order) have sounded toward him, enclosed in the womb, in the seat of the god.

children.text: apām upasthe vibhṛto yad āvasad adha svadhā adhayad yābhir īyate ||
children.translated_text: When he had dwelt, borne in the lap of the waters, then he drank the innate powers by which he moves.

children.text: yuyūṣataḥ savayasā tad id vapuḥ samānam arthaṃ vitaritratā mithaḥ
children.translated_text: The two of the same age, wishing to unite, share that very form with one another, spreading a common purpose.

children.text: ād īm bhago na havyaḥ sam asmad ā voﾱhur na raśmīn sam ayaṃsta sārathiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, like <s>Bhaga</s>, fit to be invoked, he drew them together toward us, as a charioteer gathers the reins of a draught-horse.

children.text: yam īṃ dvā savayasā saparyataḥ samāne yonā mithunā samokasā
children.translated_text: Two of the same age worship him, in the same womb, a pair dwelling in one home.

children.text: divā na naktam palito yuvājani purū carann ajaro mānuṣā yugā ||
children.translated_text: Not by day nor by night, gray-haired yet young, he has been born, unaging, wandering through many human ages.

children.text: tam īṃ hinvanti dhītayo daśa vriśo devam martāsa ūtaye havāmahe
children.translated_text: The ten inspired thoughts urge him, the vigorous god; we mortals call him for aid.

children.text: dhanor adhi pravata ā sa ṛṇvaty abhivrajadbhir vayunā navādhita ||
children.translated_text: From the slope above the bow he rushes on, newly kindled with those who advance and with their skill.

children.text: tvaṃ hy agne divyasya rājasi tvam pārthivasya paśupā iva tmanā
children.translated_text: For you, O <s>Agni</s>, rule what is heavenly; you yourself rule what is earthly, like a guardian of cattle.

children.text: enī ta ete bṛhatī abhiśriyā hiraṇyayī vakvarī barhir āśāte ||
children.translated_text: These two great, golden, winding ones, with splendor, sit down upon the sacred grass for you.

children.text: agne juṣasva prati harya tad vaco mandra svadhāva ṛtajāta sukrato
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, enjoy and welcome that speech, O gladdening, self-powered, <s>ṛta</s>-born one of good insight.

children.text: yo viśvataḥ pratyaṅṅ asi darśato raṇvaḥ saṃdṛṣṭau pitumāṁ iva kṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You who face every side, visible and delightful to behold, are like a dwelling rich in nourishment.

children.text: Chapter 145
tam pṛcchatā sa jagāmā sa veda sa cikitvāṁ īyate sā nv īyate
children.translated_text: Ask him: he has gone, he knows; discerning, he goes, indeed he goes.

children.text: tasmin santi praśiṣas tasminn iṣṭayaḥ sa vājasya śavasaḥ śuṣmiṇas patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In him are commands, in him are offerings; he is lord of the prize, of strength, and of powerful force.

children.text: tam it pṛcchanti na simo vi pṛcchati sveneva dhīro manasā yad agrabhīt
children.translated_text: They ask him; no ordinary man questions him when the wise one has grasped it with his own mind.

children.text: na mṛṣyate prathamaṃ nāparaṃ vaco 'sya kratvā sacate apradṛpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The undeceived one, by his will, does not forget the first word or the later word.

children.text: tam id gacchanti juhvas tam arvatīr viśvāny ekaḥ śṛṇavad vacāṃsi me
children.translated_text: To him the tongues go, to him the mares; alone he will hear all my words.

children.text: purupraiṣas taturir yajñasādhano 'cchidrotiḥ śiśur ādatta saṃ rabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Much-summoned, overcoming, accomplishing the sacrifice, with unbroken aid, the child has taken hold of ardor.

children.text: upasthāyaṃ carati yat samārata sadyo jātas tatsāra yujyebhiḥ
children.translated_text: He moves nearby when they have come together; newborn at once, he fitted himself with his yokemates.

children.text: abhi śvāntam mṛśate nāndye mude yad īṃ gacchanty uśatīr apiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: He touches the panting one for joy and gladness when the eager ones go to him, who is set in place.

children.text: sa īm mṛgo apyo vanargur upa tvacy upamasyāṃ ni dhāyi
children.translated_text: This wild beast, hidden in the waters and moving in the forest, was placed under the skin, in the nearest place.

children.text: vy abravīd vayunā martyebhyo 'gnir vidvāṁ ṛtaciddhi satyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, knowing the ways among mortals, the knower of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), for he is true, spoke out.

children.text: Chapter 146
trimūrdhānaṃ saptaraśmiṃ gṛṇīṣe 'nūnam agnim pitror upasthe
children.translated_text: I praise <s>Agni</s>, three-headed, seven-rayed, not deficient, in the lap of his parents,

children.text: niṣattam asya carato dhruvasya viśvā divo rocanāpaprivāṃsam ||
children.translated_text: seated there, filling all the lights of heaven belonging to this moving, steadfast one.

children.text: ukṣā mahāṁ abhi vavakṣa ene ajaras tasthāv itaūtir ṛṣvaḥ
children.translated_text: The great bull has bellowed around this; unaging, lofty, with his help he has stood here.

children.text: urvyāḥ pado ni dadhāti sānau rihanty ūdho aruṣāso asya ||
children.translated_text: He sets his steps upon the ridge of the broad earth; his ruddy ones lick at his udder.

children.text: samānaṃ vatsam abhi saṃcarantī viṣvag dhenū vi carataḥ sumeke
children.translated_text: The two well-fashioned milk-cows move around the same calf, wandering apart in every direction.

children.text: anapavṛjyāṁ adhvano mimāne viśvān ketāṁ adhi maho dadhāne ||
children.translated_text: Measuring the path that cannot be turned aside, placing all signs upon the great one.

children.text: dhīrāsaḥ padaṃ kavayo nayanti nānā hṛdā rakṣamāṇā ajuryam
children.translated_text: The thoughtful seers lead the track, guarding in different hearts the undecaying one.

children.text: siṣāsantaḥ pary apaśyanta sindhum āvir ebhyo abhavat sūryo nṝn ||
children.translated_text: Desiring to win, they looked around the river; the sun became manifest to these men.

children.text: didṛkṣeṇyaḥ pari kāṣṭhāsu jenya īﾱenyo maho arbhāya jīvase
children.translated_text: He is worth seeing around the boundaries, victorious, praiseworthy for life, for great and small alike.

children.text: purutrā yad abhavat sūr ahaibhyo garbhebhyo maghavā viśvadarśataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the generous, all-seeing sun appeared in many places to them from the wombs.

children.text: Chapter 147
kathā te agne śucayanta āyor dadāśur vājebhir āśuṣāṇāḥ
children.translated_text: How have your shining worshipers, O <s>Agni</s>, giving eagerly with prizes,

children.text: ubhe yat toke tanaye dadhānā ṛtasya sāman raṇayanta devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: holding both offspring and descendants, made the gods rejoice in the chant of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order)?

children.text: bodhā me asya vacaso yaviṣṭha maṃhiṣṭhasya prabhṛtasya svadhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Awaken to this word of mine, youngest one, self-powered lord of the most generous offering.

children.text: pīyati tvo anu tvo gṛṇāti vandārus te tanvaṃ vande agne ||
children.translated_text: He swells after you; he praises after you; as your worshiper I honor your body, O <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: ye pāyavo māmateyaṃ te agne paśyanto andhaṃ duritād arakṣan
children.translated_text: Those guardians of yours, O <s>Agni</s>, who, seeing, protected <s>Māmateya</s> the blind man from distress,

children.text: rarakṣa tān sukṛto viśvavedā dipsanta id ripavo nāha debhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the all-knowing one has protected those doers of good; hostile enemies seeking to harm did not overpower them.

children.text: yo no agne ararivāṁ aghāyur arātīvā marcayati dvayena
children.translated_text: Whoever, O <s>Agni</s>, being ungenerous, evil-minded, and hostile to us, tries to harm us with duplicity...

children.text: mantro guruḥ punar astu so asmā anu mṛkṣīṣṭa tanvaṃ duruktaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: May the weighty spell again be there; may he wipe away from our body the evil words that have pursued us.

children.text: uta vā yaḥ sahasya pravidvān marto martam marcayati dvayena
children.translated_text: And if some mortal, O powerful one, knowingly makes a mortal wither by double-dealing,

children.text: ataḥ pāhi stavamāna stuvantam agne mākir no duritāya dhāyīḥ ||
children.translated_text: from that, O praised <s>Agni</s>, protect the one who praises and chants; let no one hand us over to misfortune.

children.text: Chapter 148
mathīd yad īṃ viṣṭo mātariśvā hotāraṃ viśvāpsuṃ viśvadevyam
children.translated_text: When <s>Mātariśvan</s> rubbed him out from the one spread abroad, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), all-pervading and belonging to all the gods,

children.text: ni yaṃ dadhur manuṣyāsu vikṣu svar ṇa citraṃ vapuṣe vibhāvam ||
children.translated_text: whom men set down among the human settlements, like the sun, bright and splendid in form.

children.text: dadānam in na dadabhanta manmāgnir varūtham mama tasya cākan
children.translated_text: Giving, he did not deceive my thoughts; <s>Agni</s> has favored my shelter and his own.

children.text: juṣanta viśvāny asya karmopastutim bharamāṇasya kāroḥ ||
children.translated_text: May all his works please him, as the singer bears his song of praise.

children.text: nitye cin nu yaṃ sadane jagṛbhre praśastibhir dadhire yajñiyāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Even in his constant seat the worshipful ones have grasped him and set him in place with praises.

children.text: pra sū nayanta gṛbhayanta iṣṭāv aśvāso na rathyo rārahāṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They lead him forward and take hold of him at the rite, like chariot-horses eagerly pulling the car.

children.text: purūṇi dasmo ni riṇāti jambhair ād rocate vana ā vibhāvā
children.translated_text: The wondrous one grinds up many things with his jaws; then the bright one shines in the wood.

children.text: ād asya vāto anu vāti śocir astur na śaryām asanām anu dyūn ||
children.translated_text: Then the wind blows after his flame, as an archer follows the arrow shot through the days.

children.text: na yaṃ ripavo na riṣaṇyavo garbhe santaṃ reṣaṇā reṣayanti
children.translated_text: Enemies and assailants do not harm him while he is in the womb, nor do those who seek to injure him injure him.

children.text: andhā apaśyā na dabhann abhikhyā nityāsa īm pretāro arakṣan ||
children.translated_text: The blind, not seeing, did not deceive him by their look; eternal guardians protected him as he went before.

children.text: Chapter 149
mahaḥ sa rāya eṣate patir dann ina inasya vasunaḥ pada ā
children.translated_text: He strives for great wealth, the lord who gives, for the footstep of precious goods.

children.text: upa dhrajantam adrayo vidhann it ||
children.translated_text: The stones, as they press close to the advancing one, worship him there.

children.text: sa yo vṛṣā narāṃ na rodasyoḥ śravobhir asti jīvapītasargaḥ
children.translated_text: He who is a bull among men, with fame in the two worlds, has a living draught set free.

children.text: pra yaḥ sasrāṇaḥ śiśrīta yonau ||
children.translated_text: He, streaming forth, has taken his place in the womb.

children.text: ā yaḥ puraṃ nārmiṇīm adīded atyaḥ kavir nabhanyo nārvā
children.translated_text: He who has lit up the stronghold rich in waters, like a swift horse, a sage born of the cloud, like a coursing steed,

children.text: sūro na rurukvāñchatātmā ||
children.translated_text: like the sun, flashing out, possessing a hundredfold self.

children.text: abhi dvijanmā trī rocanāni viśvā rajāṃsi śuśucāno asthāt
children.translated_text: The twice-born one has stood over the three luminous realms and all the regions, shining brightly.

children.text: hotā yajiṣṭho apāṃ sadhasthe ||
children.translated_text: He is the best-sacrificing <s>Hotṛ</s> in the common seat of the waters.

children.text: ayaṃ sa hotā yo dvijanmā viśvā dadhe vāryāṇi śravasyā
children.translated_text: This is that <s>Hotṛ</s>, the twice-born one, who has established all desirable, fame-winning goods.

children.text: marto yo asmai sutuko dadāśa ||
children.translated_text: The mortal who, well-disposed, has made offering to him is rewarded by him.

children.text: Chapter 150
puru tvā dāśvān voce 'rir agne tava svid ā
children.translated_text: Many times I will speak to you, O <s>Agni</s>, as a worshipper; surely I am yours.

children.text: todasyeva śaraṇa ā mahasya ||
children.translated_text: I come to the shelter of the great one, as to that of a goad.

children.text: vy aninasya dhaninaḥ prahoṣe cid araruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: At the loud call of the hostile, wealthy, ungiving man,

children.text: kadā cana prajigato adevayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: of the godless ones who have advanced, never at any time may we be theirs.

children.text: sa candro vipra martyo maho vrādhantamo divi
children.translated_text: May that inspired mortal be brilliant, waxing most greatly in heaven.

children.text: pra pret te agne vanuṣaḥ syāma ||
children.translated_text: Going forth before you, O <s>Agni</s>, may we overcome the hostile man.

children.text: Chapter 151
mitraṃ na yaṃ śimyā goṣu gavyavaḥ svādhyo vidathe apsu jījanan
children.translated_text: Him whom the cattle-seeking, thoughtful ones generated among the cows like <s>Mitra</s>, in the assembly, in the waters,

children.text: arejetāṃ rodasī pājasā girā prati priyaṃ yajataṃ januṣām avaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the two worlds trembled at his force; with song they received the beloved, worshipful help of peoples.

children.text: yaddha tyad vām purumīﾱhasya sominaḥ pra mitrāso na dadhire svābhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: When your friends, self-born as it were, accepted that Soma-offering of <s>Purumīḍha</s>,

children.text: adha kratuṃ vidataṃ gātum arcata uta śrutaṃ vṛṣaṇā pastyāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then you two bulls found insight and a path; sing, and hear also the one who has a dwelling.

children.text: ā vām bhūṣan kṣitayo janma rodasyoḥ pravācyaṃ vṛṣaṇā dakṣase mahe
children.translated_text: The peoples have adorned you two for the sake of the birth of heaven and earth, O bulls, a thing to be proclaimed for great skill.

children.text: yad īm ṛtāya bharatho yad arvate pra hotrayā śimyā vītho adhvaram ||
children.translated_text: When you carry it for <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), when for the steed, you two pass through the rite by priestly service and exertion.

children.text: pra sā kṣitir asura yā mahi priya ṛtāvānāv ṛtam ā ghoṣatho bṛhat
children.translated_text: Forward goes that mighty, dear dominion, O <s>Asura</s>; you two true to <s>ṛta</s> proclaim the great <s>ṛta</s>.

children.text: yuvaṃ divo bṛhato dakṣam ābhuvaṃ gāṃ na dhury upa yuñjāthe apaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You two harness the skill of broad heaven, the active power, and the waters to the yoke as one harnesses a cow.

children.text: mahī atra mahinā vāram ṛṇvatho 'reṇavas tuja ā sadman dhenavaḥ
children.translated_text: Here in greatness you set in motion the great chosen boon; the dustless cows press on to the dwelling.

children.text: svaranti tā uparatāti sūryam ā nimruca uṣasas takvavīr iva ||
children.translated_text: They sound forth after the withdrawn sun, like dawns moving swiftly at sunset.

children.text: ā vām ṛtāya keśinīr anūṣata mitra yatra varuṇa gātum arcathaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>ṛta</s>, the long-haired ones have sung to you two, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, where you sing the path.

children.text: ava tmanā sṛjatam pinvataṃ dhiyo yuvaṃ viprasya manmanām irajyathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By yourselves release and swell the thoughts; you two impel the inspired poet's acts of thought.

children.text: yo vāṃ yajñaiḥ śaśamāno ha dāśati kavir hotā yajati manmasādhanaḥ
children.translated_text: The poet, the <s>Hotṛ</s>, who praises you with sacrifices and worships, accomplishing the inspired thought,

children.text: upāha taṃ gacchatho vītho adhvaram acchā giraḥ sumatiṃ gantam asmayū ||
children.translated_text: you approach him, pass through the rite, and come toward our songs and kindly intention.

children.text: yuvāṃ yajñaiḥ prathamā gobhir añjata ṛtāvānā manaso na prayuktiṣu
children.translated_text: Men first anoint you two with sacrifices and cows, you two true to <s>ṛta</s>, as in the impulses of the mind.

children.text: bharanti vām manmanā saṃyatā giro 'dṛpyatā manasā revad āśāthe ||
children.translated_text: Their songs, yoked with thought, bring praise to you; with an unproud mind you two expect the rich offering.

children.text: revad vayo dadhāthe revad āśāthe narā māyābhir itaūti māhinam
children.translated_text: You two grant rich vitality, and you expect rich offering, O men, with wondrous powers, aiding this greatness.

children.text: na vāṃ dyāvo 'habhir nota sindhavo na devatvam paṇayo nānaśur magham ||
children.translated_text: Neither the heavens by day, nor the rivers, nor the <s>Paṇis</s> have attained your divinity or your bounty.

children.text: Chapter 152
yuvaṃ vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe yuvor acchidrā mantavo ha sargāḥ
children.translated_text: You two clothe yourselves in nourishing garments; your courses and ordinances are unbroken.

children.text: avātiratam anṛtāni viśva ṛtena mitrāvaruṇā sacethe ||
children.translated_text: You have driven away all falsehoods; with <s>ṛta</s>, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, you are joined.

children.text: etac cana tvo vi ciketad eṣāṃ satyo mantraḥ kaviśasta ṛghāvān
children.translated_text: Even this true mantra, praised by the sage and straight-going, has not been understood by these men.

children.text: triraśriṃ hanti caturaśrir ugro devanido ha prathamā ajūryan ||
children.translated_text: The fierce four-edged one strikes the three-cornered one; the god-revilers, though foremost, have not grown old.

children.text: apād eti prathamā padvatīnāṃ kas tad vām mitrāvaruṇā ciketa
children.translated_text: The footless one goes first among those with feet; who has perceived this of you two, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>?

children.text: garbho bhāram bharaty ā cid asya ṛtam piparty anṛtaṃ ni tārīt ||
children.translated_text: The embryo bears the burden even of this; <s>ṛta</s> carries it across, and falsehood has sunk down.

children.text: prayantam it pari jāraṃ kanīnām paśyāmasi nopanipadyamānam
children.translated_text: We see him going around the maidens as a lover, yet not lying down with them.

children.text: anavapṛgṇā vitatā vasānam priyam mitrasya varuṇasya dhāma ||
children.translated_text: Unseparated, spread out, he is clothed in the beloved abode of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: anaśvo jāto anabhīśur arvā kanikradat patayad ūrdhvasānuḥ
children.translated_text: Born horseless, without reins, yet a racer, neighing, flying, with his ridge lifted high,

children.text: acittam brahma jujuṣur yuvānaḥ pra mitre dhāma varuṇe gṛṇantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the young men have welcomed the uncomprehended sacred utterance, singing in the domain of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: ā dhenavo māmateyam avantīr brahmapriyam pīpayan sasminn ūdhan
children.translated_text: The milk-cows, helping <s>Māmateya</s>, have filled the lover of sacred speech at the same udder.

children.text: pitvo bhikṣeta vayunāni vidvān āsāvivāsann aditim uruṣyet ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the ways, he asks for a draught; drawing near with his mouth, he would protect spacious <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: ā vām mitrāvaruṇā havyajuṣṭiṃ namasā devāv avasā vavṛtyām
children.translated_text: With homage, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, I would turn your enjoyment of the oblation and your help toward us, O gods.

children.text: asmākam brahma pṛtanāsu sahyā asmākaṃ vṛṣṭir divyā supārā ||
children.translated_text: May our sacred utterance prevail in battles; may our heavenly rain be easy to cross.

children.text: Chapter 153
yajāmahe vām mahaḥ sajoṣā havyebhir mitrāvaruṇā namobhiḥ
children.translated_text: We worship you two, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, in greatness and shared goodwill, with oblations and reverences.

children.text: ghṛtair ghṛtasnū adha yad vām asme adhvaryavo na dhītibhir bharanti ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the <s>Adhvaryu</s> priests bring for you two, dripping with ghee, their inspired thoughts with ghee on our behalf.

children.text: prastutir vāṃ dhāma na prayuktir ayāmi mitrāvaruṇā suvṛktiḥ
children.translated_text: For you two the proclamation is your station, not a mere dispatch; I come, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, with well-turned praise.

children.text: anakti yad vāṃ vidatheṣu hotā sumnaṃ vāṃ sūrir vṛṣaṇāv iyakṣan ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) adorns you two in the assemblies, the generous patron seeks to win your favor, O strong ones.

children.text: pīpāya dhenur aditir ṛtāya janāya mitrāvaruṇā havirde
children.translated_text: The milch cow <s>Aditi</s> has swelled for <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), for the people, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, yielding oblation.

children.text: hinoti yad vāṃ vidathe saparyan sa rātahavyo mānuṣo na hotā ||
children.translated_text: When, serving you two in the assembly, he sends it forth, the human giver of oblations acts like a <s>Hotṛ</s>.

children.text: uta vāṃ vikṣu madyāsv andho gāva āpaś ca pīpayanta devīḥ
children.translated_text: And among the clans, in the exhilarating draughts, the cows and the divine waters have made you two swell.

children.text: uto no asya pūrvyaḥ patir dan vītam pātam payasa usriyāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And may the ancient lord of this give to us; come, drink the milk of the ruddy cow.

children.text: Chapter 154
viṣṇor nu kaṃ vīryāṇi pra vocaṃ yaḥ pārthivāni vimame rajāṃsi
children.translated_text: Now I will proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who measured out the earthly realms,

children.text: yo askabhāyad uttaraṃ sadhasthaṃ vicakramāṇas tredhorugāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who propped up the upper seat, striding in three steps, the far-going one.

children.text: pra tad viṣṇu stavate vīryeṇa mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: For this heroic power <s>Viṣṇu</s> is praised, like a fearsome wild beast, mountain-dwelling and roaming where he will,

children.text: yasyoruṣu triṣu vikramaṇeṣv adhikṣiyanti bhuvanāni viśvā ||
children.translated_text: in whose three wide strides all beings dwell.

children.text: pra viṣṇave śūṣam etu manma girikṣita urugāyāya vṛṣṇe
children.translated_text: Let my thought, a strong hymn, go forth to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to the mountain-dwelling, far-sung bull,

children.text: ya idaṃ dīrgham prayataṃ sadhastham eko vimame tribhir it padebhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: who alone measured out this long, far-extended seat with just three steps.

children.text: yasya trī pūrṇā madhunā padāny akṣīyamāṇā svadhayā madanti
children.translated_text: His three steps, full of sweetness, inexhaustible, rejoice by their own power,

children.text: ya u tridhātu pṛthivīm uta dyām eko dādhāra bhuvanāni viśvā ||
children.translated_text: he who alone upheld the threefold earth and also heaven, and all beings.

children.text: tad asya priyam abhi pātho aśyāṃ naro yatra devayavo madanti
children.translated_text: May I attain that dear path of his, where god-loving men rejoice,

children.text: urukramasya sa hi bandhur itthā viṣṇoḥ pade parame madhva utsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for there indeed is the kinship of the wide-strider; in the highest step of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is a spring of sweetness.

children.text: tā vāṃ vāstūny uśmasi gamadhyai yatra gāvo bhūriśṛṅgā ayāsaḥ
children.translated_text: We desire to go to those dwellings of yours, where the many-horned, untiring cows are,

children.text: atrāha tad urugāyasya vṛṣṇaḥ paramam padam ava bhāti bhūri ||
children.translated_text: for there that highest step of the far-sung bull shines forth broadly.

children.text: Chapter 155
pra vaḥ pāntam andhaso dhiyāyate mahe śūrāya viṣṇave cārcata
children.translated_text: Sing forth for the one who seeks the Soma draught; praise mighty heroic <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: yā sānuni parvatānām adābhyā mahas tasthatur arvateva sādhunā ||
children.translated_text: The two who, unassailable in greatness, stood upon the ridges of the mountains like racers on a good course.

children.text: tveṣam itthā samaraṇaṃ śimīvator indrāviṣṇū sutapā vām uruṣyati
children.translated_text: Fierce indeed is the conflict of the two mighty ones; O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the pressed Soma protects you widely.

children.text: yā martyāya pratidhīyamānam it kṛśānor astur asanām uruṣyathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You two protect the weapon's mouth of <s>Kṛśānu</s>, when it is set against a mortal.

children.text: tā īṃ vardhanti mahy asya pauṃsyaṃ ni mātarā nayati retase bhuje
children.translated_text: These powers increase his great manly force; he leads the two mothers down for the enjoyment of the seed.

children.text: dadhāti putro 'varam param pitur nāma tṛtīyam adhi rocane divaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The son sets the lower and the higher name of the father, and the third in the shining realm of heaven.

children.text: tat tad id asya pauṃsyaṃ gṛṇīmasīnasya trātur avṛkasya mīﾱhuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: That very manly power of his we sing, of the seated protector, harmless and bountiful.

children.text: yaḥ pārthivāni tribhir id vigāmabhir uru kramiṣṭorugāyāya jīvase ||
children.translated_text: He, with only three strides, traversed the earthly regions broadly, the far-striding, far-sung one, for life.

children.text: dve id asya kramaṇe svardṛśo 'bhikhyāya martyo bhuraṇyati
children.translated_text: Only two of his steps can a mortal perceive, looking toward heaven.

children.text: tṛtīyam asya nakir ā dadharṣati vayaś cana patayantaḥ patatriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His third no one dares approach, not even the winged birds in their flight.

children.text: caturbhiḥ sākaṃ navatiṃ ca nāmabhiś cakraṃ na vṛttaṃ vyatīṃr avīvipat
children.translated_text: With four times ninety names he set it in motion, like a rounded wheel.

children.text: bṛhaccharīro vimimāna ṛkvabhir yuvākumāraḥ praty ety āhavam ||
children.translated_text: Great-bodied, measuring himself out with hymns, young, a youth, he comes forward to the call.

children.text: Chapter 156
bhavā mitro na śevyo ghṛtāsutir vibhūtadyumna evayā u saprathāḥ
children.translated_text: Be gracious like <s>Mitra</s>, with ghee as your offering, with manifest brilliance, truly wide-spreading.

children.text: adhā te viṣṇo viduṣā cid ardhya stomo yajñaś ca rādhyo haviṣmatā ||
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, even by a knowing worshiper your praise and sacrifice are to be fulfilled with an oblation.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvyāya vedhase navīyase sumajjānaye viṣṇave dadāśati
children.translated_text: Whoever gives to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the ancient ordainer, ever new, of good birth,

children.text: yo jātam asya mahato mahi bravat sed u śravobhir yujyaṃ cid abhy asat ||
children.translated_text: who proclaims the great greatness of this mighty-born one, he indeed will gain even well-yoked fame.

children.text: tam u stotāraḥ pūrvyaṃ yathā vida ṛtasya garbhaṃ januṣā pipartana
children.translated_text: O singers, foster him as you know him, the ancient one, the embryo of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order) by birth.

children.text: āsya jānanto nāma cid vivaktana mahas te viṣṇo sumatim bhajāmahe ||
children.translated_text: Knowing even his name, proclaim it aloud; O great <s>Viṣṇu</s>, may we share in your favor.

children.text: tam asya rājā varuṇas tam aśvinā kratuṃ sacanta mārutasya vedhasaḥ
children.translated_text: King <s>Varuṇa</s> and the <s>Aśvins</s> accompanied that resolve of his, the inspiration of the <s>Marut</s>-ordainer.

children.text: dādhāra dakṣam uttamam aharvidaṃ vrajaṃ ca viṣṇuḥ sakhivāṁ aporṇute ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> upheld the highest skill, knowing the day, and, rich in allies, opened the cattle-pen.

children.text: ā yo vivāya sacathāya daivya indrāya viṣṇuḥ sukṛte sukṛttaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, better in good action, came to divine fellowship for <s>Indra</s>, for the well-done deed.

children.text: vedhā ajinvat triṣadhastha āryam ṛtasya bhāge yajamānam ābhajat ||
children.translated_text: The ordainer, abiding in the three stations, quickened the noble one and assigned the sacrificer to a share of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order).

children.text: Chapter 157
abodhy agnir jma ud eti sūryo vy uṣāś candrā mahy āvo arciṣā
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> has awakened; <s>Sūrya</s> rises from the earth; the bright dawns have shone out with great radiance.

children.text: āyukṣātām aśvinā yātave ratham prāsāvīd devaḥ savitā jagat pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aśvins</s> have yoked their chariot for the journey; god <s>Savitṛ</s> has set the whole moving world in motion, each part apart.

children.text: yad yuñjāthe vṛṣaṇam aśvinā rathaṃ ghṛtena no madhunā kṣatram ukṣatam
children.translated_text: When you two yoke the strong chariot, O <s>Aśvins</s>, sprinkle our dominion with ghee and honey.

children.text: asmākam brahma pṛtanāsu jinvataṃ vayaṃ dhanā śūrasātā bhajemahi ||
children.translated_text: Quicken our sacred formulation in battles; may we share in the riches won by heroes.

children.text: arvāṅ tricakro madhuvāhano ratho jīrāśvo aśvinor yātu suṣṭutaḥ
children.translated_text: Let the three-wheeled, honey-bearing chariot of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with swift horses and well praised, come hither,

children.text: trivandhuro maghavā viśvasaubhagaḥ śaṃ na ā vakṣad dvipade catuṣpade ||
children.translated_text: three-seated, bounteous, endowed with every blessing; may it bring welfare to our two-footed and four-footed beings.

children.text: ā na ūrjaṃ vahatam aśvinā yuvam madhumatyā naḥ kaśayā mimikṣatam
children.translated_text: Bring nourishment to us, you two <s>Aśvins</s>; mix us with your honeyed whip.

children.text: prāyus tāriṣṭaṃ nī rapāṃsi mṛkṣataṃ sedhataṃ dveṣo bhavataṃ sacābhuvā ||
children.translated_text: Carry us beyond to full length of life; wipe away calamities; drive off hatred; become our companions.

children.text: yuvaṃ ha garbhaṃ jagatīṣu dhattho yuvaṃ viśveṣu bhuvaneṣv antaḥ
children.translated_text: You two place the embryo among moving creatures; you two are within all the worlds.

children.text: yuvam agniṃ ca vṛṣaṇāv apaś ca vanaspatīṃr aśvināv airayethām ||
children.translated_text: You two, O strong <s>Aśvins</s>, stir <s>Agni</s>, the waters, and the forest trees.

children.text: yuvaṃ ha stho bhiṣajā bheṣajebhir atho ha stho rathyā rāthyebhiḥ
children.translated_text: You two are physicians with remedies; and you are charioteers with chariot-teams.

children.text: atho ha kṣatram adhi dhattha ugrā yo vāṃ haviṣmān manasā dadāśa ||
children.translated_text: And you two, fierce ones, establish lordly power for the oblation-bearing man who has devoted himself to you with his mind.

children.text: Chapter 158
vasū rudrā purumantū vṛdhantā daśasyataṃ no vṛṣaṇāv abhiṣṭau
children.translated_text: O wealthy <s>Rudras</s>, rich in counsel and growing strong, grant us favor, O vigorous ones, with your aid.

children.text: dasrā ha yad rekṇa aucathyo vām pra yat sasrāthe akavābhir ūtī ||
children.translated_text: O wondrous two, when <s>Aucathya</s> sought your treasure, when you set forth with tireless aids,

children.text: ko vāṃ dāśat sumataye cid asyai vasū yad dhethe namasā pade goḥ
children.translated_text: who would make an offering to you for this favor, when, O wealthy ones, you place treasures with reverence at the cow's station?

children.text: jigṛtam asme revatīḥ purandhīḥ kāmapreṇeva manasā carantā ||
children.translated_text: Seize for us rich and bountiful gifts, moving with your mind as if filled with desire.

children.text: yukto ha yad vāṃ taugryāya perur vi madhye arṇaso dhāyi pajraḥ
children.translated_text: When your yoked vessel was set for <s>Taugrya</s> in the middle of the flood,

children.text: upa vām avaḥ śaraṇaṃ gameyaṃ śūro nājma patayadbhir evaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: may I come to your help and shelter, like a hero to the race with flying steeds.

children.text: upastutir aucathyam uruṣyen mā mām ime patatriṇī vi dugdhām
children.translated_text: May this praise protect <s>Aucathya</s>; let these two winged ones not milk me dry.

children.text: mā mām edho daśatayaś cito dhāk pra yad vām baddhas tmani khādati kṣām ||
children.translated_text: Let not the firewood, kindled in tens, consume me, when, bound in himself, it bites the earth for you.

children.text: na mā garan nadyo mātṛtamā dāsā yad īṃ susamubdham avādhuḥ
children.translated_text: The most motherly rivers did not swallow me, when the servants cast him down, well bound.

children.text: śiro yad asya traitano vitakṣat svayaṃ dāsa uro aṃsāv api gdha ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Traitana</s> cut off his head, the <s>Dāsa</s> himself struck at breast and shoulders.

children.text: dīrghatamā māmateyo jujurvān daśame yuge
children.translated_text: <s>Dīrghatamas</s>, son of <s>Mamatā</s>, grown old in the tenth age,

children.text: apām arthaṃ yatīnām brahmā bhavati sārathiḥ ||
children.translated_text: became the guiding priest, the charioteer, for those going in quest of the waters.

children.text: Chapter 159
pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī ṛtāvṛdhā mahī stuṣe vidatheṣu pracetasā
children.translated_text: With sacrifices I praise Heaven and Earth, great increasers of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), wise ones in the assemblies.

children.text: devebhir ye devaputre sudaṃsasetthā dhiyā vāryāṇi prabhūṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: They, divine children among the gods, of good deeds, thus by inspired thought adorn desirable things.

children.text: uta manye pitur adruho mano mātur mahi svatavas taddhavīmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: And I contemplate the harmless mind of the father and the great power of the mother, with invocations.

children.text: suretasā pitarā bhūma cakratur uru prajāyā amṛtaṃ varīmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The two parents, rich in seed, made the earth wide for offspring, an immortal breadth with wide spaces.

children.text: te sūnavaḥ svapasaḥ sudaṃsaso mahī jajñur mātarā pūrvacittaye
children.translated_text: Those sons, skillful and of good deeds, were born from the two great mothers for primal understanding.

children.text: sthātuś ca satyaṃ jagataś ca dharmaṇi putrasya pāthaḥ padam advayāvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the law of what stands and what moves, they guard the true path of the guileless son.

children.text: te māyino mamire supracetaso jāmī sayonī mithunā samokasā
children.translated_text: Those artful, very wise ones measured out the kindred pair, born of one womb and dwelling in one home.

children.text: navyaṃ navyaṃ tantum ā tanvate divi samudre antaḥ kavayaḥ sudītayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise, bright-shining ones stretch out an ever-new thread in heaven and within the sea.

children.text: tad rādho adya savitur vareṇyaṃ vayaṃ devasya prasave manāmahe
children.translated_text: Today we would think upon that desirable gift of <s>Savitṛ</s>, at the impulse of the god.

children.text: asmabhyaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī sucetunā rayiṃ dhattaṃ vasumantaṃ śatagvinam ||
children.translated_text: O Heaven and Earth, with good understanding bestow on us wealth rich in goods, possessing a hundred cows.

children.text: Chapter 160
te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuva ṛtāvarī rajaso dhārayatkavī
children.translated_text: For Heaven and Earth are beneficent to all, bearers of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), wise sustainers of the region.

children.text: sujanmanī dhiṣaṇe antar īyate devo devī dharmaṇā sūryaḥ śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: Between the two well-born wise ones the pure god <s>Sūrya</s> moves by <s>dharma</s> (cosmic law).

children.text: uruvyacasā mahinī asaścatā pitā mātā ca bhuvanāni rakṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Broad in reach, mighty, and inexhaustible, father and mother protect the worlds.

children.text: sudhṛṣṭame vapuṣye na rodasī pitā yat sīm abhi rūpair avāsayat ||
children.translated_text: The two worlds are most firm and fair to behold, when the father clothes him with forms.

children.text: sa vahniḥ putraḥ pitroḥ pavitravān punāti dhīro bhuvanāni māyayā
children.translated_text: That bearer, the son of the two parents, possessing a purifier, the wise one purifies the worlds by his wondrous power.

children.text: dhenuṃ ca pṛśniṃ vṛṣabhaṃ suretasaṃ viśvāhā śukram payo asya dukṣata ||
children.translated_text: Every day they milk his bright milk: the speckled cow and the bull rich in seed.

children.text: ayaṃ devānām apasām apastamo yo jajāna rodasī viśvaśambhuvā
children.translated_text: This one is the most active of the active gods, who generated the two world-halves, beneficent to all.

children.text: vi yo mame rajasī sukratūyayājarebhi skambhanebhiḥ sam ānṛce ||
children.translated_text: He who measured out the two regions with good purpose is hymned together with unaging supports.

children.text: te no gṛṇāne mahinī mahi śravaḥ kṣatraṃ dyāvāpṛthivī dhāsatho bṛhat
children.translated_text: O great Heaven and Earth, when praised, may you bestow on us great fame and broad dominion.

children.text: yenābhi kṛṣṭīs tatanāma viśvahā panāyyam ojo asme sam invatam ||
children.translated_text: By it may we extend ourselves among the peoples every day; set praiseworthy strength within us.

children.text: Chapter 161
kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ yaviṣṭho na ājagan kim īyate dūtyaṃ kad yad ūcima
children.translated_text: Who, then, has come to us as the best, who as the youngest? What embassy is moving, and when shall we speak?

children.text: na nindima camasaṃ yo mahākulo 'gne bhrātar druṇa id bhūtim ūdima ||
children.translated_text: We do not blame the cup, which is of great lineage; O brother <s>Agni</s>, we have spoken of its worth in the wooden vessel.

children.text: ekaṃ camasaṃ caturaḥ kṛṇotana tad vo devā abruvan tad va āgamam
children.translated_text: Make the one cup into four: that the gods said to you, and that message came to you.

children.text: saudhanvanā yady evā kariṣyatha sākaṃ devair yajñiyāso bhaviṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Saudhanvanas</s>, if you do this, you will become worthy of sacrifice together with the gods.

children.text: agniṃ dūtam prati yad abravītanāśvaḥ kartvo ratha uteha kartvaḥ
children.translated_text: When you answered <s>Agni</s> the messenger: 'A horse must be made, and here a chariot must be made;

children.text: dhenuḥ kartvā yuvaśā kartvā dvā tāni bhrātar anu vaḥ kṛtvy emasi ||
children.translated_text: a cow must be made, and youth must be made; those two tasks, brothers, we shall perform after you.'

children.text: cakṛvāṃsa ṛbhavas tad apṛcchata kved abhūd yaḥ sya dūto na ājagan
children.translated_text: Having made it, O <s>Ṛbhus</s>, you asked: 'Where has he gone, the messenger who came to us?'

children.text: yadāvākhyac camasāñcaturaḥ kṛtān ād it tvaṣṭā gnāsv antar ny ānaje ||
children.translated_text: When he announced that the cups had been made four, then <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> hid himself among the women.

children.text: hanāmaināṃ iti tvaṣṭā yad abravīc camasaṃ ye devapānam anindiṣuḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> said, 'Let us slay these men, who have disparaged the cup, the gods' drinking vessel,'

children.text: anyā nāmāni kṛṇvate sute sacāṁ anyair enān kanyā nāmabhi sparat ||
children.translated_text: they took other names at the pressing; with other names the maiden touched them.

children.text: indro harī yuyuje aśvinā ratham bṛhaspatir viśvarūpām upājata
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> yoked his two bay horses; the <s>Aśvins</s> yoked their chariot; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> approached <s>Viśvarūpā</s>.

children.text: ṛbhur vibhvā vājo devāṁ agacchata svapaso yajñiyam bhāgam aitana ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Vibhvan</s>, and <s>Vāja</s> went to the gods; skillful ones, you came to the sacrificial share.

children.text: niś carmaṇo gām ariṇīta dhītibhir yā jarantā yuvaśā tākṛṇotana
children.translated_text: By your insights you released the cow from the hide; the one that was aging you made young.

children.text: saudhanvanā aśvād aśvam atakṣata yuktvā ratham upa devāṁ ayātana ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Saudhanvanas</s>, from a horse you fashioned a horse; having yoked the chariot, you went to the gods.

children.text: idam udakam pibatety abravītanedaṃ vā ghā pibatā muñjanejanam
children.translated_text: 'Drink this water,' they said, 'or rather drink this rinsing of muñja grass.'

children.text: saudhanvanā yadi tan neva haryatha tṛtīye ghā savane mādayādhvai ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Saudhanvanas</s>, if that does not please you, then rejoice at the third pressing.

children.text: āpo bhūyiṣṭhā ity eko abravīd agnir bhūyiṣṭha ity anyo abravīt
children.translated_text: 'The waters are greatest,' one said; 'Agni is greatest,' another said.

children.text: vadharyantīm bahubhyaḥ praiko abravīd ṛtā vadantaś camasāṁ apiṃśata ||
children.translated_text: One proclaimed the yielding one to many; speaking truths, they shaped the cup.

children.text: śroṇām eka udakaṃ gām avājati māṃsam ekaḥ piṃśati sūnayābhṛtam
children.translated_text: One drove the lame cow to the water; one cut the flesh brought with the slaughtering knife.

children.text: ā nimrucaḥ śakṛd eko apābharat kiṃ svit putrebhyaḥ pitarā upāvatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: One carried away the dung until sunset; how, then, did the two parents serve their sons?

children.text: udvatsv asmā akṛṇotanā tṛṇaṃ nivatsv apaḥ svapasyayā naraḥ
children.translated_text: In the uplands you made grass for him, and in the lowlands waters, O men, by your skill.

children.text: agohyasya yad asastanā gṛhe tad adyedam ṛbhavo nānu gacchatha ||
children.translated_text: What was in the house of the hidden one, O <s>Ṛbhus</s>, do you not follow that today?

children.text: saṃmīlya yad bhuvanā paryasarpata kva svit tātyā pitarā va āsatuḥ
children.translated_text: When, closing together, you crept around the worlds, where then were those two parents of yours?

children.text: aśapata yaḥ karasnaṃ va ādade yaḥ prābravīt pro tasmā abravītana ||
children.translated_text: He who seized your arm cursed; he who spoke beforehand, to him you spoke in reply.

children.text: suṣupvāṃsa ṛbhavas tad apṛcchatāgohya ka idaṃ no abūbudhat
children.translated_text: Having slept, the <s>Ṛbhus</s> asked this: "O hidden one, who has awakened us here?"

children.text: śvānam basto bodhayitāram abravīt saṃvatsara idam adyā vy akhyata ||
children.translated_text: The goat said, "The dog was the awakener; this very year has now been disclosed today."

children.text: divā yānti maruto bhūmyāgnir ayaṃ vāto antarikṣeṇa yāti
children.translated_text: By day the <s>Maruts</s> go; <s>Agni</s> goes by the earth; this <s>Vāta</s> goes through the midspace.

children.text: adbhir yāti varuṇaḥ samudrair yuṣmāṁ icchantaḥ śavaso napātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s> goes with the waters, with the oceans, seeking you, O sons of power.

children.text: Chapter 162
mā no mitro varuṇo aryamāyur indra ṛbhukṣā marutaḥ pari khyan
children.translated_text: May <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Āyu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Ṛbhukṣan</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> not look askance at us,

children.text: yad vājino devajātasya sapteḥ pravakṣyāmo vidathe vīryāṇi ||
children.translated_text: when in the assembly we shall proclaim the heroic deeds of the prize-winning steed, the god-born courser.

children.text: yan nirṇijā rekṇasā prāvṛtasya rātiṃ gṛbhītām mukhato nayanti
children.translated_text: When they lead forward from the mouth the accepted gift of the one wrapped in a splendid covering,

children.text: suprāṅ ajo memyad viśvarūpa indrāpūṣṇoḥ priyam apy eti pāthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the goat, facing forward, bleating, many-formed, goes along the dear path of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>.

children.text: eṣa cchāgaḥ puro aśvena vājinā pūṣṇo bhāgo nīyate viśvadevyaḥ
children.translated_text: This goat, ahead of the swift horse, is led as <s>Pūṣan</s>'s share, belonging to all the gods.

children.text: abhipriyaṃ yat puroﾱāśam arvatā tvaṣṭed enaṃ sauśravasāya jinvati ||
children.translated_text: When the beloved sacrificial cake goes before with the courser, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> quickens him for fair renown.

children.text: yaddhaviṣyam ṛtuśo devayānaṃ trir mānuṣāḥ pary aśvaṃ nayanti
children.translated_text: When, season by season, men lead the horse around three times as the oblation that goes to the gods,

children.text: atrā pūṣṇaḥ prathamo bhāga eti yajñaṃ devebhyaḥ prativedayann ajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the goat comes first as <s>Pūṣan</s>'s share, announcing the sacrifice to the gods.

children.text: hotādhvaryur āvayā agnimindho grāvagrābha uta śaṃstā suvipraḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s>, the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, the attendant, the kindler of <s>Agni</s>, the holder of the pressing-stones, and the well-inspired reciter,

children.text: tena yajñena svaraṃkṛtena sviṣṭena vakṣaṇā ā pṛṇadhvam ||
children.translated_text: with that sacrifice, well adorned and well performed, fill the spaces with the offering.

children.text: yūpavraskā uta ye yūpavāhāś caṣālaṃ ye aśvayūpāya takṣati
children.translated_text: Those who cut the sacrificial post, and those who carry the post, and those who fashion the top-piece for the horse's post,

children.text: ye cārvate pacanaṃ saṃbharanty uto teṣām abhigūrtir na invatu ||
children.translated_text: and those who gather the cooking equipment for the courser, may the effort of those men aid us.

children.text: upa prāgāt suman me 'dhāyi manma devānām āśā upa vītapṛṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: The favorable thought has come near; my hymn has been set down; the expectations of the gods have come near to the broad-backed one.

children.text: anv enaṃ viprā ṛṣayo madanti devānām puṣṭe cakṛmā subandhum ||
children.translated_text: Following him, the inspired seers rejoice; in the nourishment of the gods we have made him a good kinsman.

children.text: yad vājino dāma saṃdānam arvato yā śīrṣaṇyā raśanā rajjur asya
children.translated_text: Whatever tether of the prize-winning horse there is, whatever halter of the courser, whatever head-rope or rein is his,

children.text: yad vā ghāsya prabhṛtam āsye tṛṇaṃ sarvā tā te api deveṣv astu ||
children.translated_text: or whatever grass has been placed in his mouth as fodder, may all those things of yours be also among the gods.

children.text: yad aśvasya kraviṣo makṣikāśa yad vā svarau svadhitau riptam asti
children.translated_text: Whatever of the horse's raw flesh the flies eat, or whatever is stuck to the spit or to the axe,

children.text: yaddhastayoḥ śamitur yan nakheṣu sarvā tā te api deveṣv astu ||
children.translated_text: whatever is on the slaughterer's hands or in his nails, may all those things of yours be also among the gods.

children.text: yad ūvadhyam udarasyāpavāti ya āmasya kraviṣo gandho asti
children.translated_text: Whatever flows out from the belly and its contents, whatever smell there is of the raw flesh,

children.text: sukṛtā tacchamitāraḥ kṛṇvantūta medhaṃ śṛtapākam pacantu ||
children.translated_text: let the preparers make that well prepared, and let them cook the sacrificial portion until it is fully done.

children.text: yat te gātrād agninā pacyamānād abhi śūlaṃ nihatasyāvadhāvati
children.translated_text: Whatever runs off from your limb as it is cooked by fire, impaled and fixed upon the spit,

children.text: mā tad bhūmyām ā śriṣan mā tṛṇeṣu devebhyas tad uśadbhyo rātam astu ||
children.translated_text: let that not fall upon the earth or among the grasses; let it be given to the gods who long for it.

children.text: ye vājinam paripaśyanti pakvaṃ ya īm āhuḥ surabhir nir hareti
children.translated_text: Those who watch the cooked prize-winning horse, and those who say of it, "It is fragrant; take it out,"

children.text: ye cārvato māṃsabhikṣām upāsata uto teṣām abhigūrtir na invatu ||
children.translated_text: and those who wait upon the courser for a share of meat, may the approval of those men aid us.

children.text: yan nīkṣaṇam māṃspacanyā ukhāyā yā pātrāṇi yūṣṇa āsecanāni
children.translated_text: The inspection of the flesh-cooking pot, the vessels, and the pourings of broth,

children.text: ūṣmaṇyāpidhānā carūṇām aṅkāḥ sūnāḥ pari bhūṣanty aśvam ||
children.translated_text: the heat, the covers of the cauldrons, the hooks, the skewers, and the spits adorn the horse all around.

children.text: nikramaṇaṃ niṣadanaṃ vivartanaṃ yac ca paḍbīśam arvataḥ
children.translated_text: The stepping out, the sitting down, the turning around, and whatever foot-fetter belongs to the courser,

children.text: yac ca papau yac ca ghāsiṃ jaghāsa sarvā tā te api deveṣv astu ||
children.translated_text: and what he drank and what fodder he ate, may all those things of yours be also among the gods.

children.text: mā tvāgnir dhvanayīd dhūmagandhir mokhā bhrājanty abhi vikta jaghriḥ
children.translated_text: May smoky-smelling <s>Agni</s> not make you crackle; may the shining pot not split apart as it smells you.

children.text: iṣṭaṃ vītam abhigūrtaṃ vaṣaṭkṛtaṃ taṃ devāsaḥ prati gṛbhṇanty aśvam ||
children.translated_text: The horse, sacrificed, consumed, approved, and marked with the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call, the gods receive.

children.text: yad aśvāya vāsa upastṛṇanty adhīvāsaṃ yā hiraṇyāny asmai
children.translated_text: The cloth that they spread beneath the horse, the upper covering, and the golden ornaments placed for him,

children.text: saṃdānam arvantam paḍbīśam priyā deveṣv ā yāmayanti ||
children.translated_text: the tether, the courser, and the foot-fetter: these dear things they send onward among the gods.

children.text: yat te sāde mahasā śūkṛtasya pārṣṇyā vā kaśayā vā tutoda
children.translated_text: Whatever has struck you in your seat, by the force of the well-made equipment, whether by heel or by whip,

children.text: sruceva tā haviṣo adhvareṣu sarvā tā te brahmaṇā sūdayāmi ||
children.translated_text: all that of yours, like an oblation with a ladle in the rites, I set right with sacred utterance.

children.text: catustriṃśad vājino devabandhor vaṅkrīr aśvasya svadhitiḥ sam eti
children.translated_text: The axe comes upon the thirty-four ribs of the prize-winning horse, the kinsman of the gods.

children.text: acchidrā gātrā vayunā kṛṇota paruṣparur anughuṣyā vi śasta ||
children.translated_text: Make the limbs uninjured with skill; joint by joint, call them out and cut them apart.

children.text: ekas tvaṣṭur aśvasyā viśastā dvā yantārā bhavatas tatha ṛtuḥ
children.translated_text: One is the cutter of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s horse; two are the restrainers, and so too is the proper season.

children.text: yā te gātrāṇām ṛtuthā kṛṇomi tā tā piṇḍānām pra juhomy agnau ||
children.translated_text: Those limbs of yours which I arrange according to season, those pieces I offer forth into <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: mā tvā tapat priya ātmāpiyantam mā svadhitis tanva ā tiṣṭhipat te
children.translated_text: May your dear self not burn you as you go forth; may the axe not remain fixed upon your body.

children.text: mā te gṛdhnur aviśastātihāya chidrā gātrāṇy asinā mithū kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May no greedy man, passing beyond an uncut part, make your limbs torn apart from one another with the knife.

children.text: na vā u etan mriyase na riṣyasi devāṁ id eṣi pathibhiḥ sugebhiḥ
children.translated_text: No indeed, you do not die, nor are you harmed; you go to the gods by easy paths.

children.text: harī te yuñjā pṛṣatī abhūtām upāsthād vājī dhuri rāsabhasya ||
children.translated_text: Your two bay, dappled mares have been yoked; the racer has taken his place at the shaft of the donkey.

children.text: sugavyaṃ no vājī svaśvyam puṃsaḥ putrāṁ uta viśvāpuṣaṃ rayim
children.translated_text: May the prize-winning horse win for us wealth rich in cattle, rich in horses, with men, with sons, and nourishing all.

children.text: anāgāstvaṃ no aditiḥ kṛṇotu kṣatraṃ no aśvo vanatāṃ haviṣmān ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Aditi</s> make us free from guilt; may the oblation-bearing horse win lordly power for us.

children.text: Chapter 163
yad akrandaḥ prathamaṃ jāyamāna udyan samudrād uta vā purīṣāt
children.translated_text: When you first neighed as you were born, rising from the ocean or from the moisture,

children.text: śyenasya pakṣā hariṇasya bāhū upastutyam mahi jātaṃ te arvan ||
children.translated_text: your great birth, O courser, worthy of praise, had the wings of a falcon and the forelegs of a deer.

children.text: yamena dattaṃ trita enam āyunag indra eṇam prathamo adhy atiṣṭhat
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> gave him; <s>Trita</s> harnessed him; <s>Indra</s> was the first to mount him.

children.text: gandharvo asya raśanām agṛbhṇāt sūrād aśvaṃ vasavo nir ataṣṭa ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Gandharva</s> grasped his rein; the <s>Vasus</s> fashioned the horse from the sun.

children.text: asi yamo asy ādityo arvann asi trito guhyena vratena
children.translated_text: You are <s>Yama</s>; you are <s>Āditya</s>, O courser; you are <s>Trita</s> by a hidden vow.

children.text: asi somena samayā vipṛkta āhus te trīṇi divi bandhanāni ||
children.translated_text: You are closely joined with <s>Soma</s>; they say that your three bonds are in heaven.

children.text: trīṇi ta āhur divi bandhanāni trīṇy apsu trīṇy antaḥ samudre
children.translated_text: They say your three bonds are in heaven, three in the waters, and three within the ocean.

children.text: uteva me varuṇaś chantsy arvan yatrā ta āhuḥ paramaṃ janitram ||
children.translated_text: And, O courser, you seem to me like <s>Varuṇa</s>, there where they say your highest birthplace is.

children.text: imā te vājinn avamārjanānīmā śaphānāṃ sanitur nidhānā
children.translated_text: These are your cleansings, O racer; these are the resting-places of the hooves of the winner.

children.text: atrā te bhadrā raśanā apaśyam ṛtasya yā abhirakṣanti gopāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here I saw your auspicious reins, which, as guardians, protect <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order).

children.text: ātmānaṃ te manasārād ajānām avo divā patayantam pataṅgam
children.translated_text: With my mind I recognized your self from afar, the winged one flying downward from heaven by day.

children.text: śiro apaśyam pathibhiḥ sugebhir areṇubhir jehamānam patatri ||
children.translated_text: I saw your head moving on easy, dustless paths, O bird-like one.

children.text: atrā te rūpam uttamam apaśyaṃ jigīṣamāṇam iṣa ā pade goḥ
children.translated_text: Here I saw your highest form, striving for nourishment at the cow's footprint.

children.text: yadā te marto anu bhogam ānaﾱ ād id grasiṣṭha oṣadhīr ajīgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When a mortal came to your enjoyment, then, most eager to devour, you rose up toward the plants.

children.text: anu tvā ratho anu maryo arvann anu gāvo 'nu bhagaḥ kanīnām
children.translated_text: The chariot follows you; the young man follows you, O steed; the cows follow, and the share of maidens follows.

children.text: anu vrātāsas tava sakhyam īyur anu devā mamire vīryaṃ te ||
children.translated_text: Your bands followed your friendship; the gods measured out your heroic power.

children.text: hiraṇyaśṛṅgo 'yo asya pādā manojavā avara indra āsīt
children.translated_text: He has golden horns and iron feet; <s>Indra</s> was beneath him, swift as thought.

children.text: devā id asya haviradyam āyan yo arvantam prathamo adhyatiṣṭhat ||
children.translated_text: The gods came to his portion fit for oblation, he who was the first to mount the racehorse.

children.text: īrmāntāsaḥ silikamadhyamāsaḥ saṃ śūraṇāso divyāso atyāḥ
children.translated_text: The heavenly chargers, with slender haunches and firm middles, together bounding like heroes,

children.text: haṃsā iva śreṇiśo yatante yad ākṣiṣur divyam ajmam aśvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: go in rows like geese, when the horses have reached the heavenly course.

children.text: tava śarīram patayiṣṇv arvan tava cittaṃ vāta iva dhrajīmān
children.translated_text: Your body, O steed, is fit to fly; your mind is rushing like the wind.

children.text: tava śṛṅgāṇi viṣṭhitā purutrāraṇyeṣu jarbhurāṇā caranti ||
children.translated_text: Your horns, spread far and wide, wander, snorting, through the forests.

children.text: upa prāgācchasanaṃ vājy arvā devadrīcā manasā dīdhyānaḥ
children.translated_text: The racer, the horse, has come near the place of slaughter, thinking with a mind turned toward the gods.

children.text: ajaḥ puro nīyate nābhir asyānu paścāt kavayo yanti rebhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The goat is led before him as his navel; after him go the poets, crying aloud.

children.text: upa prāgāt paramaṃ yat sadhastham arvāṁ acchā pitaram mātaraṃ ca
children.translated_text: The horse has gone near the highest assembly-place, toward father and mother.

children.text: adyā devāñ juṣṭatamo hi gamyā athā śāste dāśuṣe vāryāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Today he should go, most beloved by the gods; then he grants desirable goods to the worshiper.

children.text: Chapter 164
asya vāmasya palitasya hotus tasya bhrātā madhyamo asty aśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Of this lovely, gray-haired <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), there is a middle brother who is ravenous.

children.text: tṛtīyo bhrātā ghṛtapṛṣṭho asyātrāpaśyaṃ viśpatiṃ saptaputram ||
children.translated_text: A third brother, ghee-backed, is his; there I saw the lord of the people with seven sons.

children.text: sapta yuñjanti ratham ekacakram eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā
children.translated_text: Seven yoke the one-wheeled chariot; one horse, bearing seven names, draws it.

children.text: trinābhi cakram ajaram anarvaṃ yatremā viśvā bhuvanādhi tasthuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wheel has three naves, unaging and unobstructed; upon it all these worlds are set.

children.text: imaṃ ratham adhi ye sapta tasthuḥ saptacakraṃ sapta vahanty aśvāḥ
children.translated_text: Those seven who stand upon this chariot: seven horses draw the seven-wheeled one.

children.text: sapta svasāro abhi saṃ navante yatra gavāṃ nihitā sapta nāma ||
children.translated_text: Seven sisters sing together around it, where the seven names of the cows are placed.

children.text: ko dadarśa prathamaṃ jāyamānam asthanvantaṃ yad anasthā bibharti
children.translated_text: Who saw the first-born as he was being born, when the boneless one bore the one with bones?

children.text: bhūmyā asur asṛg ātmā kva svit ko vidvāṃsam upa gāt praṣṭum etat ||
children.translated_text: Where was the breath, the blood, the self of the earth? Who went to the wise one to ask this?

children.text: pākaḥ pṛcchāmi manasāvijānan devānām enā nihitā padāni
children.translated_text: Immature, not knowing in mind, I ask about these hidden tracks of the gods.

children.text: vatse baṣkaye 'dhi sapta tantūn vi tatnire kavaya otavā u ||
children.translated_text: Upon the young calf the poets stretched out the seven threads and wove them.

children.text: acikitvāñcikituṣaś cid atra kavīn pṛcchāmi vidmane na vidvān
children.translated_text: Unknowing, for the sake of knowledge I ask the knowing seers here; I am not a knower.

children.text: vi yas tastambha ṣaﾱ imā rajāṃsy ajasya rūpe kim api svid ekam ||
children.translated_text: What was that one thing, in the form of the unborn, by which he propped apart these six realms?

children.text: iha bravītu ya īm aṅga vedāsya vāmasya nihitam padaṃ veḥ
children.translated_text: Let him who truly knows proclaim here the hidden station of this lovely bird.

children.text: śīrṣṇaḥ kṣīraṃ duhrate gāvo asya vavriṃ vasānā udakam padāpuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The cows milk the milk from his head; wearing their covering, they have drunk water with their foot.

children.text: mātā pitaram ṛta ā babhāja dhīty agre manasā saṃ hi jagme
children.translated_text: The mother gave the father his share in accordance with <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order); at first she came together with him in thought and mind.

children.text: sā bībhatsur garbharasā nividdhā namasvanta id upavākam īyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: She, repulsive and pierced by the essence of the embryo, and the reverent ones went to the appeal.

children.text: yuktā mātāsīd dhuri dakṣiṇāyā atiṣṭhad garbho vṛjanīṣv antaḥ
children.translated_text: The mother was yoked to the right-hand pole; the embryo stood within the enclosures.

children.text: amīmed vatso anu gām apaśyad viśvarūpyaṃ triṣu yojaneṣu ||
children.translated_text: The calf bellowed; following the cow, he saw the many-formed one in the three yojanas.

children.text: tisro mātṝs trīn pitṝn bibhrad eka ūrdhvas tasthau nem ava glāpayanti
children.translated_text: Bearing three mothers and three fathers, the one stood upright; they do not weary him below.

children.text: mantrayante divo amuṣya pṛṣṭhe viśvavidaṃ vācam aviśvaminvām ||
children.translated_text: On the back of that heaven they counsel together about speech, all-knowing yet not setting all in motion.

children.text: dvādaśāraṃ nahi taj jarāya varvarti cakram pari dyām ṛtasya
children.translated_text: The twelve-spoked wheel of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order) turns around heaven; indeed it does not grow old.

children.text: ā putrā agne mithunāso atra sapta śatāni viṃśatiś ca tasthuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Upon it, O <s>Agni</s>, seven hundred and twenty sons, in pairs, stand.

children.text: pañcapādam pitaraṃ dvādaśākṛtiṃ diva āhuḥ pare ardhe purīṣiṇam
children.translated_text: They call the father five-footed, of twelve forms, rich in moisture, in the farther half of heaven.

children.text: atheme anya upare vicakṣaṇaṃ saptacakre ṣaﾱara āhur arpitam ||
children.translated_text: But others call him the far-seeing one, set lower down in the seven-wheeled, six-spoked chariot.

children.text: pañcāre cakre parivartamāne tasminn ā tasthur bhuvanāni viśvā
children.translated_text: On the five-spoked wheel as it turns, all beings have taken their place.

children.text: tasya nākṣas tapyate bhūribhāraḥ sanād eva na śīryate sanābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its axle, though heavily burdened, is not heated; from of old, with its nave, it does not break.

children.text: sanemi cakram ajaraṃ vi vāvṛta uttānāyāṃ daśa yuktā vahanti
children.translated_text: The wheel with its felly, unaging, has rolled out; ten yoked ones draw it on the upturned one.

children.text: sūryasya cakṣū rajasaity āvṛtaṃ tasminn ārpitā bhuvanāni viśvā ||
children.translated_text: The eye of the sun moves enclosed in the atmosphere; in it all beings are set.

children.text: sākañjānāṃ saptatham āhur ekajaṃ ṣaﾱ id yamā ṛṣayo devajā iti
children.translated_text: They call the seventh of those born together the one-born; six indeed are twins, the seers say, born of the gods.

children.text: teṣām iṣṭāni vihitāni dhāmaśa sthātre rejante vikṛtāni rūpaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their desired places are arranged according to station; their forms, variously made, tremble according to form.

children.text: striyaḥ satīs tāṃ u me puṃsa āhuḥ paśyad akṣaṇvān na vi cetad andhaḥ
children.translated_text: Though they are women, people call them men; the one with eyes sees, but the blind one does not discern.

children.text: kavir yaḥ putraḥ sa īm ā ciketa yas tā vijānāt sa pituṣ pitāsat ||
children.translated_text: The poet who is the son has understood them; whoever knows them will be his father's father.

children.text: avaḥ pareṇa para enāvareṇa padā vatsam bibhratī gaur ud asthāt
children.translated_text: Carrying her calf with her foot, below by the higher and above by the lower, the cow has stood up.

children.text: sā kadrīcī kaṃ svid ardham parāgāt kva svit sūte nahi yūthe antaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In what direction has she gone away? To what half? Where does she give birth? For she is not within the herd.

children.text: avaḥ pareṇa pitaraṃ yo asyānuveda para enāvareṇa
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the father of this one below by the higher and above by the lower,

children.text: kavīyamānaḥ ka iha pra vocad devam manaḥ kuto adhi prajātam ||
children.translated_text: who here, acting as a poet, can proclaim from where the divine mind was born?

children.text: ye arvāñcas tāṁ u parāca āhur ye parāñcas tāṁ u arvāca āhuḥ
children.translated_text: Those that are turned hither they call turned away; those that are turned away they call turned hither.

children.text: indraś ca yā cakrathuḥ soma tāni dhurā na yuktā rajaso vahanti ||
children.translated_text: The things that you two, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>, have made carry the spaces like yoked pairs on a yoke.

children.text: dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣam pari ṣasvajāte
children.translated_text: Two fair-winged birds, companions and friends, clasp the same tree.

children.text: tayor anyaḥ pippalaṃ svādv atty anaśnann anyo abhi cākaśīti ||
children.translated_text: Of the two, one eats the sweet fig; the other, not eating, looks on.

children.text: yatrā suparṇā amṛtasya bhāgam animeṣaṃ vidathābhisvaranti
children.translated_text: Where the fair-winged ones, unblinking, call out for their share of immortality at the sacred gatherings,

children.text: ino viśvasya bhuvanasya gopāḥ sa mā dhīraḥ pākam atrā viveśa ||
children.translated_text: there the lord, guardian of the whole world, the wise one, has entered me here, the simple one.

children.text: yasmin vṛkṣe madhvadaḥ suparṇā niviśante suvate cādhi viśve
children.translated_text: On the tree in which the honey-eating fair-winged ones settle and all bring forth above,

children.text: tasyed āhuḥ pippalaṃ svādv agre tan non naśad yaḥ pitaraṃ na veda ||
