children.translated_text: of that they say: the sweet fig is at the top; he who does not know the father will not attain it.

children.text: yad gāyatre adhi gāyatram āhitaṃ traiṣṭubhād vā traiṣṭubhaṃ niratakṣata
children.translated_text: What is set as gāyatra upon the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, or what they fashioned as traiṣṭubha from the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>,

children.text: yad vā jagaj jagaty āhitam padaṃ ya it tad vidus te amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: or what foot is set as jagat in the <s>Jagatī</s>: those who know that have reached immortality.

children.text: gāyatreṇa prati mimīte arkam arkeṇa sāma traiṣṭubhena vākam
children.translated_text: With the <s>Gāyatrī</s> he measures the chant; with the chant, the sāman; with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the recited word.

children.text: vākena vākaṃ dvipadā catuṣpadākṣareṇa mimate sapta vāṇīḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the recited word they measure the utterance, with the two-footed and the four-footed, and with the syllable they measure the seven voices.

children.text: jagatā sindhuṃ divy astabhāyad rathantare sūryam pary apaśyat
children.translated_text: With the <s>Jagatī</s> he propped up the river in heaven; in the <s>Rathantara</s> he beheld the sun on every side.

children.text: gāyatrasya samidhas tisra āhus tato mahnā pra ririce mahitvā ||
children.translated_text: They say the <s>Gāyatrī</s> has three kindling-sticks; from there it surpassed others in greatness through its might.

children.text: upa hvaye sudughāṃ dhenum etāṃ suhasto godhug uta dohad enām
children.translated_text: I call near this cow rich in milk; let the good-handed milker also milk her.

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ savaṃ savitā sāviṣan no 'bhīddho gharmas tad u ṣu pra vocam ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Savitṛ</s> impel our best impulse; the glowing heat has been kindled: this I now proclaim.

children.text: hiṃkṛṇvatī vasupatnī vasūnāṃ vatsam icchantī manasābhy āgāt
children.translated_text: Lowing, mistress of goods and rich in goods, desiring her calf, she has come toward him with her mind.

children.text: duhām aśvibhyām payo aghnyeyaṃ sā vardhatām mahate saubhagāya ||
children.translated_text: Let this inviolable cow give milk for the <s>Aśvins</s>; may she grow for great good fortune.

children.text: gaur amīmed anu vatsam miṣantam mūrdhānaṃ hiṅṅ akṛṇon mātavā u
children.translated_text: The cow has bellowed after the blinking calf; as a mother she made the lowing sound with her head.

children.text: sṛkvāṇaṃ gharmam abhi vāvaśānā mimāti māyum payate payobhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yearning toward the steaming gharmá as it rushes forth, she bellows her call and swells with milk.

children.text: ayaṃ sa śiṅkte yena gaur abhīvṛtā mimāti māyuṃ dhvasanāv adhi śritā
children.translated_text: This one bellows by which the cow, enclosed, sounds her call, resting upon the two resounding supports.

children.text: sā cittibhir ni hi cakāra martyaṃ vidyud bhavantī prati vavrim auhata ||
children.translated_text: With her thoughts she has brought the mortal under her power; becoming lightning, she has cast off her covering.

children.text: anacchaye turagātu jīvam ejad dhruvam madhya ā pastyānām
children.translated_text: The living one, moving swiftly without shade, trembles, yet is fixed in the middle of the dwellings.

children.text: jīvo mṛtasya carati svadhābhir amartyo martyenā sayoniḥ ||
children.translated_text: The living one moves by his own powers from the dead; immortal, he shares one womb with the mortal.

children.text: apaśyaṃ gopām anipadyamānam ā ca parā ca pathibhiś carantam
children.translated_text: I saw the herdsman who never stumbles, moving on paths hither and away.

children.text: sa sadhrīcīḥ sa viṣūcīr vasāna ā varīvarti bhuvaneṣv antaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Clothing himself in those that go together and those that go apart, he turns around within the worlds.

children.text: ya īṃ cakāra na so asya veda ya īṃ dadarśa hirug in nu tasmāt
children.translated_text: He who made it does not know it; he who saw it is hidden away from it.

children.text: sa mātur yonā parivīto antar bahuprajā nirṛtim ā viveśa ||
children.translated_text: Wrapped within his mother's womb, he has entered destruction, rich in offspring.

children.text: dyaur me pitā janitā nābhir atra bandhur me mātā pṛthivī mahīyam
children.translated_text: Heaven is my father, my begetter; here is my navel. My kin is my mother, this great earth.

children.text: uttānayoś camvor yonir antar atrā pitā duhitur garbham ādhāt ||
children.translated_text: Between the two upturned bowls is the womb; here the father placed the embryo of the daughter.

children.text: pṛcchāmi tvā param antam pṛthivyāḥ pṛcchāmi yatra bhuvanasya nābhiḥ
children.translated_text: I ask you the furthest end of the earth; I ask where the navel of the world is.

children.text: pṛcchāmi tvā vṛṣṇo aśvasya retaḥ pṛcchāmi vācaḥ paramaṃ vyoma ||
children.translated_text: I ask you the seed of the vigorous horse; I ask the supreme heaven of speech.

children.text: iyaṃ vediḥ paro antaḥ pṛthivyā ayaṃ yajño bhuvanasya nābhiḥ
children.translated_text: This altar is the furthest end of the earth; this sacrifice is the navel of the world.

children.text: ayaṃ somo vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto brahmāyaṃ vācaḥ paramaṃ vyoma ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Soma</s> is the seed of the vigorous horse; this <s>brahman</s> (sacred formulation) is the supreme heaven of speech.

children.text: saptārdhagarbhā bhuvanasya reto viṣṇos tiṣṭhanti pradiśā vidharmaṇi
children.translated_text: Seven half-embryos, the seed of the world, stand in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s directions, in accordance with the law.

children.text: te dhītibhir manasā te vipaścitaḥ paribhuvaḥ pari bhavanti viśvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: By their inspired thoughts, by their mind, those discerning ones, encompassing, encompass everything from every side.

children.text: na vi jānāmi yad ivedam asmi niṇyaḥ saṃnaddho manasā carāmi
children.translated_text: I do not know what sort of thing I am; bound in secrecy, I go about with my mind.

children.text: yadā māgan prathamajā ṛtasyād id vāco aśnuve bhāgam asyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the firstborn of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order) came to me, then I obtained a share of this speech.

children.text: apāṅ prāṅ eti svadhayā gṛbhīto 'martyo martyenā sayoniḥ
children.translated_text: Held by its own power, it goes backward and forward; immortal, it shares one womb with the mortal.

children.text: tā śaśvantā viṣūcīnā viyantā ny anyaṃ cikyur na ni cikyur anyam ||
children.translated_text: Those two, eternal and going apart, move separately; people observe one, but do not observe the other.

children.text: ṛco akṣare parame vyoman yasmin devā adhi viśve niṣeduḥ
children.translated_text: The hymns are in the imperishable syllable, in the supreme heaven, where all the gods have taken their seats.

children.text: yas tan na veda kim ṛcā kariṣyati ya it tad vidus ta ime sam āsate ||
children.translated_text: He who does not know that: what will he do with a hymn? Those who do know it, they sit together here.

children.text: sūyavasād bhagavatī hi bhūyā atho vayam bhagavantaḥ syāma
children.translated_text: May you become fortunate with good pasture, and may we too become fortunate.

children.text: addhi tṛṇam aghnye viśvadānīm piba śuddham udakam ācarantī ||
children.translated_text: Eat grass, O inviolable cow, at every season; drink pure water as you move about.

children.text: gaurīr mimāya salilāni takṣaty ekapadī dvipadī sā catuṣpadī
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurī</s> has bellowed, fashioning the waters: one-footed, two-footed, she is four-footed,

children.text: aṣṭāpadī navapadī babhūvuṣī sahasrākṣarā parame vyoman ||
children.translated_text: having become eight-footed, nine-footed, and thousand-syllabled in the supreme heaven.

children.text: tasyāḥ samudrā adhi vi kṣaranti tena jīvanti pradiśaś catasraḥ
children.translated_text: From her the oceans flow forth; by her the four directions live.

children.text: tataḥ kṣaraty akṣaraṃ tad viśvam upa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: From there the imperishable syllable streams forth; on that the whole world lives.

children.text: śakamayaṃ dhūmam ārād apaśyaṃ viṣūvatā para enāvareṇa
children.translated_text: From afar I saw the smoke made of dung, by the solstitial turning, beyond the nearer and the farther one.

children.text: ukṣāṇam pṛśnim apacanta vīrās tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan ||
children.translated_text: The heroes cooked the dappled bull; those were the first <s>dharmas</s> (cosmic ordinances).

children.text: trayaḥ keśina ṛtuthā vi cakṣate saṃvatsare vapata eka eṣām
children.translated_text: Three long-haired ones look forth according to the seasons; in the year one of them shaves.

children.text: viśvam eko abhi caṣṭe śacībhir dhrājir ekasya dadṛśe na rūpam ||
children.translated_text: One watches over the whole world with powers; the rush of one is seen, but not his form.

children.text: catvāri vāk parimitā padāni tāni vidur brāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Speech is measured out in four quarters; those inspired <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> know them.

children.text: guhā trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṃ vāco manuṣyā vadanti ||
children.translated_text: Three, hidden in secret, do not stir; human beings speak the fourth quarter of speech.

children.text: indram mitraṃ varuṇam agnim āhur atho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān
children.translated_text: They call him <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Agni</s>; also he is the heavenly fair-winged <s>Garuṭmān</s>.

children.text: ekaṃ sad viprā bahudhā vadanty agniṃ yamam mātariśvānam āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Reality is one; inspired poets speak of it in many ways. They call it <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Mātariśvan</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divam ut patanti
children.translated_text: The tawny, fair-winged ones, clothed in waters, rise up to heaven on their black path.

children.text: ta āvavṛtran sadanād ṛtasyād id ghṛtena pṛthivī vy udyate ||
children.translated_text: They have turned back from the seat of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order); from there the earth is spread out with ghee.

children.text: dvādaśa pradhayaś cakram ekaṃ trīṇi nabhyāni ka u tac ciketa
children.translated_text: One wheel has twelve fellies and three hubs; who indeed understands this?

children.text: tasmin sākaṃ triśatā na śaṅkavo 'rpitāḥ ṣaṣṭir na calācalāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In it, together, as it were, three hundred pegs are fixed, and sixty, as it were, moving yet unmoving.

children.text: yas te stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūr yena viśvā puṣyasi vāryāṇi
children.translated_text: That breast of yours which lies ready, which brings delight, by which you nourish all desirable goods,

children.text: yo ratnadhā vasuvid yaḥ sudatraḥ sarasvati tam iha dhātave kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which holds treasures, finds wealth, and is very generous, O <s>Sarasvati</s>: place that here for bestowal.

children.text: yajñena yajñam ayajanta devās tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan
children.translated_text: By sacrifice the gods sacrificed to Sacrifice; those were the first <s>dharma</s>s (sacred ordinances).

children.text: te ha nākam mahimānaḥ sacanta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those powers accompanied the height of heaven, where the earlier <s>Sadhyas</s>, the gods, dwell.

children.text: samānam etad udakam uc caity ava cāhabhiḥ
children.translated_text: This same water rises up and comes down with the days.

children.text: bhūmim parjanyā jinvanti divaṃ jinvanty agnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rain-clouds quicken the earth; the fires quicken heaven.

children.text: divyaṃ suparṇaṃ vāyasam bṛhantam apāṃ garbhaṃ darśatam oṣadhīnām
children.translated_text: I call for aid <s>Sarasvant</s>, the heavenly, fair-winged, great bird, the visible embryo of the waters and of the plants,

children.text: abhīpato vṛṣṭibhis tarpayantaṃ sarasvantam avase johavīmi ||
children.translated_text: who, approaching, satisfies with rains.

children.text: Chapter 165
kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīﾱāḥ samānyā marutaḥ sam mimikṣuḥ
children.translated_text: With what splendor did the <s>Maruts</s>, of equal age and dwelling together, mingle as one?

children.text: kayā matī kuta etāsa ete 'rcanti śuṣmaṃ vṛṣaṇo vasūyā ||
children.translated_text: By what thought, and from where, have these bulls come here, shining with might and seeking wealth?

children.text: kasya brahmāṇi jujuṣur yuvānaḥ ko adhvare maruta ā vavarta
children.translated_text: Whose sacred formulations have the young ones accepted? Who has turned you, O <s>Maruts</s>, toward the rite?

children.text: śyenāṁ iva dhrajato antarikṣe kena mahā manasā rīramāma ||
children.translated_text: Like falcons darting in the mid-space, by what great mind have we taken delight?

children.text: kutas tvam indra māhinaḥ sann eko yāsi satpate kiṃ ta itthā
children.translated_text: From where do you, O <s>Indra</s>, mighty and alone, go, O lord of the good? What is this intention of yours?

children.text: sam pṛcchase samarāṇaḥ śubhānair voces tan no harivo yat te asme ||
children.translated_text: You question us, meeting with the bright ones; tell that to us, O you of the bay horses, what you have for us.

children.text: brahmāṇi me matayaḥ śaṃ sutāsaḥ śuṣma iyarti prabhṛto me adriḥ
children.translated_text: My prayers and thoughts are auspicious; the pressed draughts are ready. The pressing-stone, set in motion, stirs up my might.

children.text: ā śāsate prati haryanty ukthemā harī vahatas tā no accha ||
children.translated_text: They make their request and welcome these uttered hymns; may the two bay horses carry them here to us.

children.text: ato vayam antamebhir yujānāḥ svakṣatrebhis tanvaḥ śumbhamānāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore we, yoked with those nearest to us and adorning our bodies with our own powers,

children.text: mahobhir etāṁ upa yujmahe nv indra svadhām anu hi no babhūtha ||
children.translated_text: now join ourselves to these great powers, O <s>Indra</s>; for you have become ours according to your own nature.

children.text: kva syā vo marutaḥ svadhāsīd yan mām ekaṃ samadhattāhihatye
children.translated_text: Where was that own power of yours, O <s>Maruts</s>, when you set me alone in the slaying of <s>Ahi</s>?

children.text: ahaṃ hy ugras taviṣas tuviṣmān viśvasya śatror anamaṃ vadhasnaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For I, fierce, forceful, and very mighty, bent down every enemy with my blows.

children.text: bhūri cakartha yujyebhir asme samānebhir vṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ
children.translated_text: You have done much for us with your yoked companions, with equal manly powers, O bull.

children.text: bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭhendra kratvā maruto yad vaśāma ||
children.translated_text: For we shall do many things, O most powerful <s>Indra</s>, by resolve, O <s>Maruts</s>, whenever we wish.

children.text: vadhīṃ vṛtram maruta indriyeṇa svena bhāmena taviṣo babhūvān
children.translated_text: I slew <s>Vritra</s> with my <s>Indra</s>-power, becoming strong through my own fury and force.

children.text: aham etā manave viśvaścandrāḥ sugā apaś cakara vajrabāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: I, armed with the thunderbolt, made all these lovely waters easy to pass for <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: anuttam ā te maghavan nakir nu na tvāvāṁ asti devatā vidānaḥ
children.translated_text: No one now is higher than you, O <s>Maghavan</s>; no deity known is like you.

children.text: na jāyamāno naśate na jāto yāni kariṣyā kṛṇuhi pravṛddha ||
children.translated_text: Neither one being born nor one already born reaches the deeds that you will do; perform them, O grown mighty one.

children.text: ekasya cin me vibhv astv ojo yā nu dadhṛṣvān kṛṇavai manīṣā
children.translated_text: Let the force even of one become mine, that bold deed which I shall accomplish with insight.

children.text: ahaṃ hy ugro maruto vidāno yāni cyavam indra id īśa eṣām ||
children.translated_text: For I am the fierce one, O <s>Maruts</s>, the knowing <s>Indra</s>; I am lord of these things that I set in motion.

children.text: amandan mā maruta stomo atra yan me naraḥ śrutyam brahma cakra
children.translated_text: The praise has gladdened me here, O <s>Maruts</s>, since the men have made for me a renowned sacred formulation,

children.text: indrāya vṛṣṇe sumakhāya mahyaṃ sakhye sakhāyas tanve tanūbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for me, <s>Indra</s> the bull, the well-battling one; as friends in friendship, with their bodies, they have aided my body.

children.text: eved ete prati mā rocamānā anedyaḥ śrava eṣo dadhānāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus these, shining toward me, bearing blameless fame,

children.text: saṃcakṣyā marutaś candravarṇā acchānta me chadayāthā ca nūnam ||
children.translated_text: I shall behold the moon-bright <s>Maruts</s>; now you have come near me and covered me with favor.

children.text: ko nv atra maruto māmahe vaḥ pra yātana sakhīṃr acchā sakhāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Who now here, O <s>Maruts</s>, shall magnify you? Go forth, friends, toward your friends.

children.text: manmāni citrā apivātayanta eṣām bhūta navedā ma ṛtānām ||
children.translated_text: Making their bright thoughts resound, become known to me as possessors of <s>rta</s> (cosmic order).

children.text: ā yad duvasyād duvase na kārur asmāñcakre mānyasya medhā
children.translated_text: When the singer has worshiped you for worship, the wisdom of the honorable one has made us its own.

children.text: o ṣu vartta maruto vipram acchemā brahmāṇi jaritā vo arcat ||
children.translated_text: Turn quickly, O <s>Maruts</s>, toward the inspired poet; the singer praises these sacred formulations of yours.

children.text: eṣa va stomo maruta iyaṃ gīr māndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ
children.translated_text: This is your praise, O <s>Maruts</s>; this song is from <s>Mandarya</s>, the honorable singer.

children.text: eṣā yāsīṣṭa tanve vayāṃ vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: May this attain strength for the body; may we find refreshment and a life-giving refuge.

children.text: Chapter 166
tan nu vocāma rabhasāya janmane pūrvam mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya ketave
children.translated_text: Now let us proclaim the ancient greatness of the forceful birth, the sign of the bull.

children.text: aidheva yāman marutas tuviṣvaṇo yudheva śakrās taviṣāṇi kartana ||
children.translated_text: Like kindled fires on the course, O loudly roaring <s>Maruts</s>, like powerful fighters in battle, display your strengths.

children.text: nityaṃ na sūnum madhu bibhrata upa krīﾱanti krīﾱā vidatheṣu ghṛṣvayaḥ
children.translated_text: Always, like sons bearing sweetness, they play near; playful and eager in the assemblies.

children.text: nakṣanti rudrā avasā namasvinaṃ na mardhanti svatavaso haviṣkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Rudras</s> reach the reverent man with aid; self-strong, they do not injure the maker of oblation.

children.text: yasmā ūmāso amṛtā arāsata rāyas poṣaṃ ca haviṣā dadāśuṣe
children.translated_text: For him to whom the immortal helpers grant increase of wealth and nourishment when he honors them with oblation,

children.text: ukṣanty asmai maruto hitā iva purū rajāṃsi payasā mayobhuvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for him the <s>Maruts</s>, like beneficent ones, pour out many spaces with bliss-bringing milk.

children.text: ā ye rajāṃsi taviṣībhir avyata pra va evāsaḥ svayatāso adhrajan
children.translated_text: When they clothed the realms with their powers, your self-guided blasts rushed forward.

children.text: bhayante viśvā bhuvanāni harmyā citro vo yāmaḥ prayatāsv ṛṣṭiṣu ||
children.translated_text: All beings and houses tremble; wondrous is your course when the spears are set in motion.

children.text: yat tveṣayāmā nadayanta parvatān divo vā pṛṣṭhaṃ naryā acucyavuḥ
children.translated_text: When, in blazing courses, they make the mountains roar, or have shaken the back of heaven, O men,

children.text: viśvo vo ajman bhayate vanaspatī rathīyantīva pra jihīta oṣadhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: every forest tree fears your advance; the plant bends forward as if eager for the chariot.

children.text: yūyaṃ na ugrā marutaḥ sucetunāriṣṭagrāmāḥ sumatim pipartana
children.translated_text: You, fierce <s>Maruts</s>, with good wisdom, bring us kindly favor and villages unharmed.

children.text: yatrā vo didyud radati krivirdatī riṇāti paśvaḥ sudhiteva barhaṇā ||
children.translated_text: Where your lightning, biting with crooked teeth, tears the cattle like a well-sharpened axe.

children.text: pra skambhadeṣṇā anavabhrarādhaso 'lātṛṇāso vidatheṣu suṣṭutāḥ
children.translated_text: Firm in support, rich in unobstructed gifts, not withholding, well-praised in the rites,

children.text: arcanty arkam madirasya pītaye vidur vīrasya prathamāni pauṃsyā ||
children.translated_text: they sing the chant for the drinking of the exhilarating draught; they know the first heroic powers of the hero.

children.text: śatabhujibhis tam abhihruter aghāt pūrbhī rakṣatā maruto yam āvata
children.translated_text: With a hundred protections guard him from assault, O <s>Maruts</s>, the man whom you aid with strongholds,

children.text: janaṃ yam ugrās tavaso virapśinaḥ pāthanā śaṃsāt tanayasya puṣṭiṣu ||
children.translated_text: the man whom you, fierce, powerful, and mighty, protect from denunciation in the prospering of his offspring.

children.text: viśvāni bhadrā maruto ratheṣu vo mithaspṛdhyeva taviṣāṇy āhitā
children.translated_text: All auspicious things are set in your chariots, O <s>Maruts</s>; your strengths are laid there as if competing with one another.

children.text: aṃseṣv ā vaḥ prapatheṣu khādayo 'kṣo vaś cakrā samayā vi vāvṛte ||
children.translated_text: On your shoulders and on your paths are ornaments; your axle and wheels turn all together.

children.text: bhūrīṇi bhadrā naryeṣu bāhuṣu vakṣassu rukmā rabhasāso añjayaḥ
children.translated_text: Many auspicious things are on their manly arms; on their breasts are golden ornaments, and impetuous are their adornments.

children.text: aṃseṣv etāḥ paviṣu kṣurā adhi vayo na pakṣān vy anu śriyo dhire ||
children.translated_text: These are on their shoulders; razors are upon their wheel-rims, and they have arranged their splendors like birds their wings.

children.text: mahānto mahnā vibhvo vibhūtayo dūredṛśo ye divyā iva stṛbhiḥ
children.translated_text: Great in greatness, far-extending in their manifestations, far-seeing, heavenly as if with stars,

children.text: mandrāḥ sujihvāḥ svaritāra āsabhiḥ sammiślā indre marutaḥ pariṣṭubhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: delightful, good-tongued, sounding with their mouths, the <s>Maruts</s> are mingled around <s>Indra</s> in praise.

children.text: tad vaḥ sujātā maruto mahitvanaṃ dīrghaṃ vo dātram aditer iva vratam
children.translated_text: That, well-born <s>Maruts</s>, is your greatness; long-lasting is your gift, like the ordinance of <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: indraś cana tyajasā vi hruṇāti taj janāya yasmai sukṛte arādhvam ||
children.translated_text: Not even <s>Indra</s> overturns it by force; that is for the man, the doer of good, to whom you have shown favor.

children.text: tad vo jāmitvam marutaḥ pare yuge purū yacchaṃsam amṛtāsa āvata
children.translated_text: That kinship of yours, O <s>Maruts</s>, in a later age: protect the much-praised man, O immortals.

children.text: ayā dhiyā manave śruṣṭim āvyā sākaṃ naro daṃsanair ā cikitrire ||
children.translated_text: With this thought, making obedience manifest for <s>Manu</s>, the heroes together made themselves known by their wondrous powers.

children.text: yena dīrgham marutaḥ śūśavāma yuṣmākena parīṇasā turāsaḥ
children.translated_text: By that fullness of yours, O swift <s>Maruts</s>, we have long grown strong.

children.text: ā yat tatanan vṛjane janāsa ebhir yajñebhis tad abhīṣṭim aśyām ||
children.translated_text: When people stretched it out in the enclosure, with these sacrifices may I attain that desired help.

children.text: eṣa va stomo maruta iyaṃ gīr māndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ
children.translated_text: This praise is for you, O <s>Maruts</s>; this is the song of <s>Māndārya</s>, the honored poet.

children.text: eṣā yāsīṣṭa tanve vayāṃ vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: May it go to your person for strength; may we find nourishment, a stronghold, and life-giving support.

children.text: Chapter 167
sahasraṃ ta indrotayo naḥ sahasram iṣo harivo gūrtatamāḥ
children.translated_text: A thousand helps, O <s>Indra</s>, a thousand refreshments for us, O bay-horsed one, most welcome;

children.text: sahasraṃ rāyo mādayadhyai sahasriṇa upa no yantu vājāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a thousand riches to gladden us; may thousandfold prizes come near to us.

children.text: ā no 'vobhir maruto yāntv acchā jyeṣṭhebhir vā bṛhaddivaiḥ sumāyāḥ
children.translated_text: May the <s>Maruts</s> come hither to us with aids, with the greatest aids, O greatly heavenly and skillful ones,

children.text: adha yad eṣāṃ niyutaḥ paramāḥ samudrasya cid dhanayanta pāre ||
children.translated_text: and when their highest teams thunder for wealth even beyond the sea.

children.text: mimyakṣa yeṣu sudhitā ghṛtācī hiraṇyanirṇig uparā na ṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: In whom the well-set, ghee-bright, gold-adorned spear has gleamed, like a hidden blade,

children.text: guhā carantī manuṣo na yoṣā sabhāvatī vidathyeva saṃ vāk ||
children.translated_text: moving in secret like a woman among men, possessing assembly-speech as in the ritual gathering.

children.text: parā śubhrā ayāso yavyā sādhāraṇyeva maruto mimikṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Bright, tireless, youthful, the <s>Maruts</s> have mingled, as if in a common pasture.

children.text: na rodasī apa nudanta ghorā juṣanta vṛdhaṃ sakhyāya devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The terrible gods do not thrust heaven and earth apart; they enjoy increase for the sake of friendship.

children.text: joṣad yad īm asuryā sacadhyai viṣitastukā rodasī nṛmaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: When queenly <s>Rodasī</s>, with loosened locks and heroic spirit, is pleased to join herself to them,

children.text: ā sūryeva vidhato rathaṃ gāt tveṣapratīkā nabhaso netyā ||
children.translated_text: she goes to the rite like the sun to the chariot, brilliant-faced, a guide from the cloud.

children.text: āsthāpayanta yuvatiṃ yuvānaḥ śubhe nimiślāṃ vidatheṣu pajrām
children.translated_text: The young men set the young woman in place, shining, quick-glancing, and strong in the assemblies,

children.text: arko yad vo maruto haviṣmān gāyad gāthaṃ sutasomo duvasyan ||
children.translated_text: when your oblation-bearing singer, O <s>Maruts</s>, with Soma pressed, sang the chant while serving you.

children.text: pra taṃ vivakmi vakmyo ya eṣām marutām mahimā satyo asti
children.translated_text: I proclaim that praiseworthy greatness of these <s>Maruts</s>, which is true.

children.text: sacā yad īṃ vṛṣamaṇā ahaṃyu sthirā cij janīr vahate subhāgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When, accompanying him, proud and self-willed, even firm women bear the fortunate one.

children.text: pānti mitrāvaruṇāv avadyāc cayata īm aryamo apraśastān
children.translated_text: <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> guard him from blame; <s>Aryaman</s> drives away the disapproved ones.

children.text: uta cyavante acyutā dhruvāṇi vāvṛdha īm maruto dātivāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the unmoving, fixed things are shaken; the liberal giver grows strong with the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: nahī nu vo maruto anty asme ārāttāc cicchavaso antam āpuḥ
children.translated_text: For now, O <s>Maruts</s>, no one near us, nor even from afar, has reached the limit of your might.

children.text: te dhṛṣṇunā śavasā śūśuvāṃso 'rṇo na dveṣo dhṛṣatā pari ṣṭhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They, swollen with bold force, stand around hatred like a flood with daring power.

children.text: vayam adyendrasya preṣṭhā vayaṃ śvo vocemahi samarye
children.translated_text: Today may we be dearest to <s>Indra</s>; tomorrow may we speak out in the contest.

children.text: vayam purā mahi ca no anu dyūn tan na ṛbhukṣā narām anu ṣyāt ||
children.translated_text: May we be foremost, and great through our days; may <s>Ṛbhukṣan</s> attend to that for us among men.

children.text: eṣa va stomo maruta iyaṃ gīr māndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ
children.translated_text: This praise is for you, O <s>Maruts</s>; this is the song of <s>Māndārya</s>, the honored poet.

children.text: eṣā yāsīṣṭa tanve vayāṃ vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: May it go to your person for strength; may we find nourishment, a stronghold, and life-giving support.

children.text: Chapter 168
yajñā yajñā vaḥ samanā tuturvaṇir dhiyaṃ dhiyaṃ vo devayā u dadhidhve
children.translated_text: At each sacrifice, O overpowering ones, alike you uphold each inspired thought for the god-seeking man.

children.text: ā vo 'rvācaḥ suvitāya rodasyor mahe vavṛtyām avase suvṛktibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With well-spoken hymns I would turn you hither for welfare, for great aid from the two worlds.

children.text: vavrāso na ye svajāḥ svatavasa iṣaṃ svar abhijāyanta dhūtayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who, self-born and self-mighty like protecting covers, were born as shaking powers toward nourishment and light,

children.text: sahasriyāso apāṃ normaya āsā gāvo vandyāso nokṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thousandfold, like the waves of waters, like laudable cows, like bulls.

children.text: somāso na ye sutās tṛptāṃśavo hṛtsu pītāso duvaso nāsate
children.translated_text: Those who, like pressed Soma draughts, with satisfying shoots, drunk in the hearts, sit down for worship,

children.text: aiṣām aṃseṣu rambhiṇīva rārabhe hasteṣu khādiś ca kṛtiś ca saṃ dadhe ||
children.translated_text: on their shoulders she clings like a grasping woman; in their hands bracelet and ornament are set together.

children.text: ava svayuktā diva ā vṛthā yayur amartyāḥ kaśayā codata tmanā
children.translated_text: Self-yoked, the immortals came down from heaven at will; the whip drove them of itself.

children.text: areṇavas tuvijātā acucyavur dṛﾱhāni cin maruto bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dustless, strongly born, the <s>Maruts</s> with flashing spears shook even the firm things.

children.text: ko vo 'ntar maruta ṛṣṭividyuto rejati tmanā hanveva jihvayā
children.translated_text: Who among you, O <s>Maruts</s> whose spears are lightning, trembles by himself, like a tongue in the jaw?

children.text: dhanvacyuta iṣāṃ na yāmani purupraiṣā ahanyo naitaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shaking the wastes in the course of nourishments, much-sent forth, like <s>Naitaśa</s> of the days.

children.text: kva svid asya rajaso mahas paraṃ kvāvaram maruto yasminn āyaya
children.translated_text: Where indeed is the far limit of this great expanse? Where is the nearer one, O <s>Maruts</s>, to which you have come,

children.text: yac cyāvayatha vithureva saṃhitaṃ vy adriṇā patatha tveṣam arṇavam ||
children.translated_text: when you make what is joined tremble as if it were loose, and with the stone you scatter the roaring flood?

children.text: sātir na vo 'mavatī svarvatī tveṣā vipākā marutaḥ pipiṣvatī
children.translated_text: Your gift is strong, rich in sunlight, blazing, well-ripened, O <s>Maruts</s>, and overflowing.

children.text: bhadrā vo rātiḥ pṛṇato na dakṣiṇā pṛthujrayī asuryeva jañjatī ||
children.translated_text: Your gracious giving is fair, like the sacrificial fee of one who fills, broad-moving and stirring like divine power.

children.text: prati ṣṭobhanti sindhavaḥ pavibhyo yad abhriyāṃ vācam udīrayanti
children.translated_text: The rivers roar against the wheel-rims when they raise their cloudy voice.

children.text: ava smayanta vidyutaḥ pṛthivyāṃ yadī ghṛtam marutaḥ pruṣṇuvanti ||
children.translated_text: The lightnings smile down upon the earth when the <s>Maruts</s> sprinkle ghee-bright rain.

children.text: asūta pṛśnir mahate raṇāya tveṣam ayāsām marutām anīkam
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛśni</s> gave birth, for the great battle, to the brilliant troop of the tireless <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: te sapsarāso 'janayantābhvam ād it svadhām iṣirām pary apaśyan ||
children.translated_text: They, moving together, generated mighty force; then they perceived their own impelling law.

children.text: eṣa va stomo maruta iyaṃ gīr māndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ
children.translated_text: This praise is for you, O <s>Maruts</s>; this is the song of <s>Māndārya</s>, the honored poet.

children.text: eṣā yāsīṣṭa tanve vayāṃ vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: May it go to your person for strength; may we find nourishment, a stronghold, and life-giving support.

children.text: Chapter 169
mahaś cit tvam indra yata etān mahaś cid asi tyajaso varūtā
children.translated_text: Even from greatness, O <s>Indra</s>, you have set these free; even against great assault you are a protector.

children.text: sa no vedho marutāṃ cikitvān sumnā vanuṣva tava hi preṣṭhā ||
children.translated_text: So, O wise creator, knowing the <s>Maruts</s>, win favor for us; for they are most dear to you.

children.text: ayujran ta indra viśvakṛṣṭīr vidānāso niṣṣidho martyatrā
children.translated_text: They yoked the all-peopled forces for you, O <s>Indra</s>, knowing and irresistible among mortals.

children.text: marutām pṛtsutir hāsamānā svarmīﾱhasya pradhanasya sātau ||
children.translated_text: The battle-aid of the <s>Maruts</s>, laughing aloud, was present at the winning of the sun-bright prize.

children.text: amyak sā ta indra ṛṣṭir asme sanemy abhvam maruto junanti
children.translated_text: May that spear of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, be well directed toward us; may we win the overpowering prize; the <s>Maruts</s> set it in motion.

children.text: agniś ciddhi ṣmātase śuśukvān āpo na dvīpaṃ dadhati prayāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Agni</s> too, blazing for the one who is kindled, holds forth the offerings, as waters hold an island.

children.text: tvaṃ tū na indra taṃ rayiṃ dā ojiṣṭhayā dakṣiṇayeva rātim
children.translated_text: But you, O <s>Indra</s>, give us that wealth, a gift with your strongest liberality, as with a right hand.

children.text: stutaś ca yās te cakananta vāyo stanaṃ na madhvaḥ pīpayanta vājaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when praised, O <s>Vāyu</s>, the praises that pleased you filled the breast with sweetness and with prizes.

children.text: tve rāya indra tośatamāḥ praṇetāraḥ kasya cid ṛtāyoḥ
children.translated_text: In you, O <s>Indra</s>, are the leaders, most eager for wealth, for anyone who follows <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order).

children.text: te ṣu ṇo maruto mṛﾱayantu ye smā purā gātūyantīva devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: May those <s>Maruts</s> be gracious to us, those gods who formerly used to go as though seeking a path.

children.text: prati pra yāhīndra mīﾱhuṣo nṝn mahaḥ pārthive sadane yatasva
children.translated_text: Come forward to meet the bountiful men, O <s>Indra</s>; exert yourself in the great earthly seat.

children.text: adha yad eṣām pṛthubudhnāsa etās tīrthe nāryaḥ pauṃsyāni tasthuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when these broad-bottomed ones stood at the ford, their manly powers were set there like noble women.

children.text: prati ghorāṇām etānām ayāsām marutāṃ śṛṇva āyatām upabdiḥ
children.translated_text: Hear the approaching roar of these terrible, tireless <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: ye martyam pṛtanāyantam ūmair ṛṇāvānaṃ na patayanta sargaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They, with their powers and onrushes, cast down the mortal who seeks battle, as one casts down a debtor.

children.text: tvam mānebhya indra viśvajanyā radā marudbhiḥ śurudho goagrāḥ
children.translated_text: For the people, O <s>Indra</s>, grant universal goods, cow-led and sheltering, together with the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: stavānebhi stavase deva devair vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: Praised by the praisers, you are praised, god, together with the gods; may we obtain nourishment, shelter, and life-giving strength.

children.text: Chapter 170
na nūnam asti no śvaḥ kas tad veda yad adbhutam
children.translated_text: There is no now, nor tomorrow; who knows that wondrous thing?

children.text: anyasya cittam abhi saṃcareṇyam utādhītaṃ vi naśyati ||
children.translated_text: One should move toward the thought of another, yet even what has been learned disappears.

children.text: kiṃ na indra jighāṃsasi bhrātaro marutas tava
children.translated_text: Why do you wish to slay us, O <s>Indra</s>? The <s>Maruts</s> are your brothers.

children.text: tebhiḥ kalpasva sādhuyā mā naḥ samaraṇe vadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Set yourself in good order with them; do not strike us down in the encounter.

children.text: kiṃ no bhrātar agastya sakhā sann ati manyase
children.translated_text: Why, brother <s>Agastya</s>, though you are a friend, do you think too highly of yourself?

children.text: vidmā hi te yathā mano 'smabhyam in na ditsasi ||
children.translated_text: For we know what your mind is like; you certainly do not wish to give to us.

children.text: araṃ kṛṇvantu vediṃ sam agnim indhatām puraḥ
children.translated_text: Let them make the altar ready; let them kindle <s>Agni</s> in front.

children.text: tatrāmṛtasya cetanaṃ yajñaṃ te tanavāvahai ||
children.translated_text: There let us two extend for you the <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), the sign of the immortal.

children.text: tvam īśiṣe vasupate vasūnāṃ tvam mitrāṇām mitrapate dheṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: You are lord over goods, O lord of goods; you are the firmest lord of friends among friends.

children.text: indra tvam marudbhiḥ saṃ vadasvādha prāśāna ṛtuthā havīṃṣi ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>, speak together with the <s>Maruts</s>; then eat the offerings in due season.

children.text: Chapter 171
prati va enā namasāham emi sūktena bhikṣe sumatiṃ turāṇām
children.translated_text: I come before you with this homage; with a well-spoken hymn I beg the favor of the swift ones.

children.text: rarāṇatā maruto vedyābhir ni heﾱo dhatta vi mucadhvam aśvān ||
children.translated_text: Taking delight, O <s>Maruts</s>, in the altar-places, put away your anger and unyoke your horses.

children.text: eṣa va stomo maruto namasvān hṛdā taṣṭo manasā dhāyi devāḥ
children.translated_text: This praise of yours, O <s>Maruts</s>, reverent and shaped by the heart, has been set in place by the mind, O gods.

children.text: upem ā yāta manasā juṣāṇā yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhā namasa id vṛdhāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Come here, accepting it with your mind; for you are increased by homage alone.

children.text: stutāso no maruto mṛﾱayantūta stuto maghavā śambhaviṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Praised, may the <s>Maruts</s> be gracious to us, and, praised, may <s>Maghavan</s> be most auspicious.

children.text: ūrdhvā naḥ santu komyā vanāny ahāni viśvā maruto jigīṣā ||
children.translated_text: May our desired days stand high; may we win all contests, O <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: asmād ahaṃ taviṣād īṣamāṇa indrād bhiyā maruto rejamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Assailed by this mighty <s>Indra</s>, trembling from fear, O <s>Maruts</s>,

children.text: yuṣmabhyaṃ havyā niśitāny āsan tāny āre cakṛmā mṛﾱatā naḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sharpened oblations were meant for you; we have set them apart. Be gracious to us.

children.text: yena mānāsaś citayanta usrā vyuṣṭiṣu śavasā śaśvatīnām
children.translated_text: By that power the mindful ones awaken the bright cows at the dawnings of the everlasting days.

children.text: sa no marudbhir vṛṣabha śravo dhā ugra ugrebhi sthaviraḥ sahodāḥ ||
children.translated_text: May that bull, with the <s>Maruts</s>, bestow glory on us: fierce with the fierce ones, ancient, a giver of might.

children.text: tvam pāhīndra sahīyaso nṝn bhavā marudbhir avayātaheﾱāḥ
children.translated_text: Protect the stronger men, O <s>Indra</s>; with the <s>Maruts</s>, be one who keeps wrath away.

children.text: supraketebhiḥ sāsahir dadhāno vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: Holding brilliant aids and overpowering strength, may we obtain nourishment, shelter, and life-giving vigor.

children.text: Chapter 172
citro vo 'stu yāmaś citra ūtī sudānavaḥ
children.translated_text: Bright be your course, bright your help, O liberal ones.

children.text: maruto ahibhānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Maruts</s>, you whose radiance is serpent-like.

children.text: āre sā vaḥ sudānavo maruta ṛñjatī śaruḥ
children.translated_text: Far from us, O liberal <s>Maruts</s>, be your wounding arrow.

children.text: āre aśmā yam asyatha ||
children.translated_text: Far away be the stone that you hurl.

children.text: tṛṇaskandasya nu viśaḥ pari vṛṅkta sudānavaḥ
children.translated_text: Now turn aside from the people of <s>Tṛṇaskanda</s>, O liberal ones.

children.text: ūrdhvān naḥ karta jīvase ||
children.translated_text: Set us upright, so that we may live.

children.text: Chapter 173
gāyat sāma nabhanyaṃ yathā ver arcāma tad vāvṛdhānaṃ svarvat
children.translated_text: Sing the heavenly <s>sāman</s> (chant), as a bird might; let us praise that light-filled one who has grown strong.

children.text: gāvo dhenavo barhiṣy adabdhā ā yat sadmānaṃ divyaṃ vivāsān ||
children.translated_text: The cows, the milch-cows, unharmed upon the sacrificial grass, seek the heavenly dwelling.

children.text: arcad vṛṣā vṛṣabhiḥ sveduhavyair mṛgo nāśno ati yaj juguryāt
children.translated_text: The bull has sung with the bulls, with well-offered oblations; like a beast that is not hungry, let him not devour what is brought.

children.text: pra mandayur manāṃ gūrta hotā bharate maryo mithunā yajatraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gladdening <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), stirred in mind, bears the worshipful pair like a young man.

children.text: nakṣaddhotā pari sadma mitā yan bharad garbham ā śaradaḥ pṛthivyāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s> reaches the measured seat, bearing the embryo through the autumns of the earth.

children.text: krandad aśvo nayamāno ruvad gaur antar dūto na rodasī carad vāk ||
children.translated_text: The horse neighed as it was led; the cow bellowed; speech moved between heaven and earth like a messenger.

children.text: tā karmāṣatarāsmai pra cyautnāni devayanto bharante
children.translated_text: For him the god-seeking ones bring those deeds and impelling powers.

children.text: jujoṣad indro dasmavarcā nāsatyeva sugmyo ratheṣṭhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, of wondrous brilliance, took delight, like the <s>Nāṣatyas</s>, easy to call, standing on the chariot.

children.text: tam u ṣṭuhīndraṃ yo ha satvā yaḥ śūro maghavā yo ratheṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: Praise that <s>Indra</s>, who indeed is strong, who is heroic and bountiful, who stands on the chariot.

children.text: pratīcaś cid yodhīyān vṛṣaṇvān vavavruṣaś cit tamaso vihantā ||
children.translated_text: He fights even those turned against him; virile, he is the smiter even of enclosing darkness.

children.text: pra yad itthā mahinā nṛbhyo asty araṃ rodasī kakṣye nāsmai
children.translated_text: When, by greatness, he is such for men, the two worlds are fitting for him as a girth.

children.text: saṃ vivya indro vṛjanaṃ na bhūmā bharti svadhāvāṁ opaśam iva dyām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, self-powerful, has encompassed the wide enclosure like the earth; he bears heaven like a covering.

children.text: samatsu tvā śūra satām urāṇam prapathintamam paritaṃsayadhyai
children.translated_text: In battles, O hero, they call on you as the true one, the broad one, the best maker of paths, to be praised on every side.

children.text: sajoṣasa indram made kṣoṇīḥ sūriṃ cid ye anumadanti vājaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In shared exhilaration the peoples approve <s>Indra</s> with prizes, even the generous patron.

children.text: evā hi te śaṃ savanā samudra āpo yat ta āsu madanti devīḥ
children.translated_text: Thus indeed your invigorations are auspicious, ocean-like, when the divine waters rejoice in you.

children.text: viśvā te anu joṣyā bhūd gauḥ sūrīṃś cid yadi dhiṣā veṣi janān ||
children.translated_text: Everything desirable has become yours; even the cow is yours, if with inspired thought you seek patrons and peoples.

children.text: asāma yathā suṣakhāya ena svabhiṣṭayo narāṃ na śaṃsaiḥ
children.translated_text: May we be there for one who is a good friend, with our own aids, as men are with praises.

children.text: asad yathā na indro vandaneṣṭhās turo na karma nayamāna ukthā ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> be foremost for us in acts of praise, like a strong one whose hymns are being led to the rite.

children.text: viṣpardhaso narāṃ na śaṃsair asmākāsad indro vajrahastaḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s>, holding the thunderbolt, be ours, overcoming rivals through praises like those of men.

children.text: mitrāyuvo na pūrpatiṃ suśiṣṭau madhyāyuva upa śikṣanti yajñaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like those who seek friendship, under good instruction, they attend with sacrifices upon the lord of the stronghold in mid-life.

children.text: yajño hi ṣmendraṃ kaścid ṛndhañ juhurāṇaś cin manasā pariyan
children.translated_text: For some <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), even one approaching with the mind and invoking him, indeed strengthens <s>Indra</s>

children.text: tīrthe nācchā tātṛṣāṇam oko dīrgho na sidhram ā kṛṇoty adhvā ||
children.translated_text: At the ford, the long road does not make a home for the thirsting man, as though it were an easy path.

children.text: mo ṣū ṇa indrātra pṛtsu devair asti hi ṣmā te śuṣminn avayāḥ
children.translated_text: Do not, O <s>Indra</s>, abandon us here in battles with the gods; for, mighty one, your protection truly exists.

children.text: mahaś cid yasya mīﾱhuṣo yavyā haviṣmato maruto vandate gīḥ ||
children.translated_text: The song of the oblation-bearing singer praises the youthful <s>Maruts</s> of that great bounteous one.

children.text: eṣa stoma indra tubhyam asme etena gātuṃ harivo vido naḥ
children.translated_text: This hymn, O <s>Indra</s>, is for you from us; by it, O lord of the bay steeds, find a path for us.

children.text: ā no vavṛtyāḥ suvitāya deva vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: Turn toward us, O god, for good guidance; may we find refreshment, a living sustenance.

children.text: Chapter 174
tvaṃ rājendra ye ca devā rakṣā nṝn pāhy asura tvam asmān
children.translated_text: You are king, O <s>Indra</s>, and so are the gods; protect men, guard us, O lord.

children.text: tvaṃ satpatir maghavā nas tarutras tvaṃ satyo vasavānaḥ sahodāḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are the true lord, the bounteous one who carries us across; you are true, rich in goods, and giver of strength.

children.text: dano viśa indra mṛdhravācaḥ sapta yat puraḥ śarma śāradīr dart
children.translated_text: When, O <s>Indra</s>, you shattered the seven autumnal forts of the hostile-speaking peoples,

children.text: ṛṇor apo anavadyārṇā yūne vṛtram purukutsāya randhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: you released the flawless, flowing waters; for young <s>Purukutsa</s> you subdued <s>Vṛtra</s>.

children.text: ajā vṛta indra śūrapatnīr dyāṃ ca yebhiḥ puruhūta nūnam
children.translated_text: With those powers, O <s>Indra</s>, much-invoked one, by which you now encompassed the hero-wives and heaven,

children.text: rakṣo agnim aśuṣaṃ tūrvayāṇaṃ siṃho na dame apāṃsi vastoḥ ||
children.translated_text: you drove away the demon, the fireless and overpowering one, like a lion from the house and from the works of the dwelling.

children.text: śeṣan nu ta indra sasmin yonau praśastaye pavīravasya mahnā
children.translated_text: Now they rested there, O <s>Indra</s>, in that womb, for praise through the greatness of the roaring thunderbolt.

children.text: sṛjad arṇāṃsy ava yad yudhā gās tiṣṭhaddharī dhṛṣatā mṛṣṭa vājān ||
children.translated_text: When in battle you released the floods and the cows, the bay steeds stood firm, boldly winning the prizes.

children.text: vaha kutsam indra yasmiñcākan syūmanyū ṛjrā vātasyāśvā
children.translated_text: Carry <s>Kutsa</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, in whom you delighted; the straight horses of the wind are yoked to the pole.

children.text: pra sūraś cakraṃ vṛhatād abhīke 'bhi spṛdho yāsiṣad vajrabāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sun's wheel rolled forth from the high place nearby; with your thunderbolt-arm you drove against the rivals.

children.text: jaghanvāṁ indra mitrerūñcodapravṛddho harivo adāśūn
children.translated_text: Having struck down the false friends and the ungiving men, O lord of bay steeds, grown strong through the offering,

children.text: pra ye paśyann aryamaṇaṃ sacāyos tvayā śūrtā vahamānā apatyam ||
children.translated_text: those who looked upon <s>Aryaman</s> as an ally carried offspring, aided in battle by you.

children.text: rapat kavir indrārkasātau kṣāṃ dāsāyopabarhaṇīṃ kaḥ
children.translated_text: The poet sounded out in the contest for song, O <s>Indra</s>; he made the earth a support against the <s>Dāsa</s>.

children.text: karat tisro maghavā dānucitrā ni duryoṇe kuyavācam mṛdhi śret ||
children.translated_text: The bounteous one made three richly varied gifts; in the evil womb he laid low the ill-speaking <s>Kuyavāc</s>.

children.text: sanā tā ta indra navyā āguḥ saho nabho 'viraṇāya pūrvīḥ
children.translated_text: Of old these new powers came to you, O <s>Indra</s>, many strengths from heaven for the manly one.

children.text: bhinat puro na bhido adevīr nanamo vadhar adevasya pīyoḥ ||
children.translated_text: You split the ungodly forts as splitters do; the weapon of the godless hostile one did not bend us down.

children.text: tvaṃ dhunir indra dhunimatīr ṛṇor apaḥ sīrā na sravantīḥ
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Indra</s>, the shaker, released the shaking waters, streaming like furrows.

children.text: pra yat samudram ati śūra parṣi pārayā turvaśaṃ yaduṃ svasti ||
children.translated_text: When, O hero, you passed beyond the sea, carry <s>Turvaśa</s> and <s>Yadu</s> across in safety.

children.text: tvam asmākam indra viśvadha syā avṛkatamo narāṃ nṛpātā
children.translated_text: Be ours everywhere, O <s>Indra</s>, the most harmless among men, protector of men.

children.text: sa no viśvāsāṃ spṛdhāṃ sahodā vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: May he, giver of strength, overcome all our rivals; may we find refreshment, a living sustenance.

children.text: Chapter 175
matsy apāyi te mahaḥ pātrasyeva harivo matsaro madaḥ
children.translated_text: Your intoxicating draught has been drunk from the great vessel, like from a bowl, O lord of bay steeds.

children.text: vṛṣā te vṛṣṇa indur vājī sahasrasātamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your bull, the bull-like <s>Soma</s>-drop, is a steed, most able to win a thousand prizes.

children.text: ā nas te gantu matsaro vṛṣā mado vareṇyaḥ
children.translated_text: May your exhilarating draught come to us, a bull, a desirable intoxication,

children.text: sahāvāṁ indra sānasiḥ pṛtanāṣāﾱ amartyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: powerful, O <s>Indra</s>, winning possessions, conquering battles, immortal.

children.text: tvaṃ hi śūraḥ sanitā codayo manuṣo ratham
children.translated_text: For you are the hero and winner; you drove the chariot of man onward.

children.text: sahāvān dasyum avratam oṣaḥ pātraṃ na śociṣā ||
children.translated_text: Powerful one, you burned the lawless <s>Dasyu</s> like a vessel with flame.

children.text: muṣāya sūryaṃ kave cakram īśāna ojasā
children.translated_text: You stole the wheel of the sun, O inspired one, ruling by your might.

children.text: vaha śuṣṇāya vadhaṃ kutsaṃ vātasyāśvaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Carry <s>Kutsa</s>, with the horses of the wind, toward the weapon against <s>Śuṣṇa</s>.

children.text: śuṣmintamo hi te mado dyumnintama uta kratuḥ
children.translated_text: For your exhilaration is most mighty, and your resolve is most brilliant,

children.text: vṛtraghnā varivovidā maṃsīṣṭhā aśvasātamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: slaying <s>Vṛtra</s>, finding wide space, most thoughtful, and best at winning horses.

children.text: yathā pūrvebhyo jaritṛbhya indra maya ivāpo na tṛṣyate babhūtha
children.translated_text: As you became refreshment for the singers of old, O <s>Indra</s>, like waters for one who thirsts,

children.text: tām anu tvā nividaṃ johavīmi vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: following that summons I call you repeatedly; may we find refreshment, a living sustenance.

children.text: Chapter 176
matsi no vasyaiṣṭaya indram indo vṛṣā viśa
children.translated_text: Gladden <s>Indra</s> for our desired wealth, O <s>Soma</s>-drop; as a bull, enter the people.

children.text: ṛghāyamāṇa invasi śatrum anti na vindasi ||
children.translated_text: You press upon the raging enemy; near at hand you find no foe able to withstand you.

children.text: tasminn ā veśayā giro ya ekaś carṣaṇīnām
children.translated_text: Place the songs in him who alone is lord of the peoples.

children.text: anu svadhā yam upyate yavaṃ na carkṛṣad vṛṣā ||
children.translated_text: According to his own law he is poured out; like barley, the bull is repeatedly cultivated.

children.text: yasya viśvāni hastayoḥ pañca kṣitīnāṃ vasu
children.translated_text: In whose two hands are all the goods of the five peoples,

children.text: spāśayasva yo asmadhrug divyevāśanir jahi ||
children.translated_text: mark out the one who harms us; strike him like a thunderbolt from heaven.

children.text: asunvantaṃ samaṃ jahi dūṇāśaṃ yo na te mayaḥ
children.translated_text: Strike down the non-presser, the hostile man who gives you no delight.

children.text: asmabhyam asya vedanaṃ daddhi sūriś cid ohate ||
children.translated_text: Give us possession of this wealth; even the generous patron longs for it.

children.text: āvo yasya dvibarhaso 'rkeṣu sānuṣag asat
children.translated_text: When the aid of him of double greatness was continuous in the hymns,

children.text: ājāv indrasyendo prāvo vājeṣu vājinam ||
children.translated_text: in the contest, O <s>Soma</s>-drop, you furthered <s>Indra</s>'s steed, the prize-winning one in the prizes.

children.text: yathā pūrvebhyo jaritṛbhya indra maya ivāpo na tṛṣyate babhūtha
children.translated_text: As you became refreshment for the singers of old, O <s>Indra</s>, like waters for one who thirsts,

children.text: tām anu tvā nividaṃ johavīmi vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: following that summons I call you repeatedly; may we find refreshment, a living sustenance.

children.text: Chapter 177
ā carṣaṇiprā vṛṣabho janānāṃ rājā kṛṣṭīnām puruhūta indraḥ
children.translated_text: Come hither, O <s>Indra</s>, fulfiller of men, bull of peoples, king of tribes, much-invoked one.

children.text: stutaḥ śravasyann avasopa madrig yuktvā harī vṛṣaṇā yāhy arvāṅ ||
children.translated_text: Praised and seeking fame, come toward me with aid, having yoked your two bay, bullish steeds.

children.text: ye te vṛṣaṇo vṛṣabhāsa indra brahmayujo vṛṣarathāso atyāḥ
children.translated_text: Those bulls of yours, bull-like, yoked by sacred formulation, racers with a bull's chariot, O <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: tāṁ ā tiṣṭha tebhir ā yāhy arvāṅ havāmahe tvā suta indra some ||
children.translated_text: mount them and come here with them; we call you, O <s>Indra</s>, when the <s>Soma</s> has been pressed.

children.text: ā tiṣṭha rathaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ vṛṣā te sutaḥ somaḥ pariṣiktā madhūni
children.translated_text: Mount the bull-chariot; your pressed <s>Soma</s>, O bull, the honeyed draughts, has been sprinkled round.

children.text: yuktvā vṛṣabhyāṃ vṛṣabha kṣitīnāṃ haribhyāṃ yāhi pravatopa madrik ||
children.translated_text: Having yoked your two bull-like bay steeds, O bull of peoples, come down the slope toward me.

children.text: ayaṃ yajño devayā ayam miyedha imā brahmāṇy ayam indra somaḥ
children.translated_text: This sacrifice is god-directed, this is the oblation; these are the sacred formulations, and this, O <s>Indra</s>, is <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: stīrṇam barhir ā tu śakra pra yāhi pibā niṣadya vi mucā harī iha ||
children.translated_text: The sacrificial grass is strewn; come here, O <s>Śakra</s>, drink after sitting down, and unyoke the bay steeds here.

children.text: o suṣṭuta indra yāhy arvāṅ upa brahmāṇi mānyasya kāroḥ
children.translated_text: O well-praised <s>Indra</s>, come hither to the sacred formulations of the worthy singer.

children.text: vidyāma vastor avasā gṛṇanto vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: Singing, may we know help at daybreak through your aid; may we find refreshment, a living sustenance.

children.text: Chapter 178
yaddha syā ta indra śruṣṭir asti yayā babhūtha jaritṛbhya ūtī
children.translated_text: If that hearing obedience of yours exists, O <s>Indra</s>, by which you became aid for the singers,

children.text: mā naḥ kāmam mahayantam ā dhag viśvā te aśyām pary āpa āyoḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not burn away our swelling desire; may I attain all your protections through the course of life.

children.text: na ghā rājendra ā dabhan no yā nu svasārā kṛṇavanta yonau
children.translated_text: No one shall harm us, O king <s>Indra</s>, nor those two sisters who now make a womb for themselves.

children.text: āpaś cid asmai sutukā aveṣan gaman na indraḥ sakhyā vayaś ca ||
children.translated_text: Even the waters, easy to cross, entered him; may <s>Indra</s> come to us with friendship and vital strength.

children.text: jetā nṛbhir indraḥ pṛtsu śūraḥ śrotā havaṃ nādhamānasya kāroḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, conqueror with men in battles, the hero, is hearer of the call of the imploring poet.

children.text: prabhartā rathaṃ dāśuṣa upāka udyantā giro yadi ca tmanā bhūt ||
children.translated_text: He is the one who brings forward the chariot near for the giver, if by himself he becomes the raiser of songs.

children.text: evā nṛbhir indraḥ suśravasyā prakhādaḥ pṛkṣo abhi mitriṇo bhūt
children.translated_text: So may <s>Indra</s>, with men, seeking good renown, the breaker-open of prizes, be on the side of friends.

children.text: samarya iṣa stavate vivāci satrākaro yajamānasya śaṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the contest, with nourishment, he is praised in many voices; the sacrificer's praise is a maker of firm strength.

children.text: tvayā vayam maghavann indra śatrūn abhi ṣyāma mahato manyamānān
children.translated_text: Through you, O bountiful <s>Indra</s>, may we overcome enemies who think themselves great.

children.text: tvaṃ trātā tvam u no vṛdhe bhūr vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: You are the protector; become ours for increase. May we obtain nourishment, a secure dwelling, and life-giving bounty.

children.text: Chapter 179
pūrvīr ahaṃ śaradaḥ śaśramāṇā doṣā vastor uṣaso jarayantīḥ
children.translated_text: For many autumns I have labored, through nights and dawns that make old age come on.

children.text: mināti śriyaṃ jarimā tanūnām apy ū nu patnīr vṛṣaṇo jagamyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Old age diminishes the beauty of bodies; yet now the wives have come to their virile husbands.

children.text: ye ciddhi pūrva ṛtasāpa āsan sākaṃ devebhir avadann ṛtāni
children.translated_text: Even those ancient guardians of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order) who existed spoke truths together with the gods.

children.text: te cid avāsur nahy antam āpuḥ sam ū nu patnīr vṛṣabhir jagamyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They too grew old; they did not reach the end. So now the wives have come together with their bulls.

children.text: na mṛṣā śrāntaṃ yad avanti devā viśvā it spṛdho abhy aśnavāva
children.translated_text: The toil that the gods favor is not false; may we two overcome all contests.

children.text: jayāved atra śatanītham ājiṃ yat samyañcā mithunāv abhy ajāva ||
children.translated_text: May the wife win here the battle with a hundred courses, when we two, joined as a pair, drive toward it together.

children.text: nadasya mā rudhataḥ kāma āgann ita ājāto amutaḥ kutaścit
children.translated_text: Desire has come upon me for the bull who holds back the stream, born from here, from there, or from anywhere.

children.text: lopāmudrā vṛṣaṇaṃ nī riṇāti dhīram adhīrā dhayati śvasantam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lopāmudrā</s> draws the bull down; impatient, she drinks from the steadfast one as he pants.

children.text: imaṃ nu somam antito hṛtsu pītam upa bruve
children.translated_text: Now I address this <s>Soma</s>, drunk very near within the hearts.

children.text: yat sīm āgaś cakṛmā tat su mṛﾱatu pulukāmo hi martyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever offense we have committed, may he graciously forgive that, for a mortal has many desires.

children.text: agastyaḥ khanamānaḥ khanitraiḥ prajām apatyam balam icchamānaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s>, digging with spades, desiring progeny, offspring, and strength,

children.text: ubhau varṇāv ṛṣir ugraḥ pupoṣa satyā deveṣv āśiṣo jagāma ||
children.translated_text: the fierce seer nourished both classes; his true blessings reached the gods.

children.text: Chapter 180
yuvo rajāṃsi suyamāso aśvā ratho yad vām pary arṇāṃsi dīyat
children.translated_text: Well-guided are your horses through the realms, when your chariot flies around the floods.

children.text: hiraṇyayā vām pavayaḥ pruṣāyan madhvaḥ pibantā uṣasaḥ sacethe ||
children.translated_text: Your golden wheel-rims sprinkle; drinking sweetness, you accompany the dawns.

children.text: yuvam atyasyāva nakṣatho yad vipatmano naryasya prayajyoḥ
children.translated_text: You two reach the course of the racing, manly, worshipful one when he is in distress.

children.text: svasā yad vāṃ viśvagūrtī bharāti vājāyeṭṭe madhupāv iṣe ca ||
children.translated_text: When your all-praised sister brings it to you for prize and for nourishment, O drinkers of sweetness,

children.text: yuvam paya usriyāyām adhattam pakvam āmāyām ava pūrvyaṃ goḥ
children.translated_text: you two placed milk in the ruddy cow, the ancient ripe milk in the unripe cow.

children.text: antar yad vanino vām ṛtapsū hvāro na śucir yajate haviṣmān ||
children.translated_text: When, within, your woodland worshipper, true to <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), like a bright one offers with oblation,

children.text: yuvaṃ ha gharmam madhumantam atraye 'po na kṣodo 'vṛṇītam eṣe
children.translated_text: you two chose the honeyed <s>gharma</s> (hot offering) for <s>Atri</s>, like water or flood in his need for help.

children.text: tad vāṃ narāv aśvinā paśvaiṣṭī rathyeva cakrā prati yanti madhvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That sweetness goes toward you two, O men, O <s>Aśvins</s>, with the animals, like wheels along the road.

children.text: ā vāṃ dānāya vavṛtīya dasrā gor oheṇa taugryo na jivriḥ
children.translated_text: I would turn to you two for giving, O wonder-workers, like aged <s>Taugrya</s> with the cow's aid.

children.text: apaḥ kṣoṇī sacate māhinā vāṃ jūrṇo vām akṣur aṃhaso yajatrā ||
children.translated_text: The waters and the earth attend the greatness of you two; your axle, worthy of worship, is worn by distress.

children.text: ni yad yuvethe niyutaḥ sudānū upa svadhābhiḥ sṛjathaḥ purandhim
children.translated_text: When you yoke your teams, O good givers, and by your own powers release abundance,

children.text: preṣad veṣad vāto na sūrir ā mahe dade suvrato na vājam ||
children.translated_text: the generous patron takes the great prize to himself, like the wind rushing and settling, like one faithful to vows.

children.text: vayaṃ ciddhi vāṃ jaritāraḥ satyā vipanyāmahe vi paṇir hitāvān
children.translated_text: For we, your true singers, praise you with discernment; the <s>Paṇi</s> is far apart, though set in place.

children.text: adhā ciddhi ṣmāśvināv anindyā pātho hi ṣmā vṛṣaṇāv antidevam ||
children.translated_text: And indeed, O faultless <s>Aśvins</s>, you two are near; for the virile ones are on the path toward the god.

children.text: yuvāṃ ciddhi ṣmāśvināv anu dyūn virudrasya prasravaṇasya sātau
children.translated_text: You two indeed, O <s>Aśvins</s>, day after day, at the winning of the outpouring stream,

children.text: agastyo narāṃ nṛṣu praśastaḥ kārādhunīva citayat sahasraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s>, praised among men, has awakened you with thousands, like a sounding singer.

children.text: pra yad vahethe mahinā rathasya pra syandrā yātho manuṣo na hotā
children.translated_text: When you drive forth by the greatness of the chariot, when you go forward in your stream like a human <s>hotar</s> (sacrificial priest),

children.text: dhattaṃ sūribhya uta vā svaśvyaṃ nāsatyā rayiṣācaḥ syāma ||
children.translated_text: grant wealth to the patrons, and also good horses; O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, may we be accompanied by riches.

children.text: taṃ vāṃ rathaṃ vayam adyā huvema stomair aśvinā suvitāya navyam
children.translated_text: Today we would call that new chariot of yours with hymns, O <s>Aśvins</s>, for good aid,

children.text: ariṣṭanemim pari dyām iyānaṃ vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: with uninjured rim, travelling around heaven. May we obtain nourishment, a secure dwelling, and life-giving bounty.

children.text: Chapter 181
kad u preṣṭhāv iṣāṃ rayīṇām adhvaryantā yad unninītho apām
children.translated_text: When, O dearest ones of foods and riches, acting as <s>adhvaryus</s> (ritual officiants), did you raise up the waters?

children.text: ayaṃ vāṃ yajño akṛta praśastiṃ vasudhitī avitārā janānām ||
children.translated_text: This sacrifice has made praise for you, O treasure-placing protectors of peoples.

children.text: ā vām aśvāsaḥ śucayaḥ payaspā vātaraṃhaso divyāso atyāḥ
children.translated_text: May your bright horses, milk-drinking, wind-swift, heavenly racers,

children.text: manojuvo vṛṣaṇo vītapṛṣṭhā eha svarājo aśvinā vahantu ||
children.translated_text: mind-swift, virile, with well-spread backs, bring you here, self-ruling <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: ā vāṃ ratho 'vanir na pravatvān sṛpravandhuraḥ suvitāya gamyāḥ
children.translated_text: May your chariot come hither for good aid, like a downward-flowing riverbed, with an easy-running frame.

children.text: vṛṣṇa sthātārā manaso javīyān ahampūrvo yajato dhiṣṇyā yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its two virile standers, swifter than thought, worthy of worship, press forward as if each would be first.

children.text: iheha jātā sam avāvaśītām arepasā tanvā nāmabhiḥ svaiḥ
children.translated_text: Here and here, born here, the two have called out together, with spotless body and with their own names.

children.text: jiṣṇur vām anyaḥ sumakhasya sūrir divo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe ||
children.translated_text: One of you, victorious, is the patron of the good sacrifice; the other is borne as the fortunate son of heaven.

children.text: pra vāṃ niceruḥ kakuho vaśāṁ anu piśaṅgarūpaḥ sadanāni gamyāḥ
children.translated_text: The ridges have gone down before you, following the cows; tawny in form, they go to their seats.

children.text: harī anyasya pīpayanta vājair mathrā rajāṃsy aśvinā vi ghoṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The bay horses of the other one swell with prizes; with their sounds, O <s>Aśvins</s>, they churn the realms.

children.text: pra vāṃ śaradvān vṛṣabho na niṣṣāṭ pūrvīr iṣaś carati madhva iṣṇan
children.translated_text: Your autumnal bull has gone forth like an unopposed one; seeking sweetness, he moves through many foods.

children.text: evair anyasya pīpayanta vājair veṣantīr ūrdhvā nadyo na āguḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus they swell another with prizes; the upward-rushing ones have come like rivers.

children.text: asarji vāṃ sthavirā vedhasā gīr bāﾱhe aśvinā tredhā kṣarantī
children.translated_text: Your ancient song, fashioned by the sage, has been released, O mighty <s>Aśvins</s>, flowing in three streams.

children.text: upastutāv avataṃ nādhamānaṃ yāmann ayāmañchṛṇutaṃ havam me ||
children.translated_text: Praised by us, help the supplicant; on each journey hear my call.

children.text: uta syā vāṃ ruśato vapsaso gīs tribarhiṣi sadasi pinvate nṝn
children.translated_text: And that shining song of fair form for you two swells men at the threefold sacred seat.

children.text: vṛṣā vām megho vṛṣaṇā pīpāya gor na seke manuṣo daśasyan ||
children.translated_text: The virile cloud has swollen for you, O virile ones, giving service to man like the cow's pouring.

children.text: yuvām pūṣevāśvinā purandhir agnim uṣāṃ na jarate haviṣmān
children.translated_text: The generous worshipper praises you two, O <s>Aśvins</s>, like <s>Pūṣan</s>, and tends the fire like the dawn with oblation,

children.text: huve yad vāṃ varivasyā gṛṇāno vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: when, singing, I call upon your gracious service. May we obtain nourishment, a secure dwelling, and life-giving bounty.

children.text: Chapter 182
abhūd idaṃ vayunam o ṣu bhūṣatā ratho vṛṣaṇvān madatā manīṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: This insight has arisen; adorn it now. Let the bull-rich chariot exhilarate the inspired thinkers.

children.text: dhiyañjinvā dhiṣṇyā viśpalāvasū divo napātā sukṛte śucivratā ||
children.translated_text: Inspirers of insight, skillful ones, possessing wealth for every settlement, sons of heaven, pure in vow for the doer of good.

children.text: indratamā hi dhiṣṇyā maruttamā dasrā daṃsiṣṭhā rathyā rathītamā
children.translated_text: For you are most like <s>Indra</s>, most like the <s>Maruts</s>, skillful, most wonder-working, chariot-borne, best of charioteers.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ rathaṃ vahethe madhva ācitaṃ tena dāśvāṃsam upa yātho aśvinā ||
children.translated_text: You carry a full chariot heaped with honey; with it you come near to the worshipper, O <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: kim atra dasrā kṛṇuthaḥ kim āsāthe jano yaḥ kaś cid ahavir mahīyate
children.translated_text: What are you doing here, O wonder-workers? Why are you sitting here, while any man without oblation is honored?

children.text: ati kramiṣṭaṃ juratam paṇer asuṃ jyotir viprāya kṛṇutaṃ vacasyave ||
children.translated_text: Step beyond him; wear away the life of the <s>Paṇi</s>; make light for the inspired singer who desires speech.

children.text: jambhayatam abhito rāyataḥ śuno hatam mṛdho vidathus tāny aśvinā
children.translated_text: Crush on every side the hound that barks for wealth; strike down the hostilities, for you know these things, O <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: vācaṃ vācaṃ jaritū ratninīṃ kṛtam ubhā śaṃsaṃ nāsatyāvatam mama ||
children.translated_text: Make each utterance of the singer rich in jewels; both of you, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, favor my praise.

children.text: yuvam etaṃ cakrathuḥ sindhuṣu plavam ātmanvantam pakṣiṇaṃ taugryāya kam
children.translated_text: You two made this vessel in the rivers for <s>Taugrya</s>, a living, winged ship.

children.text: yena devatrā manasā nirūhathuḥ supaptanī petathuḥ kṣodaso mahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With it you carried him out by godward thought; with good wings you flew from the great flood.

children.text: avaviddhaṃ taugryam apsv antar anārambhaṇe tamasi praviddham
children.translated_text: <s>Taugrya</s> had been hurled down among the waters, cast into supportless darkness.

children.text: catasro nāvo jaṭhalasya juṣṭā ud aśvibhyām iṣitāḥ pārayanti ||
children.translated_text: Four deep-bellied boats, welcomed and impelled by the <s>Aśvins</s>, carry him across.

children.text: kaḥ svid vṛkṣo niṣṭhito madhye arṇaso yaṃ taugryo nādhitaḥ paryaṣasvajat
children.translated_text: What tree was fixed in the midst of the flood, which <s>Taugrya</s>, abandoned, clasped all around?

children.text: parṇā mṛgasya pataror ivārabha ud aśvinā ūhathuḥ śromatāya kam ||
children.translated_text: Clinging to it as to the feathers of a flying bird, you two, O <s>Aśvins</s>, carried him up for renown.

children.text: tad vāṃ narā nāsatyāv anu ṣyād yad vām mānāsa ucatham avocan
children.translated_text: May that song of yours, O men, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, be continued, which inspired minds have spoken for you.

children.text: asmād adya sadasaḥ somyād ā vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: From this soma-seat today may we obtain nourishment, a strong settlement, and life-giving bounty.

children.text: Chapter 183
taṃ yuñjāthām manaso yo javīyān trivandhuro vṛṣaṇā yas tricakraḥ
children.translated_text: Yoke that chariot, swifter than the mind, three-seated, O virile ones, and three-wheeled.

children.text: yenopayāthaḥ sukṛto duroṇaṃ tridhātunā patatho vir na parṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With it you approach the homes of the pious; with its triple frame you fly like birds with wings.

children.text: suvṛd ratho vartate yann abhi kṣāṃ yat tiṣṭhathaḥ kratumantānu pṛkṣe
children.translated_text: The well-turning chariot rolls when it goes over the earth, and when you two, full of purpose, stand amid the contests.

children.text: vapur vapuṣyā sacatām iyaṃ gīr divo duhitroṣasā sacethe ||
children.translated_text: May this song attend your beautiful forms; you accompany <s>Uṣas</s>, the daughter of heaven.

children.text: ā tiṣṭhataṃ suvṛtaṃ yo ratho vām anu vratāni vartate haviṣmān
children.translated_text: Mount your well-turning chariot, which follows the sacred ordinances and is rich in oblation.

children.text: yena narā nāsatyeṣayadhyai vartir yāthas tanayāya tmane ca ||
children.translated_text: By it, O men, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, you go on your course for refreshment, for offspring, and for yourselves.

children.text: mā vāṃ vṛko mā vṛkīr ā dadharṣīn mā pari varktam uta māti dhaktam
children.translated_text: Let no wolf and no she-wolf assail you; do not turn away from us, and do not burn past us.

children.text: ayaṃ vām bhāgo nihita iyaṃ gīr dasrāv ime vāṃ nidhayo madhūnām ||
children.translated_text: This share is set down for you, this song; O wonder-workers, these are your stores of honey.

children.text: yuvāṃ gotamaḥ purumīﾱho atrir dasrā havate 'vase haviṣmān
children.translated_text: <s>Gotama</s>, <s>Purumīḷha</s>, and <s>Atri</s> call you two for help, O wonder-workers, with oblation.

children.text: diśaṃ na diṣṭām ṛjūyeva yantā me havaṃ nāsatyopa yātam ||
children.translated_text: Like a traveller going straight toward an appointed direction, come near to my call, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>.

children.text: atāriṣma tamasas pāram asya prati vāṃ stomo aśvināv adhāyi
children.translated_text: We have crossed to the far shore of this darkness; the hymn has been set before you, O <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: eha yātam pathibhir devayānair vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: Come here by paths that lead to the gods; may we obtain nourishment, a strong settlement, and life-giving bounty.

children.text: Chapter 184
tā vām adya tāv aparaṃ huvemocchantyām uṣasi vahnir ukthaiḥ
children.translated_text: You two today, and you two hereafter, we would call at the brightening dawn with hymns, as the bearer calls.

children.text: nāsatyā kuha cit santāv aryo divo napātā sudāstarāya ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, wherever you may be, noble sons of heaven, come for the very generous worshipper.

children.text: asme ū ṣu vṛṣaṇā mādayethām ut paṇīṃr hatam ūrmyā madantā
children.translated_text: Among us, O virile ones, make yourselves glad; strike down the <s>Paṇis</s>, rejoicing amid the waves.

children.text: śrutam me acchoktibhir matīnām eṣṭā narā nicetārā ca karṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hear me through the directed utterances of my thoughts, O sought-for men, discerning also with your ears.

children.text: śriye pūṣann iṣukṛteva devā nāsatyā vahatuṃ sūryāyāḥ
children.translated_text: For splendor, O <s>Pūṣan</s>, fashion it like an arrow-maker; O divine <s>Nāsatyas</s>, attend the bridal procession of <s>Sūryā</s>.

children.text: vacyante vāṃ kakuhā apsu jātā yugā jūrṇeva varuṇasya bhūreḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your peaks, born in the waters, are proclaimed, like the worn yokes of great <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: asme sā vām mādhvī rātir astu stomaṃ hinotam mānyasya kāroḥ
children.translated_text: May that honeyed gift of yours be ours; impel the hymn of the venerable singer.

children.text: anu yad vāṃ śravasyā sudānū suvīryāya carṣaṇayo madanti ||
children.translated_text: When the peoples, longing for your fame, O good givers, rejoice for heroic strength.

children.text: eṣa vāṃ stomo aśvināv akāri mānebhir maghavānā suvṛkti
children.translated_text: This hymn has been made for you, O <s>Aśvins</s>, with reverent thoughts, O bountiful ones, with good praise.

children.text: yātaṃ vartis tanayāya tmane cāgastye nāsatyā madantā ||
children.translated_text: Come on your course for offspring and for yourselves; rejoice with <s>Agastya</s>, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>.

children.text: atāriṣma tamasas pāram asya prati vāṃ stomo aśvināv adhāyi
children.translated_text: We have crossed to the far shore of this darkness; the hymn has been set before you, O <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: eha yātam pathibhir devayānair vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ||
children.translated_text: Come here by paths that lead to the gods; may we obtain nourishment, a strong settlement, and life-giving bounty.

children.text: Chapter 185
katarā pūrvā katarāparāyoḥ kathā jāte kavayaḥ ko vi veda
children.translated_text: Which of these two was first, which later? How were they born, O poets? Who knows?

children.text: viśvaṃ tmanā bibhṛto yaddha nāma vi vartete ahanī cakriyeva ||
children.translated_text: They bear by themselves everything that has a name; the two days turn apart like wheels.

children.text: bhūriṃ dve acarantī carantam padvantaṃ garbham apadī dadhāte
children.translated_text: The two abundant ones move, bearing what moves; the footed one holds the footless embryo.

children.text: nityaṃ na sūnum pitror upasthe dyāvā rakṣatam pṛthivī no abhvāt ||
children.translated_text: Like an everlasting son in the lap of his parents, O <s>Dyāvā</s> and <s>Pṛthivī</s>, protect us from misfortune.

children.text: aneho dātram aditer anarvaṃ huve svarvad avadhaṃ namasvat
children.translated_text: With reverence I call on the faultless, unharmed, sun-winning gift of <s>Aditi</s>, a sheltering aid.

children.text: tad rodasī janayataṃ jaritre dyāvā rakṣatam pṛthivī no abhvāt ||
children.translated_text: Generate that for the singer, O two worlds; O <s>Dyāvā</s> and <s>Pṛthivī</s>, protect us from misfortune.

children.text: atapyamāne avasāvantī anu ṣyāma rodasī devaputre
children.translated_text: May we follow after your protection, O two worlds, rich in help and never scorching, children of the gods.

children.text: ubhe devānām ubhayebhir ahnāṃ dyāvā rakṣatam pṛthivī no abhvāt ||
children.translated_text: Both of you, with both day and night among the gods, O <s>Dyāvā</s> and <s>Pṛthivī</s>, protect us from misfortune.

children.text: saṃgacchamāne yuvatī samante svasārā jāmī pitror upasthe
children.translated_text: Coming together, young and equal, two sisters, close kin in the lap of their parents,

children.text: abhijighrantī bhuvanasya nābhiṃ dyāvā rakṣatam pṛthivī no abhvāt ||
children.translated_text: touching the navel of the world, O <s>Dyāvā</s> and <s>Pṛthivī</s>, protect us from misfortune.

children.text: urvī sadmanī bṛhatī ṛtena huve devānām avasā janitrī
children.translated_text: Wide are your seats, broad through <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order); I call the two mothers of the gods for help.

children.text: dadhāte ye amṛtaṃ supratīke dyāvā rakṣatam pṛthivī no abhvāt ||
