children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, today may we prosper by your aids, with praises, toward that heart-touching good resolve, like toward a horse,

children.text: ṛdhyāmā ta ohaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and toward that kindly purpose.

children.text: adhā hy agne krator bhadrasya dakṣasya sādhoḥ
children.translated_text: For then, O <s>Agni</s>, you became the charioteer

children.text: rathīr ṛtasya bṛhato babhūtha ||
children.translated_text: of good resolve, skill, goodness, and the great <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order).

children.text: ebhir no arkair bhavā no arvāṅ svar ṇa jyotiḥ
children.translated_text: With these hymns be turned toward us; be for us like the heavenly light,

children.text: agne viśvebhiḥ sumanā anīkaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, kindly with all your faces.

children.text: ābhiṣ ṭe adya gīrbhir gṛṇanto 'gne dāśema
children.translated_text: Praising you today with these songs, O <s>Agni</s>, may we serve you;

children.text: pra te divo na stanayanti śuṣmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: your powers thunder forth like those of heaven.

children.text: tava svādiṣṭhāgne saṃdṛṣṭir idā cid ahna idā cid aktoḥ
children.translated_text: Your sweetest appearance, O <s>Agni</s>, by day and also by night,

children.text: śriye rukmo na rocata upāke ||
children.translated_text: shines nearby for beauty like a golden ornament.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ na pūtaṃ tanūr arepāḥ śuci hiraṇyam
children.translated_text: Like purified ghee, your body is stainless; pure gold,

children.text: tat te rukmo na rocata svadhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that ornament of yours shines, O self-powered one.

children.text: kṛtaṃ ciddhi ṣmā sanemi dveṣo 'gna inoṣi martāt
children.translated_text: For even settled hatred, O <s>Agni</s>, you drive away from the mortal,

children.text: itthā yajamānād ṛtāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thus from the sacrificer, O keeper of <s>ṛta</s>.

children.text: śivā naḥ sakhyā santu bhrātrāgne deveṣu yuṣme
children.translated_text: May our friendships be gracious, and our brotherhood, O <s>Agni</s>, among you gods;

children.text: sā no nābhiḥ sadane sasminn ūdhan ||
children.translated_text: may that bond of ours be in the same seat and udder.

children.text: Chapter 307
bhadraṃ te agne sahasinn anīkam upāka ā rocate sūryasya
children.translated_text: Fair is your face, O mighty <s>Agni</s>; near at hand it shines with the sun's light,

children.text: ruśad dṛśe dadṛśe naktayā cid arūkṣitaṃ dṛśa ā rūpe annam ||
children.translated_text: bright to behold, seen even by night, not roughened, food in visible form.

children.text: vi ṣāhy agne gṛṇate manīṣāṃ khaṃ vepasā tuvijāta stavānaḥ
children.translated_text: Send forth, O <s>Agni</s>, inspired thought for the singer; loudly, with trembling force, be praised, O strongly born one,

children.text: viśvebhir yad vāvanaḥ śukra devais tan no rāsva sumaho bhūri manma ||
children.translated_text: when, bright one, you are desired with all the gods; grant us that, great and abundant thought.

children.text: tvad agne kāvyā tvan manīṣās tvad ukthā jāyante rādhyāni
children.translated_text: From you, O <s>Agni</s>, poetic inspirations, from you thoughts, from you hymns and successes are born;

children.text: tvad eti draviṇaṃ vīrapeśā itthādhiye dāśuṣe martyāya ||
children.translated_text: from you comes wealth adorned with heroes to the mortal worshipper of such understanding.

children.text: tvad vājī vājambharo vihāyā abhiṣṭikṛj jāyate satyaśuṣmaḥ
children.translated_text: From you the prize-winning steed, prize-bearing, far-ranging, victory-making, true in force, is born;

children.text: tvad rayir devajūto mayobhus tvad āśur jūjuvāṁ agne arvā ||
children.translated_text: from you comes wealth, urged by the gods and bringing happiness; from you, O <s>Agni</s>, the swift racing horse.

children.text: tvām agne prathamaṃ devayanto devam martā amṛta mandrajihvam
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Agni</s>, first god, the mortals who seek the gods worship, O immortal one with delightful tongue,

children.text: dveṣoyutam ā vivāsanti dhībhir damūnasaṃ gṛhapatim amūram ||
children.translated_text: with their thoughts, you who are free from hatred, lord of the house, dwelling in the home, unconfused.

children.text: āre asmad amatim āre aṃha āre viśvāṃ durmatiṃ yan nipāsi
children.translated_text: Far from us keep folly, far distress, far every evil thought, when you guard us;

children.text: doṣā śivaḥ sahasaḥ sūno agne yaṃ deva ā cit sacase svasti ||
children.translated_text: by night, auspicious son of strength, O <s>Agni</s>, whom even a god accompanies for well-being.

children.text: Chapter 308
yas tvām agna inadhate yatasruk tris te annaṃ kṛṇavat sasminn ahan
children.translated_text: Whoever kindles you, O <s>Agni</s>, with ladle extended, and three times in the same day prepares your food,

children.text: sa su dyumnair abhy astu prasakṣat tava kratvā jātavedaś cikitvān ||
children.translated_text: may he, discerning <s>Jātavedas</s>, prevail with splendors through your resolve.

children.text: idhmaṃ yas te jabharac chaśramāṇo maho agne anīkam ā saparyan
children.translated_text: Whoever, laboring, has brought your fuel, serving your great face, O <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: sa idhānaḥ prati doṣām uṣāsam puṣyan rayiṃ sacate ghnann amitrān ||
children.translated_text: he, kindled, from night to dawn, obtains growing wealth, slaying enemies.

children.text: agnir īśe bṛhataḥ kṣatriyasyāgnir vājasya paramasya rāyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> rules over great sovereignty; <s>Agni</s> rules over prize and highest wealth;

children.text: dadhāti ratnaṃ vidhate yaviṣṭho vy ānuṣaṅ martyāya svadhāvān ||
children.translated_text: the youngest, self-powered one bestows treasure on the worshipper, and continuously on the mortal.

children.text: yac cid dhi te puruṣatrā yaviṣṭhācittibhiś cakṛmā kac cid āgaḥ
children.translated_text: If, O youngest one, in many human ways we have committed any offense against you through lack of understanding,

children.text: kṛdhī ṣv asmāṁ aditer anāgān vy enāṃsi śiśratho viṣvag agne ||
children.translated_text: make us guiltless before <s>Aditi</s>; loosen our sins on every side, O <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: mahaś cid agna enaso abhīka ūrvād devānām uta martyānām
children.translated_text: Even from great guilt, O <s>Agni</s>, near at hand, from the wide guilt of gods and mortals,

children.text: mā te sakhāyaḥ sadam id riṣāma yacchā tokāya tanayāya śaṃ yoḥ ||
children.translated_text: may we, your friends, never suffer; grant welfare and blessing to our offspring and descendants.

children.text: yathā ha tyad vasavo gauryaṃ cit padi ṣitām amuñcatā yajatrāḥ
children.translated_text: As, O <s>Vasus</s>, you released even the cow <s>Gaurī</s> when she was bound by the foot, O worshipful ones,

children.text: evo ṣv asman muñcatā vy aṃhaḥ pra tāry agne prataraṃ na āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: so now release us from distress; extend our lifetime farther onward, O <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: Chapter 309
praty agnir uṣasām agram akhyad vibhātīnāṃ sumanā ratnadheyam
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, gracious and treasure-giving, has looked forth at the forefront of the shining dawns;

children.text: yātam aśvinā sukṛto duroṇam ut sūryo jyotiṣā deva eti ||
children.translated_text: come, O <s>Aśvins</s>, to the well-made dwelling, and the god <s>Sūrya</s> rises with light.

children.text: ūrdhvam bhānuṃ savitā devo aśred drapsaṃ davidhvad gaviṣo na satvā
children.translated_text: The god <s>Savitṛ</s> has raised his beam upward, the gleaming drop, shaking, like a warrior seeking cattle;

children.text: anu vrataṃ varuṇo yanti mitro yat sūryaṃ divy ārohayanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Mitra</s> follow the ordinance, when they make <s>Sūrya</s> ascend in heaven.

children.text: yaṃ sīm akṛṇvan tamase vipṛce dhruvakṣemā anavasyanto artham
children.translated_text: They made him to scatter darkness, for a firm and secure aim, unfailing in purpose;

children.text: taṃ sūryaṃ haritaḥ sapta yahvī spaśaṃ viśvasya jagato vahanti ||
children.translated_text: seven bay mares carry that mighty <s>Sūrya</s>, the watcher of the whole moving world.

children.text: vahiṣṭhebhir viharan yāsi tantum avavyayann asitaṃ deva vasma
children.translated_text: Moving with the best bearers, you go along the thread, unwinding the black garment, O god;

children.text: davidhvato raśmayaḥ sūryasya carmevāvādhus tamo apsv antaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the quivering rays of <s>Sūrya</s> have driven the darkness down into the waters like a hide.

children.text: anāyato anibaddhaḥ kathāyaṃ nyaṅṅ uttāno 'va padyate na
children.translated_text: Unstretched, unbound, how does this one, downward yet supine, not fall?

children.text: kayā yāti svadhayā ko dadarśa diva skambhaḥ samṛtaḥ pāti nākam ||
children.translated_text: By what self-power does he move? Who has seen it? The pillar of heaven, fixed together, guards the vault.

children.text: Chapter 310
praty agnir uṣaso jātavedā akhyad devo rocamānā mahobhiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> <s>Jātavedas</s>, the god shining with powers, has looked forth toward the dawns;

children.text: ā nāsatyorugāyā rathenemaṃ yajñam upa no yātam accha ||
children.translated_text: O wide-praised <s>Nāsatyas</s>, come to this sacrifice of ours with your chariot.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ ketuṃ savitā devo aśrej jyotir viśvasmai bhuvanāya kṛṇvan
children.translated_text: The god <s>Savitṛ</s> has raised the high banner, making light for the whole world;

children.text: āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antarikṣaṃ vi sūryo raśmibhiś cekitānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūrya</s>, discerning, has filled heaven, earth, and midspace with his rays.

children.text: āvahanty aruṇīr jyotiṣāgān mahī citrā raśmibhiś cekitānā
children.translated_text: The ruddy ones, bearing light, have come; the great radiant one is seen clearly with her rays,

children.text: prabodhayantī suvitāya devy uṣā īyate suyujā rathena ||
children.translated_text: awakening beings for good fortune; the goddess <s>Uṣas</s> goes with her well-yoked chariot.

children.text: ā vāṃ vahiṣṭhā iha te vahantu rathā aśvāsa uṣaso vyuṣṭau
children.translated_text: May your best bearers, the chariot-horses, bring you two here at the shining of dawn;

children.text: ime hi vām madhupeyāya somā asmin yajñe vṛṣaṇā mādayethām ||
children.translated_text: for these <s>soma</s> draughts are for you two to drink sweetness; rejoice at this sacrifice, O bulls.

children.text: anāyato anibaddhaḥ kathāyaṃ nyaṅṅ uttāno 'va padyate na
children.translated_text: Unstretched, unbound, how does this one, downward yet supine, not fall?

children.text: kayā yāti svadhayā ko dadarśa diva skambhaḥ samṛtaḥ pāti nākam ||
children.translated_text: By what self-power does he move? Who has seen it? The pillar of heaven, fixed together, guards the vault.

children.text: Chapter 311
agnir hotā no adhvare vājī san pari ṇīyate
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) at our sacrifice, being a prize-winning power, is led around.

children.text: devo deveṣu yajñiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is the god worshipful among the gods.

children.text: pari triviṣṭy adhvaraṃ yāty agnī rathīr iva
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> goes around the threefold sacrifice like a charioteer.

children.text: ā deveṣu prayo dadhat ||
children.translated_text: He sets delight among the gods.

children.text: pari vājapatiḥ kavir agnir havyāny akramīt
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, lord of prizes and seer, has gone around the oblations.

children.text: dadhad ratnāni dāśuṣe ||
children.translated_text: He sets treasures in place for the worshipper.

children.text: ayaṃ yaḥ sṛñjaye puro daivavāte samidhyate
children.translated_text: This is the one who is kindled before <s>Sṛñjaya Daivavāta</s>.

children.text: dyumāṁ amitradambhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is brilliant, a subduer of enemies.

children.text: asya ghā vīra īvato 'gner īśīta martyaḥ
children.translated_text: A mortal hero may indeed gain command of this vigorous <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: tigmajambhasya mīﾱhuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sharp-jawed and bountiful.

children.text: tam arvantaṃ na sānasim aruṣaṃ na divaḥ śiśum
children.translated_text: They polish him day after day like a victorious horse, like the ruddy child of heaven.

children.text: marmṛjyante dive dive ||
children.translated_text: They make him bright every day.

children.text: bodhad yan mā haribhyāṃ kumāraḥ sāhadevyaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Kumāra Sāhadevya</s> roused me for the two bay horses,

children.text: acchā na hūta ud aram ||
children.translated_text: I rose up as one called toward them.

children.text: uta tyā yajatā harī kumārāt sāhadevyāt
children.translated_text: And those two worshipful bay horses from <s>Kumāra Sāhadevya</s>,

children.text: prayatā sadya ā dade ||
children.translated_text: duly presented, I accepted at once.

children.text: eṣa vāṃ devāv aśvinā kumāraḥ sāhadevyaḥ
children.translated_text: O divine <s>Aśvins</s>, this <s>Kumāra Sāhadevya</s>,

children.text: dīrghāyur astu somakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Somaka</s>, may he be long-lived.

children.text: taṃ yuvaṃ devāv aśvinā kumāraṃ sāhadevyam
children.translated_text: O divine <s>Aśvins</s>, you two should make that <s>Kumāra Sāhadevya</s>

children.text: dīrghāyuṣaṃ kṛṇotana ||
children.translated_text: long-lived.

children.text: Chapter 312
ā satyo yātu maghavāṁ ṛjīṣī dravantv asya haraya upa naḥ
children.translated_text: Let the true, bounteous, soma-rich one come; let his bay horses run here to us.

children.text: tasmā id andhaḥ suṣumā sudakṣam ihābhipitvaṃ karate gṛṇānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For him indeed we have pressed the well-prepared Soma; being praised, let him make this a place for drinking.

children.text: ava sya śūrādhvano nānte 'smin no adya savane mandadhyai
children.translated_text: Come down, O hero, from your road; at this pressing today be gladdened for us.

children.text: śaṃsāty uktham uśaneva vedhāś cikituṣe asuryāya manma ||
children.translated_text: Like <s>Uśanas</s>, the wise fashioner proclaims the hymn, the thought for the discerning lordly one.

children.text: kavir na niṇyaṃ vidathāni sādhan vṛṣā yat sekaṃ vipipāno arcāt
children.translated_text: Like a seer accomplishing hidden rites, the bull sang when he drank the draught.

children.text: diva itthā jījanat sapta kārūn ahnā cic cakrur vayunā gṛṇantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus from heaven he generated the seven singers; even by day, praising, they made insights.

children.text: svar yad vedi sudṛśīkam arkair mahi jyotī rurucur yad dha vastoḥ
children.translated_text: When he found the fair-seen sun through hymns, great lights shone when it was day.

children.text: andhā tamāṃsi dudhitā vicakṣe nṛbhyaś cakāra nṛtamo abhiṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: He opened the blind, oppressive darknesses to sight; the most manly one made vision for men in his aid.

children.text: vavakṣa indro amitam ṛjīṣy ubhe ā paprau rodasī mahitvā
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, soma-rich, has grown beyond measure; with his greatness he filled both worlds.

children.text: ataś cid asya mahimā vi recy abhi yo viśvā bhuvanā babhūva ||
children.translated_text: From there his greatness extends still farther, he who became greater than all beings.

children.text: viśvāni śakro naryāṇi vidvān apo rireca sakhibhir nikāmaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, knowing all manly deeds, released the waters with his willing friends.

children.text: aśmānaṃ cid ye bibhidur vacobhir vrajaṃ gomantam uśijo vi vavruḥ ||
children.translated_text: They split even the stone with their words; the <s>Uśijs</s> opened the cattle-filled enclosure.

children.text: apo vṛtraṃ vavrivāṃsam parāhan prāvat te vajram pṛthivī sacetāḥ
children.translated_text: You struck down <s>Vṛtra</s>, who had enclosed the waters; the conscious earth aided your thunderbolt.

children.text: prārṇāṃsi samudriyāṇy ainoḥ patir bhavañchavasā śūra dhṛṣṇo ||
children.translated_text: You drove forth the oceanic floods; by your might, O bold hero, become their lord.

children.text: apo yad adrim puruhūta dardar āvir bhuvat saramā pūrvyaṃ te
children.translated_text: When, O much-invoked one, you split the mountain of the waters, your ancient <s>Saramā</s> came into view.

children.text: sa no netā vājam ā darṣi bhūriṃ gotrā rujann aṅgirobhir gṛṇānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Be our leader; breaking open cattle-stalls with the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, reveal abundant prize to us as you are praised.

children.text: acchā kaviṃ nṛmaṇo gā abhiṣṭau svarṣātā maghavan nādhamānam
children.translated_text: Come to the poet, O man-minded <s>Maghavan</s>, for help with the cows, as he seeks the winning of the sun.

children.text: ūtibhis tam iṣaṇo dyumnahūtau ni māyāvān abrahmā dasyur arta ||
children.translated_text: With aids, impelling him at the call for splendor, the illusion-working, prayerless <s>Dasyu</s> sank down.

children.text: ā dasyughnā manasā yāhy astam bhuvat te kutsaḥ sakhye nikāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Come home with a mind that slays the <s>Dasyu</s>; <s>Kutsa</s> became your desired companion in friendship.

children.text: sve yonau ni ṣadataṃ sarūpā vi vāṃ cikitsad ṛtacid dha nārī ||
children.translated_text: In your own seat the two of you, alike in form, sat down; the woman, knowing truth, discerned you both.

children.text: yāsi kutsena saratham avasyus todo vātasya haryor īśānaḥ
children.translated_text: You go with <s>Kutsa</s> on the same chariot, seeking aid, lord of the bay horses swift as wind.

children.text: ṛjrā vājaṃ na gadhyaṃ yuyūṣan kavir yad ahan pāryāya bhūṣāt ||
children.translated_text: Eager to win the straight prize, hard to seize, the seer adorned himself when he would strike for the crossing.

children.text: kutsāya śuṣṇam aśuṣaṃ ni barhīḥ prapitve ahnaḥ kuyavaṃ sahasrā
children.translated_text: For <s>Kutsa</s> you cut down <s>Śuṣṇa</s>, the parched one; at the day's advance you struck <s>Kuyava</s> by thousands.

children.text: sadyo dasyūn pra mṛṇa kutsyena pra sūraś cakraṃ vṛhatād abhīke ||
children.translated_text: At once with <s>Kutsa</s> you crushed the <s>Dasyus</s>; in the conflict you made the sun's wheel roll forth.

children.text: tvam piprum mṛgayaṃ śūśuvāṃsam ṛjiśvane vaidathināya randhīḥ
children.translated_text: You subdued <s>Pipru</s>, the swelling wild foe, for <s>Ṛjiśvan Vaidathina</s>.

children.text: pañcāśat kṛṣṇā ni vapaḥ sahasrātkaṃ na puro jarimā vi dardaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You cast down fifty thousand dark ones; like old age tearing a garment, you broke the strongholds apart.

children.text: sūra upāke tanvaṃ dadhāno vi yat te cety amṛtasya varpaḥ
children.translated_text: When the sun, setting his body nearby, makes your immortal form visible,

children.text: mṛgo na hastī taviṣīm uṣāṇaḥ siṃho na bhīma āyudhāni bibhrat ||
children.translated_text: you are like a wild beast, like an elephant eager for strength, like a terrifying lion bearing weapons.

children.text: indraṃ kāmā vasūyanto agman svarmīﾱhe na savane cakānāḥ
children.translated_text: Those desiring wealth have come to <s>Indra</s>, delighting in the heaven-winning Soma-pressing.

children.text: śravasyavaḥ śaśamānāsa ukthair oko na raṇvā sudṛśīva puṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeking fame and praising with hymns, they come as to a pleasant home, as to fair-seen nourishment.

children.text: tam id va indraṃ suhavaṃ huvema yas tā cakāra naryā purūṇi
children.translated_text: Let us call that easily invoked <s>Indra</s>, who performed those many manly deeds,

children.text: yo māvate jaritre gadhyaṃ cin makṣū vājam bharati spārharādhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who swiftly brings even a hard-won prize to a singer like me, rich in desirable gifts.

children.text: tigmā yad antar aśaniḥ patāti kasmiñ cic chūra muhuke janānām
children.translated_text: When the sharp thunderbolt flies among the peoples at some sudden moment, O hero,

children.text: ghorā yad arya samṛtir bhavāty adha smā nas tanvo bodhi gopāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when, O noble one, the terrible clash of men arises, then be guardian of our bodies.

children.text: bhuvo 'vitā vāmadevasya dhīnām bhuvaḥ sakhāvṛko vājasātau
children.translated_text: You have been protector of <s>Vāmadeva</s>'s inspired thoughts; you have been a harmless friend in the winning of prizes.

children.text: tvām anu pramatim ā jaganmoruśaṃso jaritre viśvadha syāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Following your wise care, may we come to broad praise; be present everywhere for the singer.

children.text: ebhir nṛbhir indra tvāyubhiṣ ṭvā maghavadbhir maghavan viśva ājau
children.translated_text: With these men who long for you, with bounteous men, O bounteous <s>Indra</s>, in every contest,

children.text: dyāvo na dyumnair abhi santo aryaḥ kṣapo madema śaradaś ca pūrvīḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded with splendors like the heavens, may we rejoice through nights and many autumns, O noble one.

children.text: eved indrāya vṛṣabhāya vṛṣṇe brahmākarma bhṛgavo na ratham
children.translated_text: Thus for <s>Indra</s>, the bull, the virile one, we have made a prayer, as the <s>Bhṛgus</s> made a chariot.

children.text: nū cid yathā naḥ sakhyā viyoṣad asan na ugro 'vitā tanūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now may he not separate us from his friendship; may the mighty one be our protector, guardian of the body.

children.text: nū ṣṭuta indra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo na pīpeḥ
children.translated_text: Now praised, O <s>Indra</s>, now being sung, swell nourishment for the singer like rivers.

children.text: akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A new prayer has been made for you, O lord of bay horses; through insight may we always be fit for the chariot.

children.text: Chapter 313
tvam mahāṁ indra tubhyaṃ ha kṣā anu kṣatram maṃhanā manyata dyauḥ
children.translated_text: You are great, O <s>Indra</s>; for you, by your greatness, earth and heaven acknowledge sovereign power.

children.text: tvaṃ vṛtraṃ śavasā jaghanvān sṛjaḥ sindhūṃr ahinā jagrasānān ||
children.translated_text: You, having slain <s>Vṛtra</s> with might, released the rivers swallowed by the serpent.

children.text: tava tviṣo janiman rejata dyau rejad bhūmir bhiyasā svasya manyoḥ
children.translated_text: At your birth heaven shook from your force; earth shook from fear of your own wrath.

children.text: ṛghāyanta subhvaḥ parvatāsa ārdan dhanvāni sarayanta āpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The well-founded mountains trembled and split; the dry lands flowed, and the waters streamed.

children.text: bhinad giriṃ śavasā vajram iṣṇann āviṣkṛṇvānaḥ sahasāna ojaḥ
children.translated_text: He split the mountain with might, hurling the thunderbolt, making his overpowering strength manifest.

children.text: vadhīd vṛtraṃ vajreṇa mandasānaḥ sarann āpo javasā hatavṛṣṇīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Exhilarated, he slew <s>Vṛtra</s> with the thunderbolt; the waters rushed swiftly, their bull struck down.

children.text: suvīras te janitā manyata dyaur indrasya kartā svapastamo bhūt
children.translated_text: Heaven, your begetter, thought himself rich in heroes; the maker of <s>Indra</s> became most skillful in work.

children.text: ya īṃ jajāna svaryaṃ suvajram anapacyutaṃ sadaso na bhūma ||
children.translated_text: He who begot this sun-winning one, bearing a good thunderbolt, made him unshaken, like the earth from its seat.

children.text: ya eka ic cyāvayati pra bhūmā rājā kṛṣṭīnām puruhūta indraḥ
children.translated_text: He alone sets the broad realms in motion, <s>Indra</s>, the much-invoked king of the peoples.

children.text: satyam enam anu viśve madanti rātiṃ devasya gṛṇato maghonaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All the peoples truly rejoice in him, in the gift of the god, the bountiful one, when he is praised.

children.text: satrā somā abhavann asya viśve satrā madāso bṛhato madiṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: All soma-draughts became his at once; all exhilarations, most intoxicating, belonged to the great one.

children.text: satrābhavo vasupatir vasūnāṃ datre viśvā adhithā indra kṛṣṭīḥ ||
children.translated_text: At once you became lord of goods, lord of riches; for the giver, O <s>Indra</s>, you took charge of all peoples.

children.text: tvam adha prathamaṃ jāyamāno 'me viśvā adhithā indra kṛṣṭīḥ
children.translated_text: Then, being born first, you took charge of all peoples, O <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tvam prati pravata āśayānam ahiṃ vajreṇa maghavan vi vṛścaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You, O bountiful one, split apart with the thunderbolt the serpent lying across the slopes.

children.text: satrāhaṇaṃ dādhṛṣiṃ tumram indram mahām apāraṃ vṛṣabhaṃ suvajram
children.translated_text: The true smiter, the bold, mighty <s>Indra</s>, great, boundless, a bull with the good thunderbolt,

children.text: hantā yo vṛtraṃ sanitota vājaṃ dātā maghāni maghavā surādhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he who slew <s>Vṛtra</s>, winner of the prize, giver of bounties, the generous <s>Maghavan</s>, rich in good gifts.

children.text: ayaṃ vṛtaś cātayate samīcīr ya ājiṣu maghavā śṛṇva ekaḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>Maghavan</s>, who alone hears in battles, drives together the streams that move in one course.

children.text: ayaṃ vājam bharati yaṃ sanoty asya priyāsaḥ sakhye syāma ||
children.translated_text: This one brings the prize that he wins; may we be dear to him in friendship.

children.text: ayaṃ śṛṇve adha jayann uta ghnann ayam uta pra kṛṇute yudhā gāḥ
children.translated_text: This one is heard of as conquering and slaying; this one wins cows in battle.

children.text: yadā satyaṃ kṛṇute manyum indro viśvaṃ dṛﾱham bhayata ejad asmāt ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Indra</s> makes his fury true, every firm thing fears and trembles before him.

children.text: sam indro gā ajayat saṃ hiraṇyā sam aśviyā maghavā yo ha pūrvīḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> won the cows together, the gold together, and the horses together; <s>Maghavan</s> won the many possessions of old.

children.text: ebhir nṛbhir nṛtamo asya śākai rāyo vibhaktā sambharaś ca vasvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With these men, through his powers, the most manly one is the distributor of wealth and the gatherer of goods.

children.text: kiyat svid indro adhy eti mātuḥ kiyat pitur janitur yo jajāna
children.translated_text: How far does <s>Indra</s> go beyond his mother? How far beyond the father, the begetter who begot him?

children.text: yo asya śuṣmam muhukair iyarti vāto na jūta stanayadbhir abhraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He repeatedly sets his force in motion, like wind-driven clouds that thunder.

children.text: kṣiyantaṃ tvam akṣiyantaṃ kṛṇotīyarti reṇum maghavā samoham
children.translated_text: You make the settled man unsettled; <s>Maghavan</s> raises dust and confusion.

children.text: vibhañjanur aśanimāṁ iva dyaur uta stotāram maghavā vasau dhāt ||
children.translated_text: Breaking things apart like heaven armed with lightning, <s>Maghavan</s> also sets the singer in wealth.

children.text: ayaṃ cakram iṣaṇat sūryasya ny etaśaṃ rīramat sasṛmāṇam
children.translated_text: This one set the wheel of the Sun in motion; he checked <s>Etaśa</s> as he sped onward.

children.text: ā kṛṣṇa īṃ juhurāṇo jigharti tvaco budhne rajaso asya yonau ||
children.translated_text: The dark one, bending toward him, swallows him at the bottom of the skin, in the womb of this midspace.

children.text: asiknyāṃ yajamāno na hotā ||
children.translated_text: In the dark one he is like a sacrificer, like a <s>hotṛ</s> (invoking priest).

children.text: gavyanta indraṃ sakhyāya viprā aśvāyanto vṛṣaṇaṃ vājayantaḥ
children.translated_text: The inspired poets, desiring cows, desiring horses, and seeking the prize, call <s>Indra</s>, the bull, for friendship.

children.text: janīyanto janidām akṣitotim ā cyāvayāmo 'vate na kośam ||
children.translated_text: Desiring offspring, they call the giver of offspring and unfailing aid; we draw him down as one draws a bucket into a well.

children.text: trātā no bodhi dadṛśāna āpir abhikhyātā marḍitā somyānām
children.translated_text: Be our protector, our visible ally, our overseer, merciful to the soma-pressers.

children.text: sakhā pitā pitṛtamaḥ pitṝṇāṃ kartem u lokam uśate vayodhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Be friend, father, and most fatherly of fathers, the maker of room for the one who longs, the giver of life.

children.text: sakhīyatām avitā bodhi sakhā gṛṇāna indra stuvate vayo dhāḥ
children.translated_text: When friendship is sought, be a protecting friend; praised, O <s>Indra</s>, give vigor to the worshipper.

children.text: vayaṃ hy ā te cakṛmā sabādha ābhiḥ śamībhir mahayanta indra ||
children.translated_text: For we have made you close to us, O <s>Indra</s>, with these aids in our constraint, magnifying you.

children.text: stuta indro maghavā yaddha vṛtrā bhūrīṇy eko apratīni hanti
children.translated_text: Praised, <s>Indra</s> the bountiful, when he strikes the <s>Vṛtras</s>, alone slays many irresistible foes.

children.text: asya priyo jaritā yasya śarman nakir devā vārayante na martāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dear to him is the singer in whose shelter neither gods nor mortals can hinder him.

children.text: evā na indro maghavā virapśī karat satyā carṣaṇīdhṛd anarvā
children.translated_text: Thus may <s>Indra</s>, bountiful and abundant, supporter of peoples, irresistible, make true things for us.

children.text: tvaṃ rājā januṣāṃ dhehy asme adhi śravo māhinaṃ yaj jaritre ||
children.translated_text: You, king of living beings by birth, place in us high renown and greatness for the singer.

children.text: nū ṣṭuta indra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo na pīpeḥ
children.translated_text: Now praised, now being sung, O <s>Indra</s>, fill the singer with refreshment as rivers fill their banks.

children.text: akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A new prayer has been made for you, O bay-horsed one; through inspired thought may we be your chariot-companions always.

children.text: Chapter 314
ayam panthā anuvittaḥ purāṇo yato devā udajāyanta viśve
children.translated_text: This is the ancient path that has been discovered, from which all the gods came forth.

children.text: ataś cid ā janiṣīṣṭa pravṛddho mā mātaram amuyā pattave kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From there, too, you were born, grown great; do not cause your mother to fall away yonder.

children.text: nāham ato nir ayā durgahaitat tiraścatā pārśvān nir gamāṇi
children.translated_text: I will not go out from here by this difficult passage; I will go out sideways through the flanks.

children.text: bahūni me akṛtā kartvāni yudhyai tvena saṃ tvena pṛcchai ||
children.translated_text: Many deeds of mine remain undone and must be done; I must fight, and with you I must contend and question.

children.text: parāyatīm mātaram anv acaṣṭa na nānu gāny anu nū gamāni
children.translated_text: He looked after his mother as she went away: 'I will not follow the paths that must be followed; I will not go after her now.'

children.text: tvaṣṭur gṛhe apibat somam indraḥ śatadhanyaṃ camvoḥ sutasya ||
children.translated_text: In the house of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Indra</s> drank the soma, pressed in the two bowls and rich with a hundred powers.

children.text: kiṃ sa ṛdhak kṛṇavad yaṃ sahasram māso jabhāra śaradaś ca pūrvīḥ
children.translated_text: What will he do apart, he whom his mother bore for a thousand months and for many autumns?

children.text: nahī nv asya pratimānam asty antar jāteṣūta ye janitvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For indeed there is no measure of him among those born, nor among those who are to be born.

children.text: avadyam iva manyamānā guhākar indram mātā vīryeṇā nyṛṣṭam
children.translated_text: Thinking it something blameworthy, <s>Indra</s>'s mother hid him in secret, cast away by reason of his heroic power.

children.text: athod asthāt svayam atkaṃ vasāna ā rodasī apṛṇāj jāyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he rose up by himself, clothing himself in a garment; as he was born, he filled heaven and earth.

children.text: etā arṣanty alalābhavantīr ṛtāvarīr iva saṃkrośamānāḥ
children.translated_text: These waters flow, as if impossible to hold back, truth-bearing, crying out together.

children.text: etā vi pṛccha kim idam bhananti kam āpo adrim paridhiṃ rujanti ||
children.translated_text: Ask these what they are saying, what rock, what enclosing barrier the waters are breaking.

children.text: kim u ṣvid asmai nivido bhanantendrasyāvadyaṃ didhiṣanta āpaḥ
children.translated_text: What proclamations do the waters speak for him? Are they wishing to reveal <s>Indra</s>'s blame?

children.text: mamaitān putro mahatā vadhena vṛtraṃ jaghanvāṁ asṛjad vi sindhūn ||
children.translated_text: 'My son, having slain <s>Vṛtra</s> with a great blow, has released these rivers.'

children.text: mamac cana tvā yuvatiḥ parāsa mamac cana tvā kuṣavā jagāra
children.translated_text: 'For my sake a young woman cast you away; for my sake <s>Kuṣavā</s> swallowed you.

children.text: mamac cid āpaḥ śiśave mamṛḍyur mamac cid indraḥ sahasod atiṣṭhat ||
children.translated_text: For my sake the waters were gracious to the child; for my sake <s>Indra</s> rose up with might.'

children.text: mamac cana te maghavan vyaṃso nivividhvāṁ apa hanū jaghāna
children.translated_text: 'For my sake, O <s>Maghavan</s>, when your shoulder was pierced, he struck your jaws away.

children.text: adhā nividdha uttaro babhūvāñchiro dāsasya sam piṇag vadhena ||
children.translated_text: Then, though pierced, you became the higher one; with the blow you crushed the head of the <s>Dāsa</s>.'

children.text: gṛṣṭiḥ sasūva sthaviraṃ tavāgām anādhṛṣyaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ tumram indram
children.translated_text: The cow gave birth to your strong, ancient bull, unassailable, mighty <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: arīﾱhaṃ vatsaṃ carathāya mātā svayaṃ gātuṃ tanva icchamānam ||
children.translated_text: The mother bore the unlicked calf for wandering, desiring a path for her own body.

children.text: uta mātā mahiṣam anv avenad amī tvā jahati putra devāḥ
children.translated_text: And the mother followed the great bull, saying, 'These gods are abandoning you, my son.'

children.text: athābravīd vṛtram indro haniṣyan sakhe viṣṇo vitaraṃ vi kramasva ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indra</s>, about to slay <s>Vṛtra</s>, said: "Friend <s>Viṣṇu</s>, stride out more widely."

children.text: kas te mātaraṃ vidhavām acakracchayuṃ kas tvām ajighāṃsac carantam
children.translated_text: Who made your mother a widow? Who wished to kill you as you moved about?

children.text: kas te devo adhi mārḍīka āsīd yat prākṣiṇāḥ pitaram pādagṛhya ||
children.translated_text: Which god was there to show you mercy, when you struck down your father, grasping him by the foot?

children.text: avartyā śuna āntrāṇi pece na deveṣu vivide marḍitāram
children.translated_text: In distress I cooked the entrails of a dog; among the gods I found no giver of mercy.

children.text: apaśyaṃ jāyām amahīyamānām adhā me śyeno madhv ā jabhāra ||
children.translated_text: I saw my wife being dishonored; then the eagle brought the sweet draught to me.

children.text: Chapter 315
evā tvām indra vajrinn atra viśve devāsaḥ suhavāsa ūmāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Indra</s>, wielder of the vajra, here all the gods, easy to invoke, aided you.

children.text: mahām ubhe rodasī vṛddham ṛṣvaṃ nir ekam id vṛṇate vṛtrahatye ||
children.translated_text: Grown great and lofty beyond both heaven and earth, they chose you alone for the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>.

children.text: avāsṛjanta jivrayo na devā bhuvaḥ samrāﾱ indra satyayoniḥ
children.translated_text: The gods let loose, as trembling old ones might; you became sovereign, O <s>Indra</s>, true in birth.

children.text: ahann ahim pariśayānam arṇaḥ pra vartanīr arado viśvadhenāḥ ||
children.translated_text: You struck the serpent lying around the flood; you opened the courses and dug out the all-nourishing waters.

children.text: atṛpṇuvantaṃ viyatam abudhyam abudhyamānaṃ suṣupāṇam indra
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>, the serpent was unsated, stretched out, unconscious, unaware, and sleeping deeply.

children.text: sapta prati pravata āśayānam ahiṃ vajreṇa vi riṇā aparvan ||
children.translated_text: As it lay across the seven slopes, you split the serpent apart with the joint-breaking vajra.

children.text: akṣodayacchavasā kṣāma budhnaṃ vār ṇa vātas taviṣībhir indraḥ
children.translated_text: With power <s>Indra</s> shook the earth's foundation, as wind shakes the waters with its mighty forces.

children.text: dṛﾱhāny aubhnād uśamāna ojo 'vābhinat kakubhaḥ parvatānām ||
children.translated_text: Seeking strength, he smashed the firm things; he split open the flanks of the mountains.

children.text: abhi pra dadrur janayo na garbhaṃ rathā iva pra yayuḥ sākam adrayaḥ
children.translated_text: The mothers broke forth like embryos; the rocks went forward together like chariots.

children.text: atarpayo visṛta ubja ūrmīn tvaṃ vṛtāṁ ariṇā indra sindhūn ||
children.translated_text: You satisfied the released, pressed-down waves; you freed the rivers enclosed by <s>Vṛtra</s>, O <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tvam mahīm avaniṃ viśvadhenāṃ turvītaye vayyāya kṣarantīm
children.translated_text: You released the great all-nourishing stream, flowing for <s>Turvīti</s> <s>Vayya</s>.

children.text: aramayo namasaijad arṇaḥ sutaraṇāṁ akṛṇor indra sindhūn ||
children.translated_text: You quieted the surging flood with reverence; you made the rivers easy to cross, O <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: prāgruvo nabhanvo na vakvā dhvasrā apinvad yuvatīr ṛtajñāḥ
children.translated_text: The forward-bending, cloud-born young women, knowing the truth, swelled like eloquent speakers.

children.text: dhanvāny ajrāṁ apṛṇak tṛṣāṇāṁ adhog indra staryo daṃsupatnīḥ ||
children.translated_text: You filled the waterless deserts that were thirsty; below, O <s>Indra</s>, the barren ones became wives of the drop-rich lord.

children.text: pūrvīr uṣasaḥ śaradaś ca gūrtā vṛtraṃ jaghanvāṁ asṛjad vi sindhūn
children.translated_text: Having slain <s>Vṛtra</s>, you released many dawns and autumns that had been swallowed, and you released the rivers.

children.text: pariṣṭhitā atṛṇad badbadhānāḥ sīrā indraḥ sravitave pṛthivyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> pierced the enclosed, bound-up channels of the earth so that they might flow.

children.text: vamrībhiḥ putram agruvo adānaṃ niveśanāddhariva ā jabhartha
children.translated_text: With the ants, O bay-horsed one, you brought the ungrasped son out from his dwelling.

children.text: vy andho akhyad ahim ādadāno nir bhūd ukhacchit sam aranta parva ||
children.translated_text: The blind one looked out when he took hold of the serpent; even the vessel-splitter emerged, and the joints came together.

children.text: pra te pūrvāṇi karaṇāni viprāvidvāṃ āha viduṣe karāṃsi
children.translated_text: The inspired poet, knowing, proclaims your former deeds to the one who knows, and your acts to be done.

children.text: yathā yathā vṛṣṇyāni svagūrtāpāṃsi rājan naryāviveṣīḥ ||
children.translated_text: As, again and again, O king, you entered the heroic powers and self-praised works of men.

children.text: nū ṣṭuta indra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo na pīpeḥ
children.translated_text: Now praised, O <s>Indra</s>, now being lauded, fill the singer with nourishment as rivers do.

children.text: akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A new sacred formulation has been made for you, O bay-horsed one; through insight may we always be fit for the chariot.

children.text: Chapter 316
ā na indro dūrād ā na āsād abhiṣṭikṛd avase yāsad ugraḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> come to us from afar; may the fierce accomplisher of help come near to us for protection.

children.text: ojiṣṭhebhir nṛpatir vajrabāhuḥ saṃge samatsu turvaṇiḥ pṛtanyūn ||
children.translated_text: With the strongest powers, the lord of men, vajra-armed, victorious in the clash, overcomes the fighters in battles.

children.text: ā na indro haribhir yātv acchārvācīno 'vase rādhase ca
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> come here toward us with his bay horses, facing this way, for aid and bounty.

children.text: tiṣṭhāti vajrī maghavā virapśīmaṃ yajñam anu no vājasātau ||
children.translated_text: The vajra-bearer, bounteous and widely powerful, stands by this sacrifice of ours in the winning of prizes.

children.text: imaṃ yajñaṃ tvam asmākam indra puro dadhat saniṣyasi kratuṃ naḥ
children.translated_text: Setting this sacrifice of ours in front, O <s>Indra</s>, you will accomplish our purpose.

children.text: śvaghnīva vajrin sanaye dhanānāṃ tvayā vayam arya ājiṃ jayema ||
children.translated_text: O vajra-bearer, as one strikes down the hostile for the winning of wealth, with you may we win the noble contest.

children.text: uśann u ṣu ṇaḥ sumanā upāke somasya nu suṣutasya svadhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Willing and kindly, come near to us, self-powered one, for the well-pressed soma.

children.text: pā indra pratibhṛtasya madhvaḥ sam andhasā mamadaḥ pṛṣṭhyena ||
children.translated_text: Drink, O <s>Indra</s>, of the presented honey; rejoice with the pressed soma draught upon your back.

children.text: vi yo rarapśa ṛṣibhir navebhir vṛkṣo na pakvaḥ sṛṇyo na jetā
children.translated_text: He who has shone forth with new seers, like a ripe tree, like a sickle that conquers,

children.text: maryo na yoṣām abhi manyamāno 'cchā vivakmi puruhūtam indram ||
children.translated_text: like a young man longing for a woman, I speak toward much-invoked <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: girir na yaḥ svatavāṁ ṛṣva indraḥ sanād eva sahase jāta ugraḥ
children.translated_text: He who, like a mountain, is self-strong and lofty, <s>Indra</s>, fierce and born from of old for might,

children.text: ādartā vajraṃ sthaviraṃ na bhīma udneva kośaṃ vasunā nyṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: a splitter with the vajra, terrible like an ancient one, like a water-skin stored with treasure in the waters.

children.text: na yasya vartā januṣā nv asti na rādhasa āmarītā maghasya
children.translated_text: There is no one who can turn aside his birth, nor any diminisher of his bounty or gift.

children.text: udvāvṛṣāṇas taviṣīva ugrāsmabhyaṃ daddhi puruhūta rāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Swelling upward with fierce force, give riches to us, O much-invoked one.

children.text: īkṣe rāyaḥ kṣayasya carṣaṇīnām uta vrajam apavartāsi gonām
children.translated_text: I look for wealth, for an abode among peoples; you are the opener of the pen of cattle.

children.text: śikṣānaraḥ samitheṣu prahāvān vasvo rāśim abhinetāsi bhūrim ||
children.translated_text: Instructing men, prominent in contests, you are the leader to a great heap of goods.

children.text: kayā tacchṛṇve śacyā śaciṣṭho yayā kṛṇoti muhu kā cid ṛṣvaḥ
children.translated_text: By what power do I hear of that, O most powerful one, by which the lofty one acts again and again?

children.text: puru dāśuṣe vicayiṣṭho aṃho 'thā dadhāti draviṇaṃ jaritre ||
children.translated_text: Most discerning, he removes much distress for the worshipper; then he gives wealth to the singer.

children.text: mā no mardhīr ā bharā daddhi tan naḥ pra dāśuṣe dātave bhūri yat te
children.translated_text: Do not neglect us; bring and give that to us. Give much of what is yours to the giver.

children.text: navye deṣṇe śaste asmin ta ukthe pra bravāma vayam indra stuvantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this new gift, in this praised hymn, we who praise will proclaim you, O <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: nū ṣṭuta indra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo na pīpeḥ
children.translated_text: Now praised, O <s>Indra</s>, now being lauded, fill the singer with nourishment as rivers do.

children.text: akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A new sacred formulation has been made for you, O bay-horsed one; through insight may we always be fit for the chariot.

children.text: Chapter 317
ā yātv indro 'vasa upa na iha stutaḥ sadhamād astu śūraḥ
children.translated_text: Let praised <s>Indra</s> come here to us for aid; let the hero be present at the common exhilaration.

children.text: vāvṛdhānas taviṣīr yasya pūrvīr dyaur na kṣatram abhibhūti puṣyāt ||
children.translated_text: His many powers are increasing; like heaven, may his dominion foster overwhelming might.

children.text: tasyed iha stavatha vṛṣṇyāni tuvidyumnasya tuvirādhaso nṝn
children.translated_text: Praise here the manly deeds of him, very brilliant and very bountiful toward men.

children.text: yasya kratur vidathyo na samrāṭ sāhvān tarutro abhy asti kṛṣṭīḥ ||
children.translated_text: His resolve, worthy of the assembly, stands over the peoples like a sovereign, victorious and overcoming.

children.text: ā yātv indro diva ā pṛthivyā makṣū samudrād uta vā purīṣāt
children.translated_text: Let <s>Indra</s> come from heaven, from earth, swiftly from the sea, or from the waters.

children.text: svarṇarād avase no marutvān parāvato vā sadanād ṛtasya ||
children.translated_text: Golden-rayed and accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>, may he come for our aid, or from the distance, from the seat of truth.

children.text: sthūrasya rāyo bṛhato ya īśe tam u ṣṭavāma vidatheṣv indram
children.translated_text: He who is lord of firm and great wealth, that <s>Indra</s> we praise in the rites.

children.text: yo vāyunā jayati gomatīṣu pra dhṛṣṇuyā nayati vasyo accha ||
children.translated_text: He who, with <s>Vāyu</s>, conquers among the cow-rich prizes, and boldly leads toward better wealth.

children.text: upa yo namo namasi stabhāyann iyarti vācaṃ janayan yajadhyai
children.translated_text: He who, supporting homage upon homage, sends forth speech, generating it for worship.

children.text: ṛñjasānaḥ puruvāra ukthair endraṃ kṛṇvīta sadaneṣu hotā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s>, making ready with hymns, should make <s>Indra</s>, much-invoked, present in the seats.

children.text: dhiṣā yadi dhiṣaṇyantaḥ saraṇyān sadanto adrim auśijasya gohe
children.translated_text: When, by inspired thought, the thoughtful ones sit down by the refuge, by the stone in the hiding-place of <s>Auśija</s>,

children.text: ā duroṣāḥ pāstyasya hotā yo no mahān saṃvaraṇeṣu vahniḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the <s>Hotṛ</s> of the dwelling comes to the strong doors, he who is our great carrier in the enclosures.

children.text: satrā yad īm bhārvarasya vṛṣṇaḥ siṣakti śuṣma stuvate bharāya
children.translated_text: When the force of that strong, splendid one clings entirely to the singer for support,

children.text: guhā yad īm auśijasya gohe pra yad dhiye prāyase madāya ||
children.translated_text: when it is hidden in the hiding-place of <s>Auśija</s>, then it goes forth for thought, for advance, and for exhilaration.

children.text: vi yad varāṃsi parvatasya vṛṇve payobhir jinve apāṃ javāṃsi
children.translated_text: When I uncover the chosen spaces of the mountain, I quicken the swift courses of the waters with their milk.

children.text: vidad gaurasya gavayasya gohe yadī vājāya sudhyo vahanti ||
children.translated_text: In the hiding-place of the tawny bull, of the wild cow, he finds it, when the wise ones carry it for the prize.

children.text: bhadrā te hastā sukṛtota pāṇī prayantārā stuvate rādha indra
children.translated_text: Your hands are fortunate, and your palms are well-working, O <s>Indra</s>, givers of reward to the praising man.

children.text: kā te niṣattiḥ kim u no mamatsi kiṃ nod ud u harṣase dātavā u ||
children.translated_text: What is your sitting-place? What will you bestow on us? What will you raise up for us in delight, to give?

children.text: evā vasva indraḥ satyaḥ samrāḍḍhantā vṛtraṃ varivaḥ pūrave kaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Indra</s>, true lord of wealth, the sovereign, slew <s>Vṛtra</s> and made wide room for <s>Pūru</s>.

children.text: puruṣṭuta kratvā naḥ śagdhi rāyo bhakṣīya te 'vaso daivyasya ||
children.translated_text: O much-praised one, with your insight give us power over riches; may I partake of your divine help.

children.text: nū ṣṭuta indra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo na pīpeḥ
children.translated_text: Now praised, O <s>Indra</s>, now being sung, fill the singer with refreshment as rivers fill him.

children.text: akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A new sacred formulation has been made for you, O tawny-horsed one; through inspired thought may we always be chariot-worthy servants.

children.text: Chapter 318
yan na indro jujuṣe yac ca vaṣṭi tan no mahān karati śuṣmy ā cit
children.translated_text: What <s>Indra</s> has accepted from us, and what he desires, that mighty, forceful one will do for us.

children.text: brahma stomam maghavā somam ukthā yo aśmānaṃ śavasā bibhrad eti ||
children.translated_text: The bounteous one comes bearing the sacred formulation, the chant, Soma, and hymns, carrying the stone by his might.

children.text: vṛṣā vṛṣandhiṃ caturaśrim asyann ugro bāhubhyāṃ nṛtamaḥ śacīvān
children.translated_text: The bull, fierce, best among men, powerful, hurling the four-cornered thunderbolt with his arms, smashes the stronghold.

children.text: śriye paruṣṇīm uṣamāṇa ūrṇāṃ yasyāḥ parvāṇi sakhyāya vivye ||
children.translated_text: For beauty he clothed <s>Paruṣṇī</s> like wool in the morning light, whose joints he unfolded for friendship.

children.text: yo devo devatamo jāyamāno maho vājebhir mahadbhiś ca śuṣmaiḥ
children.translated_text: The god, most divine at his birth, with great prizes and great powers,

children.text: dadhāno vajram bāhvor uśantaṃ dyām amena rejayat pra bhūma ||
children.translated_text: holding the eager thunderbolt in his arms, shook heaven with his force and sent the earth trembling.

children.text: viśvā rodhāṃsi pravataś ca pūrvīr dyaur ṛṣvāj janiman rejata kṣāḥ
children.translated_text: All barriers and the many slopes trembled; heaven, lofty from his birth, trembled, and the lands trembled.

children.text: ā mātarā bharati śuṣmy ā gor nṛvat parijman nonuvanta vātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He bears the two mothers with force like that of cattle; the winds, like men, continually roar around him as he ranges about.

children.text: tā tū ta indra mahato mahāni viśveṣv it savaneṣu pravācyā
children.translated_text: These, then, O <s>Indra</s>, are your great deeds, to be proclaimed at all Soma-pressings.

children.text: yacchūra dhṛṣṇo dhṛṣatā dadhṛṣvān ahiṃ vajreṇa śavasāviveṣīḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, O hero, bold one, boldly daring, you pierced the serpent with the thunderbolt by your might.

children.text: tā tū te satyā tuvinṛmṇa viśvā pra dhenavaḥ sisrate vṛṣṇa ūdhnaḥ
children.translated_text: These true deeds of yours, O strong-in-men one, all pour forth like cows from the udder of the bull.

children.text: adhā ha tvad vṛṣamaṇo bhiyānāḥ pra sindhavo javasā cakramanta ||
children.translated_text: Then, frightened by you, O mighty bull, the rivers set their wheels in motion with speed.

children.text: atrāha te harivas tā u devīr avobhir indra stavanta svasāraḥ
children.translated_text: Here indeed, O tawny-horsed <s>Indra</s>, those divine sisters praise you with their aids,

children.text: yat sīm anu pra muco badbadhānā dīrghām anu prasitiṃ syandayadhyai ||
children.translated_text: when you released them from their bonds so that they might flow along their long course.

children.text: pipīﾱe aṃśur madyo na sindhur ā tvā śamī śaśamānasya śaktiḥ
children.translated_text: The exhilarating stalk swelled like a river; toward you came the strength of the one who labors at the pressing.

children.text: asmadryak chuśucānasya yamyā āśur na raśmiṃ tuvyojasaṃ goḥ ||
children.translated_text: Toward us came the bright, kindred force, like the swift ray of a powerfully strong cow.

children.text: asme varṣiṣṭhā kṛṇuhi jyeṣṭhā nṛmṇāni satrā sahure sahāṃsi
children.translated_text: Make the highest and greatest manly powers for us, O overpowering one, all-surpassing strengths.

children.text: asmabhyaṃ vṛtrā suhanāni randhi jahi vadhar vanuṣo martyasya ||
children.translated_text: For us loosen the easily slain <s>Vṛtras</s>; strike the weapon of the hostile mortal.

children.text: asmākam it su śṛṇuhi tvam indrāsmabhyaṃ citrāṁ upa māhi vājān
children.translated_text: Hear us alone, O <s>Indra</s>; bring splendid prizes near to us.

children.text: asmabhyaṃ viśvā iṣaṇaḥ purandhīr asmākaṃ su maghavan bodhi godāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Bring all nourishing abundance to us; O bounteous one, be a giver of cows for us.

children.text: nū ṣṭuta indra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo na pīpeḥ
children.translated_text: Now praised, O <s>Indra</s>, now being sung, fill the singer with refreshment as rivers fill him.

children.text: akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A new sacred formulation has been made for you, O tawny-horsed one; through inspired thought may we always be chariot-worthy servants.

children.text: Chapter 319
kathā mahām avṛdhat kasya hotur yajñaṃ juṣāṇo abhi somam ūdhaḥ
children.translated_text: How did the great one grow? At whose <s>Hotṛ</s>'s rite, enjoying the sacrifice, did he swell over the Soma?

children.text: pibann uśāno juṣamāṇo andho vavakṣa ṛṣvaḥ śucate dhanāya ||
children.translated_text: Drinking, desiring, and enjoying the draught, the lofty one has grown strong, shining for treasure.

children.text: ko asya vīraḥ sadhamādam āpa sam ānaṃśa sumatibhiḥ ko asya
children.translated_text: What hero of his attained the common exhilaration? Who shared equally in his good thoughts?

children.text: kad asya citraṃ cikite kad ūtī vṛdhe bhuvacchaśamānasya yajyoḥ ||
children.translated_text: When was his bright aid perceived? When will he become worthy of worship for the increase of the one who praises him?

children.text: kathā śṛṇoti hūyamānam indraḥ kathā śṛṇvann avasām asya veda
children.translated_text: How does <s>Indra</s> hear the one who calls? Hearing, how does he know his help?

children.text: kā asya pūrvīr upamātayo ha kathainam āhuḥ papuriṃ jaritre ||
children.translated_text: What are his many former measures? How do they call him an abundant giver for the singer?

children.text: kathā sabādhaḥ śaśamāno asya naśad abhi draviṇaṃ dīdhyānaḥ
children.translated_text: How, while being praised, does he overcome oppression and, meditating, win wealth?

children.text: devo bhuvan navedā ma ṛtānāṃ namo jagṛbhvāṁ abhi yaj jujoṣat ||
children.translated_text: May the god, the knower of beings and of truths, accept the reverence that has been grasped and offered.

children.text: kathā kad asyā uṣaso vyuṣṭau devo martasya sakhyaṃ jujoṣa
children.translated_text: How and when, at the shining forth of this <s>Uṣas</s>, did the god accept friendship with the mortal?

children.text: kathā kad asya sakhyaṃ sakhibhyo ye asmin kāmaṃ suyujaṃ tatasre ||
children.translated_text: How and when did his friendship come to the friends who spread a well-yoked desire upon him?

children.text: kim ād amatraṃ sakhyaṃ sakhibhyaḥ kadā nu te bhrātram pra bravāma
children.translated_text: What, then, is the measureless friendship for the friends? When shall we proclaim your brotherhood?

children.text: śriye sudṛśo vapur asya sargāḥ svar ṇa citratamam iṣa ā goḥ ||
children.translated_text: For splendor are the beautiful releases of his form, bringing the most variegated heavenly light and nourishment from the cow.

children.text: druhaṃ jighāṃsan dhvarasam anindrāṃ tetikte tigmā tujase anīkā
children.translated_text: Intending to strike the deceitful, harmful, Indra-less one, he sharpens keen fronts for the charge.

children.text: ṛṇā cid yatra ṛṇayā na ugro dūre ajñātā uṣaso babādhe ||
children.translated_text: Where even debts are repaid by debt, there the fierce one drove the unknown dawns far away from us.

children.text: ṛtasya hi śurudhaḥ santi pūrvīr ṛtasya dhītir vṛjināni hanti
children.translated_text: For the protections of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order) are many and ancient; the thought of <s>ṛta</s> destroys crooked acts.

children.text: ṛtasya śloko badhirā tatarda karṇā budhānaḥ śucamāna āyoḥ ||
children.translated_text: The verse of <s>ṛta</s> has pierced deaf ears, awakening and purifying the life of man.

children.text: ṛtasya dṛﾱhā dharuṇāni santi purūṇi candrā vapuṣe vapūṃṣi
children.translated_text: The firm supports of <s>ṛta</s> are many; its bright forms are there for its visible form.

children.text: ṛtena dīrgham iṣaṇanta pṛkṣa ṛtena gāva ṛtam ā viveśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By <s>ṛta</s> they seek long nourishment and abundance; by <s>ṛta</s> the cows have entered <s>ṛta</s>.

children.text: ṛtaṃ yemāna ṛtam id vanoty ṛtasya śuṣmas turayā u gavyuḥ
children.translated_text: Holding to <s>ṛta</s>, one wins only <s>ṛta</s>; the force of <s>ṛta</s> hastens toward cattle.

children.text: ṛtāya pṛthvī bahule gabhīre ṛtāya dhenū parame duhāte ||
children.translated_text: For <s>ṛta</s> the broad, deep earth exists; for <s>ṛta</s> the two cows milk in the highest place.

children.text: nū ṣṭuta indra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo na pīpeḥ
children.translated_text: Now praised, O <s>Indra</s>, now being sung, fill the singer with refreshment as rivers fill him.

children.text: akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A new sacred formulation has been made for you, O tawny-horsed one; through inspired thought may we always be chariot-worthy servants.

children.text: Chapter 320
kā suṣṭutiḥ śavasaḥ sūnum indram arvācīnaṃ rādhasa ā vavartat
children.translated_text: What excellent praise has turned <s>Indra</s>, the son of strength, hither for bounty?

children.text: dadir hi vīro gṛṇate vasūni sa gopatir niṣṣidhāṃ no janāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the hero gives goods to the singer; he, lord of cows, O people, is our remover of restraints.

children.text: sa vṛtrahatye havyaḥ sa īḍyaḥ sa suṣṭuta indraḥ satyarādhāḥ
children.translated_text: He is to be invoked at the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>; he is to be praised; he, <s>Indra</s>, well lauded, is true in his gifts.

children.text: sa yāmann ā maghavā martyāya brahmaṇyate suṣvaye varivo dhāt ||
children.translated_text: On the march, may <s>Maghavan</s> grant wide space to the mortal who prays and presses Soma well.

children.text: tam in naro vi hvayante samīke ririkvāṃsas tanvaḥ kṛṇvata trām
children.translated_text: Men call upon him in every way in the clash, spending their bodies and making him their protector.

children.text: mitho yat tyāgam ubhayāso agman naras tokasya tanayasya sātau ||
children.translated_text: When both sides have come to mutual attack, men seek the winning of child and offspring.

children.text: kratūyanti kṣitayo yoga ugrāśuṣāṇāso mitho arṇasātau
children.translated_text: The peoples strive for resolve, fierce in the yoking, eager against one another in the struggle for the prize.

children.text: saṃ yad viśo 'vavṛtranta yudhmā ād in nema indrayante abhīke ||
children.translated_text: When the clans gather round for battle, then some, close at hand, become devoted to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: ād iddha nema indriyaṃ yajanta ād it paktiḥ puroﾱāśaṃ riricyāt
children.translated_text: Then indeed some worship <s>Indra</s>'s power; then the cooked cake, the <s>puroḍāśa</s> offering, is set apart.

children.text: ād it somo vi papṛcyād asuṣvīn ād ij jujoṣa vṛṣabhaṃ yajadhyai ||
children.translated_text: Then the Soma is mixed for the Soma-presser; then he has taken pleasure in worshipping the bull.

children.text: kṛṇoty asmai varivo ya itthendrāya somam uśate sunoti
children.translated_text: He makes wide room for the one who, desiring <s>Indra</s> in this way, presses Soma for him.

children.text: sadhrīcīnena manasāvivenan tam it sakhāyaṃ kṛṇute samatsu ||
children.translated_text: With a mind turned the same way and not hostile, he makes that one his friend in battles.

children.text: ya indrāya sunavat somam adya pacāt paktīr uta bhṛjjāti dhānāḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever today will press Soma for <s>Indra</s>, cook the cakes, and roast the grains,

children.text: prati manāyor ucathāni haryan tasmin dadhad vṛṣaṇaṃ śuṣmam indraḥ ||
children.translated_text: in him <s>Indra</s>, the bull, places manly force, delighting in songs directed to his thought.

children.text: yadā samaryaṃ vy aced ṛghāvā dīrghaṃ yad ājim abhy akhyad aryaḥ
children.translated_text: When the noble one perceived the contest, when he looked out over the long race of battle,

children.text: acikradad vṛṣaṇam patny acchā duroṇa ā niśitaṃ somasudbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wife cried out toward the bull in the house, toward him sharpened by the Soma-pressers.

children.text: bhūyasā vasnam acarat kanīyo 'vikrīto akāniṣam punar yan
children.translated_text: I went about seeking a greater price, though offered less; unsold, I have come back again.

children.text: sa bhūyasā kanīyo nārirecīd dīnā dakṣā vi duhanti pra vāṇam ||
children.translated_text: He has not been surpassed, the lesser by the greater; poor but skillful ones milk out inspired speech.

children.text: ka imaṃ daśabhir mamendraṃ krīṇāti dhenubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Who will buy this <s>Indra</s> from me for ten milch cows?

children.text: yadā vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanad athainam me punar dadat ||
children.translated_text: When he has struck down the <s>Vṛtras</s>, then let him give him back to me again.

children.text: nū ṣṭuta indra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo na pīpeḥ
children.translated_text: Now praised, now being sung, O <s>Indra</s>, fill the singer with refreshment as rivers fill their banks.

children.text: akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A new prayer has been made for you, O bay-horsed one; through inspired thought may we be your chariot-companions always.

children.text: Chapter 321
ko adya naryo devakāma uśann indrasya sakhyaṃ jujoṣa
children.translated_text: What manly one today, god-loving and desiring, has taken pleasure in <s>Indra</s>'s friendship?

children.text: ko vā mahe 'vase pāryāya samiddhe agnau sutasoma īṭṭe ||
children.translated_text: Or who, with Soma pressed and the fire kindled, seeks him for great help that carries beyond?

children.text: ko nānāma vacasā somyāya manāyur vā bhavati vasta usrāḥ
children.translated_text: Who has bowed with speech to the Soma-worthy one, or, intent in mind, becomes one who clothes the bright dawns?

children.text: ka indrasya yujyaṃ kaḥ sakhitvaṃ ko bhrātraṃ vaṣṭi kavaye ka ūtī ||
children.translated_text: Who wants <s>Indra</s>'s yoke, who his friendship, who brotherhood with him, who aid for the inspired poet?

children.text: ko devānām avo adyā vṛṇīte ka ādityāṁ aditiṃ jyotir īṭṭe
children.translated_text: Who today chooses the help of the gods? Who seeks the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Aditi</s>, and the light?

children.text: kasyāśvināv indro agniḥ sutasyāṃśoḥ pibanti manasāvivenam ||
children.translated_text: Whose pressed Soma do the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Agni</s> drink with an undivided mind?

children.text: tasmā agnir bhārataḥ śarma yaṃsaj jyok paśyāt sūryam uccarantam
children.translated_text: For him may <s>Agni Bhārata</s> grant shelter; may he long behold the rising sun,

children.text: ya indrāya sunavāmety āha nare naryāya nṛtamāya nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: the man who says, 'Let us press Soma for <s>Indra</s>, for the manly hero, the most manly of men.'

children.text: na taṃ jinanti bahavo na dabhrā urv asmā aditiḥ śarma yaṃsat
children.translated_text: Neither many nor few overcome him; wide <s>Aditi</s> shall extend shelter for him.

children.text: priyaḥ sukṛt priya indre manāyuḥ priyaḥ suprāvīḥ priyo asya somī ||
children.translated_text: Dear is the well-doer, dear to <s>Indra</s>, intent in mind; dear is the good protector, dear is his Soma-presser.

children.text: suprāvyaḥ prāśuṣāﾱ eṣa vīraḥ suṣveḥ paktiṃ kṛṇute kevalendraḥ
children.translated_text: This hero is easy to aid for the generous worshipper; for the good Soma-presser <s>Indra</s> alone prepares the cooked offering.

children.text: nāsuṣver āpir na sakhā na jāmir duṣprāvyo 'vahanted avācaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the non-presser there is no companion, no friend, no kinsman; hard to aid, the low-speaking ones are carried downward.

children.text: na revatā paṇinā sakhyam indro 'sunvatā sutapāḥ saṃ gṛṇīte
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, drinker of the pressed Soma, does not enter friendship with the wealthy <s>Paṇi</s> who presses no Soma.

children.text: āsya vedaḥ khidati hanti nagnaṃ vi suṣvaye paktaye kevalo bhūt ||
children.translated_text: His treasure troubles him; he strikes down the naked one; for the good presser, for the cooked offering, he becomes the only one.

children.text: indram pare 'vare madhyamāsa indraṃ yānto 'vasitāsa indram
children.translated_text: Those beyond, those nearer, and those in the middle go to <s>Indra</s>; those seeking help go to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: indraṃ kṣiyanta uta yudhyamānā indraṃ naro vājayanto havante ||
children.translated_text: Those who dwell at home and those who fight, men seeking the prize, call upon <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: Chapter 322
aham manur abhavaṃ sūryaś cāhaṃ kakṣīvāṁ ṛṣir asmi vipraḥ
children.translated_text: I became <s>Manu</s>, and I became the Sun; I am <s>Kakṣīvān</s>, the seer, the inspired poet.

children.text: ahaṃ kutsam ārjuneyaṃ ny ṛñje 'haṃ kavir uśanā paśyatā mā ||
children.translated_text: I have adorned <s>Kutsa Ārjuneya</s>; I am the poet <s>Uśanā</s>. Look upon me.

children.text: aham bhūmim adadām āryāyāhaṃ vṛṣṭiṃ dāśuṣe martyāya
children.translated_text: I gave the earth to the <s>Ārya</s>; I gave rain to the worshipping mortal.

children.text: aham apo anayaṃ vāvaśānā mama devāso anu ketam āyan ||
children.translated_text: I led forth the roaring waters; the gods followed after my sign.

children.text: aham puro mandasāno vy airaṃ nava sākaṃ navatīḥ śambarasya
children.translated_text: Exhilarated, I shattered the forts, the ninety-nine together belonging to <s>Śambara</s>,

children.text: śatatamaṃ veśyaṃ sarvatātā divodāsam atithigvaṃ yad āvam ||
children.translated_text: and the hundredth dwelling, in the all-sided struggle, when I aided <s>Divodāsa Atithigva</s>.

children.text: pra su ṣa vibhyo maruto vir astu pra śyenaḥ śyenebhya āśupatvā
children.translated_text: Let the hero go forth from among you, O <s>Maruts</s>; let the falcon go forth from the falcons with swift flight.

children.text: acakrayā yat svadhayā suparṇo havyam bharan manave devajuṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: When the fair-winged one, without wheels, by his own power, carried the god-loved oblation for <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: bharad yadi vir ato vevijānaḥ pathoruṇā manojavā asarji
children.translated_text: When the bird, trembling from there, carried it, he was released upon the broad path, swift as thought.

children.text: tūyaṃ yayau madhunā somyenota śravo vivide śyeno atra ||
children.translated_text: He went quickly with the honeyed Soma; and here the falcon won renown.

children.text: ṛjīpī śyeno dadamāno aṃśum parāvataḥ śakuno mandram madam
children.translated_text: The straight-flying falcon, giving the Soma-stalk, the bird from afar, the gladdening exhilaration,

children.text: somam bharad dādṛhāṇo devāvān divo amuṣmād uttarād ādāya ||
children.translated_text: carried the Soma, holding it fast, accompanied by the gods, taking it from that highest heaven.

children.text: ādāya śyeno abharat somaṃ sahasraṃ savāṁ ayutaṃ ca sākam
children.translated_text: Taking it, the falcon brought the Soma together with a thousand pressings and ten thousand besides.

children.text: atrā purandhir ajahād arātīr made somasya mūrā amūraḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, in the exhilaration of Soma, discerning <s>Purandhi</s>, not deluded, left the hostile fools behind.

children.text: Chapter 323
garbhe nu sann anv eṣām avedam ahaṃ devānāṃ janimāni viśvā
children.translated_text: Even while in the womb, I knew all the births of these gods.

children.text: śatam mā pura āyasīr arakṣann adha śyeno javasā nir adīyam ||
children.translated_text: A hundred iron forts guarded me; then, as a falcon, I flew out with speed.

children.text: na ghā sa mām apa joṣaṃ jabhārābhīm āsa tvakṣasā vīryeṇa
children.translated_text: He did not carry me away against my will; he came upon them with craft and heroic power.

children.text: īrmā purandhir ajahād arātīr uta vātāṁ ataracchūśuvānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Discerning <s>Purandhi</s> left the hostilities behind and, swelling with force, crossed the winds.

children.text: ava yacchyeno asvanīd adha dyor vi yad yadi vāta ūhuḥ purandhim
children.translated_text: When the falcon cried out, then from heaven, when the winds bore <s>Purandhi</s> apart,

children.text: sṛjad yad asmā ava ha kṣipaj jyāṃ kṛśānur astā manasā bhuraṇyan ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Kṛśānu</s>, the archer, hastening in mind, shot at him and let the bowstring fly,

children.text: ṛjipya īm indrāvato na bhujyuṃ śyeno jabhāra bṛhato adhi ṣṇoḥ
children.translated_text: the straight-flying falcon, aided by <s>Indra</s>, carried him from the great height as one carries <s>Bhujyu</s>.

children.text: antaḥ patat patatry asya parṇam adha yāmani prasitasya tad veḥ ||
children.translated_text: Inside it the bird's wing fell as it flew; below was the course of that hastening bird.

children.text: adha śvetaṃ kalaśaṃ gobhir aktam āpipyānam maghavā śukram andhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the white vessel, anointed with milk, swelled; <s>Maghavan</s> had the bright draught

children.text: adhvaryubhiḥ prayatam madhvo agram indro madāya prati dhat pibadhyai śūro madāya prati dhat pibadhyai ||
children.translated_text: the first sweetness, prepared by the <s>adhvaryu</s> priests, set before <s>Indra</s> for exhilaration, for drinking; before the hero for exhilaration, for drinking.

children.text: Chapter 324
tvā yujā tava tat soma sakhya indro apo manave sasrutas kaḥ
children.translated_text: With you as ally, in your friendship, O <s>Soma</s>, <s>Indra</s> made the waters flow for <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: ahann ahim ariṇāt sapta sindhūn apāvṛṇod apihiteva khāni ||
children.translated_text: He slew <s>Ahi</s>, drove forth the seven rivers, and opened the closed places as if they were channels.

children.text: tvā yujā ni khidat sūryasyendraś cakraṃ sahasā sadya indo
children.translated_text: With you as ally, O drop of <s>Soma</s>, <s>Indra</s> at once, by force, broke down the wheel of the sun,

children.text: adhi ṣṇunā bṛhatā vartamānam maho druho apa viśvāyu dhāyi ||
children.translated_text: as it was turning upon the great height; the great malice of <s>Viśvāyu</s> was put away.

children.text: ahann indro adahad agnir indo purā dasyūn madhyandinād abhīke
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> slew and <s>Agni</s> burned, O drop of <s>Soma</s>, the former <s>Dasyus</s> in the midday encounter.

children.text: durge duroṇe kratvā na yātām purū sahasrā śarvā ni barhīt ||
children.translated_text: By their skill they did not go into the hard-to-reach dwelling; they cut down many thousands of missiles.

children.text: viśvasmāt sīm adhamāṁ indra dasyūn viśo dāsīr akṛṇor apraśastāḥ
children.translated_text: From every side, O <s>Indra</s>, you made the <s>Dasyus</s> lowest; you made the servile peoples without renown.

children.text: abādhethām amṛṇataṃ ni śatrūn avindethām apacitiṃ vadhatraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: You two drove them away and crushed the enemies; with your weapons you found satisfaction.

children.text: evā satyam maghavānā yuvaṃ tad indraś ca somorvam aśvyaṃ goḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, O two bounteous ones, that is true: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s> won the broad horse-prize and cow-prize.

children.text: ādardṛtam apihitāny aśnā riricathuḥ kṣāś cit tatṛdānā ||
children.translated_text: You split open the covered stores of food; you emptied even the strongholds as they were being pierced.

children.text: Chapter 325
ā na stuta upa vājebhir ūtī indra yāhi haribhir mandasānaḥ
children.translated_text: Come to us, praised one, with aids and prizes, O <s>Indra</s>; come with your bay horses, rejoicing.

children.text: tiraś cid aryaḥ savanā purūṇy āṅgūṣebhir gṛṇānaḥ satyarādhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even across many pressings of the noble man, praised with songs, you are true in bounty.

children.text: ā hi ṣmā yāti naryaś cikitvān hūyamānaḥ sotṛbhir upa yajñam
children.translated_text: For he, the manly and discerning one, comes when called by the pressers to the sacrifice.

children.text: svaśvo yo abhīrur manyamānaḥ suṣvāṇebhir madati saṃ ha vīraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who has good horses, thinking himself fearless, rejoices with the good pressers, together with heroes.

children.text: śrāvayed asya karṇā vājayadhyai juṣṭām anu pra diśam mandayadhyai
children.translated_text: Let him make his ears hear, so that he may win the prize; let him rejoice along the beloved direction.

children.text: udvāvṛṣāṇo rādhase tuviṣmān karan na indraḥ sutīrthābhayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Rising up strongly for bounty, mighty <s>Indra</s> will make good crossings and safety for us.

children.text: acchā yo gantā nādhamānam ūtī itthā vipraṃ havamānaṃ gṛṇantam
children.translated_text: He who will go with aid to the needy man, to the inspired singer who invokes and praises in this way,

children.text: upa tmani dadhāno dhury āśūn sahasrāṇi śatāni vajrabāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: setting the swift burden-bearers under his own yoke, the thunderbolt-armed one has thousands and hundreds.

children.text: tvotāso maghavann indra viprā vayaṃ te syāma sūrayo gṛṇantaḥ
children.translated_text: Aided by you, O bounteous <s>Indra</s>, may we inspired singers be your praising patrons,

children.text: bhejānāso bṛhaddivasya rāya ākāyyasya dāvane purukṣoḥ ||
children.translated_text: sharing in the wealth of <s>Bṛhaddiva</s>, of <s>Ākāyya</s>, rich in gifts and many cattle.

children.text: Chapter 326
nakir indra tvad uttaro na jyāyāṁ asti vṛtrahan
children.translated_text: No one, O <s>Indra</s>, is higher than you; no one greater exists, O <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer.

children.text: nakir evā yathā tvam ||
children.translated_text: No one is just as you are.

children.text: satrā te anu kṛṣṭayo viśvā cakreva vāvṛtuḥ
children.translated_text: All peoples have completely turned after you, like wheels.

children.text: satrā mahāṁ asi śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are altogether great and famed.

children.text: viśve caned anā tvā devāsa indra yuyudhuḥ
children.translated_text: Not even all the gods, O <s>Indra</s>, have defeated you,

children.text: yad ahā naktam ātiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: when you extended day and night.

children.text: yatrota bādhitebhyaś cakraṃ kutsāya yudhyate
children.translated_text: Where, moreover, for the hard-pressed, the wheel fought for <s>Kutsa</s>,

children.text: muṣāya indra sūryam ||
children.translated_text: there, O <s>Indra</s>, you stole away the sun for <s>Muṣa</s>.

children.text: yatra devāṁ ṛghāyato viśvāṁ ayudhya eka it
children.translated_text: Where, fighting alone, you fought all the hostile gods,

children.text: tvam indra vanūṃr ahan ||
children.translated_text: you, O <s>Indra</s>, slew the assailants.

children.text: yatrota martyāya kam ariṇā indra sūryam
children.translated_text: Where, O <s>Indra</s>, you set the sun in motion for that mortal,

children.text: prāvaḥ śacībhir etaśam ||
children.translated_text: you protected <s>Etaśa</s> with your powers.

children.text: kim ād utāsi vṛtrahan maghavan manyumattamaḥ
children.translated_text: What, then, are you, O <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer, O bounteous one, most full of wrath?

children.text: atrāha dānum ātiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: There indeed you overpowered <s>Dānu</s>.

children.text: etad ghed uta vīryam indra cakartha pauṃsyam
children.translated_text: This indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, was the heroic manly deed that you performed,

children.text: striyaṃ yad durhaṇāyuvaṃ vadhīr duhitaraṃ divaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when you slew the hard-to-subdue woman, the daughter of heaven.

children.text: divaś cid ghā duhitaram mahān mahīyamānām
children.translated_text: Even the daughter of heaven, great and growing mighty,

children.text: uṣāsam indra sam piṇak ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uṣas</s>, the dawn, O <s>Indra</s>, you crushed together.

children.text: apoṣā anasaḥ sarat sampiṣṭād aha bibhyuṣī
children.translated_text: Away from her wagon <s>Uṣas</s> fled, afraid of the shattered car,

children.text: ni yat sīṃ śiśnathad vṛṣā ||
children.translated_text: when the bull crushed her.

children.text: etad asyā anaḥ śaye susampiṣṭaṃ vipāśy ā
children.translated_text: This wagon of hers lies by the <s>Vipāś</s>, well crushed;

children.text: sasāra sīm parāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: she herself has gone away from afar.

children.text: uta sindhuṃ vibālyaṃ vitasthānām adhi kṣami
children.translated_text: And the <s>Sindhu</s>, the <s>Vibālī</s>, and the <s>Vitasthā</s>, upon the earth,

children.text: pari ṣṭhā indra māyayā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>, you encompassed with <s>māyā</s> (supernatural power).

children.text: uta śuṣṇasya dhṛṣṇuyā pra mṛkṣo abhi vedanam
children.translated_text: And with bold force you struck away the hiding-place of <s>Śuṣṇa</s>,

children.text: puro yad asya saṃpiṇak ||
children.translated_text: when you crushed his strongholds.

children.text: uta dāsaṃ kaulitaram bṛhataḥ parvatād adhi
children.translated_text: And from the great mountain, O <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: avāhann indra śambaram ||
children.translated_text: you struck down <s>Śambara</s>, the <s>Kaulitara</s> <s>Dāsa</s>.

children.text: uta dāsasya varcinaḥ sahasrāṇi śatāvadhīḥ
children.translated_text: And you slew hundreds and thousands belonging to <s>Varcin</s> the <s>Dāsa</s>,

children.text: adhi pañca pradhīṃr iva ||
children.translated_text: as if upon five spokes.

children.text: uta tyam putram agruvaḥ parāvṛktaṃ śatakratuḥ
children.translated_text: And that son of <s>Agru</s>, cast far away,

children.text: uktheṣv indra ābhajat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> of a hundred powers assigned to the hymns.

children.text: uta tyā turvaśāyadū asnātārā śacīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: And those two, <s>Turvaśa</s> and <s>Yadu</s>, unable to swim,

children.text: indro vidvāṁ apārayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, lord of powers, knowingly carried across.

children.text: uta tyā sadya āryā sarayor indra pārataḥ
children.translated_text: And those noble ones, at once across the <s>Sarayu</s>, O <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: arṇācitrarathāvadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: you slew <s>Arṇa</s> and <s>Citraratha</s>.

children.text: anu dvā jahitā nayo 'ndhaṃ śroṇaṃ ca vṛtrahan
children.translated_text: Follow after the two left behind, the blind man and the lame man, O <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer;

children.text: na tat te sumnam aṣṭave ||
children.translated_text: that favor of yours is not to be treated with contempt.

children.text: śatam aśmanmayīnām purām indro vy āsyat
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> split open a hundred stone-built strongholds

children.text: divodāsāya dāśuṣe ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Divodāsa</s>, the worshipper.
