children.text: anv aha māsā anv id vanāny anv oṣadhīr anu parvatāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Day after day, the months follow him; the forests follow, the plants follow, and the mountains follow.

children.text: anv indraṃ rodasī vāvaśāne anv āpo ajihata jāyamānam ||
children.translated_text: Heaven and earth, longing, followed <s>Indra</s>; the waters stirred after him as he was being born.

children.text: karhi svit sā ta indra cetyāsad aghasya yad bhinado rakṣa eṣat
children.translated_text: When will that deed of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, become renowned: that you split apart the evil as the demon came on?

children.text: mitrakruvo yacchasane na gāvaḥ pṛthivyā āpṛg amuyā śayante ||
children.translated_text: When the betrayers of friendship lie there, covering the earth, like cattle in the enclosure.

children.text: śatrūyanto abhi ye nas tatasre mahi vrādhanta ogaṇāsa indra
children.translated_text: Those who, acting as enemies, have spread themselves against us, the great hostile hosts, O <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: andhenāmitrās tamasā sacantāṃ sujyotiṣo aktavas tāṁ abhi ṣyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: let the unfriendly ones join with blind darkness; let the nights of good light pass over them.

children.text: purūṇi hi tvā savanā janānām brahmāṇi mandan gṛṇatām ṛṣīṇām
children.translated_text: For the many Soma-pressings of the people and the sacred formulations of the praising seers have gladdened you.

children.text: imām āghoṣann avasā sahūtiṃ tiro viśvāṁ arcato yāhy arvāṅ ||
children.translated_text: As they proclaim aloud this invocation that calls for aid, come here across all worshippers.

children.text: evā te vayam indra bhuñjatīnāṃ vidyāma sumatīnāṃ navānām
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Indra</s>, may we come to know your new good favors, those that are to be enjoyed.

children.text: vidyāma vastor avasā gṛṇanto viśvāmitrā uta ta indra nūnam ||
children.translated_text: Praising with aid at morning, may the <s>Viśvāmitras</s> know them, and now your favors too, O <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: śunaṃ huvema maghavānam indram asmin bhare nṛtamaṃ vājasātau
children.translated_text: May we call for blessing upon bountiful <s>Indra</s>, the most manly one, in this contest for the winning of prizes,

children.text: śṛṇvantam ugram ūtaye samatsu ghnantaṃ vṛtrāṇi saṃjitaṃ dhanānām ||
children.translated_text: upon him who listens, fierce for help in battles, who strikes down the <s>Vṛtras</s> and wins the riches.

children.text: Chapter 927
sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s> has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet.

children.text: sa bhūmiṃ viśvato vṛtvāty atiṣṭhad daśāṅgulam ||
children.translated_text: Having enveloped the earth on every side, he stood beyond it by ten fingers' breadth.

children.text: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yac ca bhavyam
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this, whatever has been and whatever will be.

children.text: utāmṛtatvasyeśāno yad annenātirohati ||
children.translated_text: And he is lord of immortality, and of what grows beyond through food.

children.text: etāvān asya mahimāto jyāyāṃś ca pūruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: So great is his greatness; yet the <s>Puruṣa</s> is greater than this.

children.text: pādo 'sya viśvā bhūtāni tripād asyāmṛtaṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: All beings are one quarter of him; three quarters of him are the immortal in heaven.

children.text: tripād ūrdhva ud ait puruṣaḥ pādo 'syehābhavat punaḥ
children.translated_text: Three quarters of the <s>Puruṣa</s> rose upward; one quarter of him became here again.

children.text: tato viṣvaṅ vy akrāmat sāśanānaśane abhi ||
children.translated_text: From there he spread out in every direction over what eats and what does not eat.

children.text: tasmād virāḍ ajāyata virājo adhi pūruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: From him <s>Virāj</s> was born; from <s>Virāj</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: sa jāto aty aricyata paścād bhūmim atho puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Once born, he extended beyond, behind the earth and also before it.

children.text: yat puruṣeṇa haviṣā devā yajñam atanvata
children.translated_text: When, with the <s>Puruṣa</s> as the oblation, the gods stretched out the sacrifice,

children.text: vasanto asyāsīd ājyaṃ grīṣma idhmaḥ śaraddhaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: spring was its ghee, summer its fuel, and autumn its oblation.

children.text: taṃ yajñam barhiṣi praukṣan puruṣaṃ jātam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: They sprinkled that sacrifice upon the sacrificial grass, the <s>Puruṣa</s> born at the beginning.

children.text: tena devā ayajanta sādhyā ṛṣayaś ca ye ||
children.translated_text: With it the gods sacrificed, and so did the <s>Sādhyas</s> and the seers who were there.

children.text: tasmād yajñāt sarvahutaḥ saṃbhṛtam pṛṣadājyam
children.translated_text: From that sacrifice, offered wholly, the curdled ghee was gathered together.

children.text: paśūn tāṃś cakre vāyavyān āraṇyān grāmyāś ca ye ||
children.translated_text: He made those animals: those of the air, those of the forest, and those that belong to the village.

children.text: tasmād yajñāt sarvahuta ṛcaḥ sāmāni jajñire
children.translated_text: From that sacrifice, offered wholly, the Ṛc verses and the Sāman chants were born.

children.text: chandāṃsi jajñire tasmād yajus tasmād ajāyata ||
children.translated_text: The meters were born from it; from it the Yajus was born.

children.text: tasmād aśvā ajāyanta ye ke cobhayādataḥ
children.translated_text: From it horses were born, and whatever animals have teeth in both jaws.

children.text: gāvo ha jajñire tasmāt tasmāj jātā ajāvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cows indeed were born from it; from it goats and sheep were born.

children.text: yat puruṣaṃ vy adadhuḥ katidhā vy akalpayan
children.translated_text: When they divided the <s>Puruṣa</s>, into how many portions did they arrange him?

children.text: mukhaṃ kim asya kau bāhū kā ūrū pādā ucyete ||
children.translated_text: What was called his mouth? What were his two arms? What were his two thighs and feet called?

children.text: brāhmaṇo 'sya mukham āsīd bāhū rājanyaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was his mouth; his two arms were made the <s>Rājanya</s>.

children.text: ūrū tad asya yad vaiśyaḥ padbhyāṃ śūdro ajāyata ||
children.translated_text: What was his two thighs became the <s>Vaiśya</s>; from his two feet the <s>Śūdra</s> was born.

children.text: candramā manaso jātaś cakṣoḥ sūryo ajāyata
children.translated_text: The moon was born from his mind; from his eye the sun was born.

children.text: mukhād indraś cāgniś ca prāṇād vāyur ajāyata ||
children.translated_text: From his mouth came <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>; from his breath <s>Vāyu</s> was born.

children.text: nābhyā āsīd antarikṣaṃ śīrṣṇo dyauḥ sam avartata
children.translated_text: From his navel arose the midspace; from his head heaven took shape.

children.text: padbhyām bhūmir diśaḥ śrotrāt tathā lokāṁ akalpayan ||
children.translated_text: From his feet came the earth, from his ear the directions; likewise they fashioned the worlds.

children.text: saptāsyāsan paridhayas triḥ sapta samidhaḥ kṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Seven were its enclosing sticks, and thrice seven fuel-sticks were made,

children.text: devā yad yajñaṃ tanvānā abadhnan puruṣam paśum ||
children.translated_text: when the gods, extending the sacrifice, bound <s>Puruṣa</s> as the sacrificial animal.

children.text: yajñena yajñam ayajanta devās tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan
children.translated_text: By sacrifice the gods sacrificed to Sacrifice; those were the first <s>dharmas</s> (sacred ordinances).

children.text: te ha nākam mahimānaḥ sacanta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those powers reached the vault of heaven, where the ancient <s>Sādhyas</s> are, the gods.

children.text: Chapter 928
saṃ jāgṛvadbhir jaramāṇa idhyate dame damūnā iṣayann iḍas pade
children.translated_text: He is kindled by the wakeful ones as he matures; in the house, as lord of the house, he quickens at the seat of <s>Iḍā</s>.

children.text: viśvasya hotā haviṣo vareṇyo vibhur vibhāvā suṣakhā sakhīyate ||
children.translated_text: As Hotṛ of the whole oblation, most excellent, pervading and shining, a good friend, he is befriended.

children.text: sa darśataśrīr atithir gṛhe gṛhe vane vane śiśriye takvavīr iva
children.translated_text: Splendid in appearance, the guest has settled in every house, in every forest, like a swift hero.

children.text: janaṃ janaṃ janyo nāti manyate viśa ā kṣeti viśyo viśaṃ viśam ||
children.translated_text: Born among people, he does not despise person after person; belonging to the clans, he dwells among clan after clan.

children.text: sudakṣo dakṣaiḥ kratunāsi sukratur agne kaviḥ kāvyenāsi viśvavit
children.translated_text: Skillful through skills, by will you are well-willed; O <s>Agni</s>, as a poet, by poetry you are all-knowing.

children.text: vasur vasūnāṃ kṣayasi tvam eka id dyāvā ca yāni pṛthivī ca puṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: You alone, a treasure among treasures, dwell in all that heaven and earth sustain.

children.text: prajānann agne tava yonim ṛtviyam iḍāyās pade ghṛtavantam āsadaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing your proper womb, O <s>Agni</s>, you have sat down at the seat of <s>Iḍā</s>, rich in ghee.

children.text: ā te cikitra uṣasām ivetayo 'repasaḥ sūryasyeva raśmayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your stainless impulses have shone forth like the dawns, like the rays of the sun.

children.text: tava śriyo varṣyasyeva vidyutaś citrāś cikitra uṣasāṃ na ketavaḥ
children.translated_text: Your beauties have flashed out like the lightning of the rain-cloud, variegated like the signs of the dawns.

children.text: yad oṣadhīr abhisṛṣṭo vanāni ca pari svayaṃ cinuṣe annam āsye ||
children.translated_text: When you are sent forth into the plants and the forests, you yourself gather food into your mouth.

children.text: tam oṣadhīr dadhire garbham ṛtviyaṃ tam āpo agniṃ janayanta mātaraḥ
children.translated_text: The plants held him as the timely embryo; the waters, his mothers, generated that <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: tam it samānaṃ vaninaś ca vīrudho 'ntarvatīś ca suvate ca viśvahā ||
children.translated_text: The trees and the plants, having him within, bring forth that same one every day.

children.text: vātopadhūta iṣito vaśāṁ anu tṛṣu yad annā veviṣad vitiṣṭhase
children.translated_text: Driven by the wind and impelled, when you spread out after the dry food, following its track,

children.text: ā te yatante rathyo yathā pṛthak chardhāṃsy agne ajarāṇi dhakṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: your ageless hosts set themselves in motion separately, like charioteers, O <s>Agni</s>, as they burn.

children.text: medhākāraṃ vidathasya prasādhanam agniṃ hotāram paribhūtamam matim
children.translated_text: They choose <s>Agni</s>, maker of wisdom, arranger of the assembly, the Hotṛ, the surpassing inspired thought.

children.text: tam id arbhe haviṣy ā samānam it tam in mahe vṛṇate nānyaṃ tvat ||
children.translated_text: They choose that very same one for the small oblation and that very same one for the great; there is no other apart from you.

children.text: tvām id atra vṛṇate tvāyavo hotāram agne vidatheṣu vedhasaḥ
children.translated_text: It is you here that those devoted to you choose, O <s>Agni</s>, as Hotṛ in the assemblies, O wise one.

children.text: yad devayanto dadhati prayāṃsi te haviṣmanto manavo vṛktabarhiṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the god-seeking men, bearing oblations and with sacred grass spread, set their offerings for you,

children.text: tavāgne hotraṃ tava potram ṛtviyaṃ tava neṣṭraṃ tvam agnid ṛtāyataḥ
children.translated_text: yours, O <s>Agni</s>, is the Hotṛ's office, yours the Potṛ's office in due season; yours is the Neṣṭṛ's office, and you are the Agnīdh for the seeker of truth.

children.text: tava praśāstraṃ tvam adhvarīyasi brahmā cāsi gṛhapatiś ca no dame ||
children.translated_text: Yours is the Praśāstṛ's office; you perform the Adhvaryu's work; you are also the Brahman and the lord of the house in our home.

children.text: yas tubhyam agne amṛtāya martyaḥ samidhā dāśad uta vā haviṣkṛti
children.translated_text: The mortal who gives to you, immortal <s>Agni</s>, with kindling fuel or with the making of oblation,

children.text: tasya hotā bhavasi yāsi dūtyam upa brūṣe yajasy adhvarīyasi ||
children.translated_text: for him you become Hotṛ; you go on the embassy, you speak near him, you sacrifice, and you perform the Adhvaryu's work.

children.text: imā asmai matayo vāco asmad āṃ ṛco giraḥ suṣṭutayaḥ sam agmata
children.translated_text: These thoughts, these words from us, these verses, songs, and well-spoken praises have come together for him.

children.text: vasūyavo vasave jātavedase vṛddhāsu cid vardhano yāsu cākanat ||
children.translated_text: Seeking wealth, they have come to the wealth-giving <s>Jātavedas</s>, the increaser even amid those grown strong, in whom he delights.

children.text: imām pratnāya suṣṭutiṃ navīyasīṃ voceyam asmā uśate śṛṇotu naḥ
children.translated_text: I would speak this newer good praise for the ancient one; may he, desiring it, hear us.

children.text: bhūyā antarā hṛdy asya nispṛśe jāyeva patya uśatī suvāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: May it be more deeply within his heart to touch, like a well-dressed wife longing for her husband.

children.text: yasminn aśvāsa ṛṣabhāsa ukṣaṇo vaśā meṣā avasṛṣṭāsa āhutāḥ
children.translated_text: In him horses, bulls, steers, barren cows, and sheep have been released and offered.

children.text: kīlālape somapṛṣṭhāya vedhase hṛdā matiṃ janaye cārum agnaye ||
children.translated_text: For lovely <s>Agni</s>, the soma-sprinkled creator in the sweet drink, I generate a fair thought with my heart.

children.text: ahāvy agne havir āsye te srucīva ghṛtaṃ camvīva somaḥ
children.translated_text: The oblation has been offered, O <s>Agni</s>, into your mouth, like ghee in a ladle and like soma in a cup.

children.text: vājasaniṃ rayim asme suvīram praśastaṃ dhehi yaśasam bṛhantam ||
children.translated_text: Bestow on us prize-winning wealth, rich in heroes, praised, renowned, and great.

children.text: Chapter 929
yajñasya vo rathyaṃ viśpatiṃ viśāṃ hotāram aktor atithiṃ vibhāvasum
children.translated_text: I call for you the charioteer of the sacrifice, the lord of the peoples, the Hotṛ of the clans by night, the guest rich in radiance.

children.text: śocañchuṣkāsu hariṇīṣu jarbhurad vṛṣā ketur yajato dyām aśāyata ||
children.translated_text: Blazing among the dry tawny woods and licking them, the bull, the worshipful beacon, has reached heaven.

children.text: imam añjaspām ubhaye akṛṇvata dharmāṇam agniṃ vidathasya sādhanam
children.translated_text: Both sides have made this straight-going <s>Agni</s>, the support of <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), the accomplisher of the assembly.

children.text: aktuṃ na yahvam uṣasaḥ purohitaṃ tanūnapātam aruṣasya niṃsate ||
children.translated_text: The dawns praise the mighty one like the night, the Purohita, <s>Tanūnapāt</s> of the ruddy one.

children.text: baḍ asya nīthā vi paṇeś ca manmahe vayā asya prahutā āsur attave
children.translated_text: Indeed, we think on his guidances and away from the <s>Paṇi</s>; his branches, well offered, were there for eating.

children.text: yadā ghorāso amṛtatvam āśatād ij janasya daivyasya carkiran ||
children.translated_text: When the terrible ones reached immortality, then they proclaimed the race of the divine people.

children.text: ṛtasya hi prasitir dyaur uru vyaco namo mahy aramatiḥ panīyasī
children.translated_text: For the advance of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic truth) is heaven, broad in expanse; reverence is due to great <s>Aramati</s>, most worthy of praise.

children.text: indro mitro varuṇaḥ saṃ cikitrire 'tho bhagaḥ savitā pūtadakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s> have recognized it, and also <s>Bhaga</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s> of purified skill.

children.text: pra rudreṇa yayinā yanti sindhavas tiro mahīm aramatiṃ dadhanvire
children.translated_text: With <s>Rudra</s> as their guide the rivers go forward; they have borne great <s>Aramati</s> across.

children.text: yebhiḥ parijmā pariyann uru jrayo vi roruvaj jaṭhare viśvam ukṣate ||
children.translated_text: With these powers the one who goes around, moving widely, roars aloud and pours the whole into his belly.

children.text: krāṇā rudrā maruto viśvakṛṣṭayo divaḥ śyenāso asurasya nīḍayaḥ
children.translated_text: The active <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Maruts</s> of all peoples, are eagles of heaven, abodes of the <s>Asura</s>.

children.text: tebhiś caṣṭe varuṇo mitro aryamendro devebhir arvaśebhir arvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With them <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, and <s>Indra</s> watch among the gods, the nearer ones among the near.

children.text: indre bhujaṃ śaśamānāsa āśata sūro dṛśīke vṛṣaṇaś ca pauṃsye
children.translated_text: In <s>Indra</s> the praising ones have obtained protection; in the sun they have obtained sight, and in the bulls, manly power.

children.text: pra ye nv asyārhaṇā tatakṣire yujaṃ vajraṃ nṛṣadaneṣu kāravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those singers have now fashioned his worthy yoke, the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), in the seats of men.

children.text: sūraś cid ā harito asya rīramad indrād ā kaścid bhayate tavīyasaḥ
children.translated_text: Even the sun has set his bay steeds in motion; someone indeed fears mighty <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: bhīmasya vṛṣṇo jaṭharād abhiśvaso dive dive sahuri stann abādhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the belly of the fearsome bull, breathing hard, the overpowering one thunders day after day, unobstructed.

children.text: stomaṃ vo adya rudrāya śikvase kṣayadvīrāya namasā didiṣṭana
children.translated_text: Today offer your hymn with reverence to strong <s>Rudra</s>, to the ruler of heroes.

children.text: yebhiḥ śivaḥ svavāṁ evayāvabhir divaḥ siṣakti svayaśā nikāmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With those auspicious, self-strong, advancing aids, self-famous, he reaches heaven according to his desires.

children.text: te hi prajāyā abharanta vi śravo bṛhaspatir vṛṣabhaḥ somajāmayaḥ
children.translated_text: For they have carried wide renown for progeny; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> the bull, together with those born of <s>Soma</s>,

children.text: yajñair atharvā prathamo vi dhārayad devā dakṣair bhṛgavaḥ saṃ cikitrire ||
children.translated_text: <s>Atharvan</s> first established it with sacrifices; the gods, with their skills, and the <s>Bhṛgus</s> came to understand.

children.text: te hi dyāvāpṛthivī bhūriretasā narāśaṃsaś caturaṅgo yamo 'ditiḥ
children.translated_text: For these, Heaven and Earth rich in seed, <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> with four limbs, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Aditi</s>,

children.text: devas tvaṣṭā draviṇodā ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ pra rodasī maruto viṣṇur arhire ||
children.translated_text: the god <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Draviṇodā</s>, the <s>Ṛbhukṣaṇs</s>, the two worlds, the <s>Maruts</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, have been honored.

children.text: uta sya na uśijām urviyā kavir ahiḥ śṛṇotu budhnyo havīmani
children.translated_text: And may that <s>Ahi Budhnya</s>, the wide-ranging poet of the <s>Uśijs</s>, hear us at the invocation;

children.text: sūryāmāsā vicarantā divikṣitā dhiyā śamīnahuṣī asya bodhatam ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Sun</s> and <s>Moon</s>, moving about and dwelling in heaven, and <s>Śamī</s> with <s>Nahuṣī</s>, understand this thought.

children.text: pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṃ viśvadevyo 'pāṃ napād avatu vāyur iṣṭaye
children.translated_text: May <s>Pūṣan</s> further our course for us; may <s>Apāṃ Napāt</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, with all the gods, protect us for our desired aim.

children.text: ātmānaṃ vasyo abhi vātam arcata tad aśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Sing toward the better self and toward the wind; hear that journey, O readily invoked <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: viśām āsām abhayānām adhikṣitaṃ gīrbhir u svayaśasaṃ gṛṇīmasi
children.translated_text: We praise with songs the self-renowned overseer of all these fearless peoples,

children.text: gnābhir viśvābhir aditim anarvaṇam aktor yuvānaṃ nṛmaṇā adhā patim ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aditi</s>, unassailable, with all the divine women, young in the night, man-minded, and then the lord.

children.text: rebhad atra januṣā pūrvo aṅgirā grāvāṇa ūrdhvā abhi cakṣur adhvaram
children.translated_text: Here, by birth, the first <s>Aṅgiras</s>, loud-sounding, arose; the pressing stones lifted their eye toward the rite.

children.text: yebhir vihāyā abhavad vicakṣaṇaḥ pāthaḥ sumekaṃ svadhitir vananvati ||
children.translated_text: By them he became far-ranging and discerning; the well-fitted path, like an axe, wins the wood.

children.text: Chapter 930
mahi dyāvāpṛthivī bhūtam urvī nārī yahvī na rodasī sadaṃ naḥ
children.translated_text: O great Heaven and Earth, be spacious for us, two mighty women, two worlds, as our settled seat.

children.text: tebhir naḥ pātaṃ sahyasa ebhir naḥ pātaṃ śūṣaṇi ||
children.translated_text: Protect us with these powers, protect us with these aids in might.

children.text: yajñe yajñe sa martyo devān saparyati
children.translated_text: At every sacrifice the mortal worships the gods,

children.text: yaḥ sumnair dīrghaśruttama ā vivāsaty enān ||
children.translated_text: the one who, with favors and most far-heard praise, seeks to draw them here.

children.text: viśveṣām irajyavo devānāṃ vār mahaḥ
children.translated_text: Of all the gods, the swift ones, there is great shelter;

children.text: viśve hi viśvamahaso viśve yajñeṣu yajñiyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for all are of universal greatness, and all are worthy of sacrifice in the sacrifices.

children.text: te ghā rājāno amṛtasya mandrā aryamā mitro varuṇaḥ parijmā
children.translated_text: Those indeed are the gladdening kings of immortality: <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Parijman</s>.

children.text: kad rudro nṛṇāṃ stuto marutaḥ pūṣaṇo bhagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too, when praised, are <s>Rudra</s> of men, the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, and <s>Bhaga</s>.

children.text: uta no naktam apāṃ vṛṣaṇvasū sūryāmāsā sadanāya sadhanyā
children.translated_text: And may Night, the waters rich in strength, and <s>Sun</s> and <s>Moon</s>, dwelling together, be for our abode;

children.text: sacā yat sādy eṣām ahir budhneṣu budhnyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Ahi Budhnya</s>, the serpent of the depths, sits together with them among the foundations.

children.text: uta no devāv aśvinā śubhas patī dhāmabhir mitrāvaruṇā uruṣyatām
children.translated_text: And may the divine <s>Aśvins</s>, lords of beauty, and <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s> protect us with their abodes;

children.text: mahaḥ sa rāya eṣate 'ti dhanveva duritā ||
children.translated_text: he strives for great wealth, passing beyond troubles as beyond a desert.

children.text: uta no rudrā cin mṛḍatām aśvinā viśve devāso rathaspatir bhagaḥ
children.translated_text: And may even the <s>Rudras</s> be gracious to us: the <s>Aśvins</s>, all the gods, <s>Rathaspati</s>, and <s>Bhaga</s>,

children.text: ṛbhur vāja ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ parijmā viśvavedasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Vāja</s>, <s>Ṛbhukṣaṇ</s>, <s>Parijman</s>, the all-knowing ones.

children.text: ṛbhur ṛbhukṣā ṛbhur vidhato mada ā te harī jūjuvānasya vājinā
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Ṛbhukṣā</s>, <s>Ṛbhu</s> in the exhilaration of the rite: your two bay steeds are eager and strong,

children.text: duṣṭaraṃ yasya sāma cid ṛdhag yajño na mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he whose chant is hard to cross, whose sacrifice is distinct and not merely human.

children.text: kṛdhī no ahrayo deva savitaḥ sa ca stuṣe maghonām
children.translated_text: Make us free from harm, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>; and I praise the bountiful ones.

children.text: saho na indro vahnibhir ny eṣāṃ carṣaṇīnāṃ cakraṃ raśmiṃ na yoyuve ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> with his bearers, as among these peoples, draw the wheel as one draws a rein.

children.text: aiṣu dyāvāpṛthivī dhātam mahad asme vīreṣu viśvacarṣaṇi śravaḥ
children.translated_text: In these, O Heaven and Earth, place great fame for us among our heroes, O all-peopled ones,

children.text: pṛkṣaṃ vājasya sātaye pṛkṣaṃ rāyota turvaṇe ||
children.translated_text: refreshment for the winning of strength, refreshment together with wealth for overcoming.

children.text: etaṃ śaṃsam indrāsmayuṣ ṭvaṃ kūcit santaṃ sahasāvann abhiṣṭaye
children.translated_text: This praise that longs for <s>Indra</s>, wherever it may be, you, O mighty one, accept for aid.

children.text: sadā pāhy abhiṣṭaye medatāṃ vedatā vaso ||
children.translated_text: Always protect us for aid; let them be gracious and let them know, O good one.

children.text: etam me stomaṃ tanā na sūrye dyutadyāmānaṃ vāvṛdhanta nṛṇām
children.translated_text: This hymn of mine, shining to heaven like the sun, men have made grow through the generations,

children.text: saṃvananaṃ nāśvyaṃ taṣṭevānapacyutam ||
children.translated_text: a means of winning together, not to be shaken off, like something well fashioned.

children.text: vāvarta yeṣāṃ rāyā yuktaiṣāṃ hiraṇyayī
children.translated_text: Their golden wealth turned around, yoked with their teams;

children.text: nemadhitā na pauṃsyā vṛtheva viṣṭāntā ||
children.translated_text: their manly powers were set in the middle, stretched out as if freely.

children.text: pra tad duḥśīme pṛthavāne vene pra rāme vocam asure maghavatsu
children.translated_text: I will proclaim that among lordly benefactors to <s>Duḥśīma Pṛthavāna Vena</s> and to <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: ye yuktvāya pañca śatāsmayu pathā viśrāvy eṣām ||
children.translated_text: those who, for the yoking, made five hundred famous along our path.

children.text: adhīn nv atra saptatiṃ ca sapta ca
children.translated_text: Here now, seventy and seven as well

children.text: sadyo didiṣṭa tānvaḥ sadyo didiṣṭa pārthyaḥ sadyo didiṣṭa māyavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tānva</s> gave at once, <s>Pārthya</s> gave at once, and <s>Māyava</s> gave at once.

children.text: Chapter 931
praite vadantu pra vayaṃ vadāma grāvabhyo vācaṃ vadatā vadadbhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Let these speak forth; let us speak forth. Speak the voice for the speaking pressing stones,

children.text: yad adrayaḥ parvatāḥ sākam āśavaḥ ślokaṃ ghoṣam bharathendrāya sominaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the rocks, the mountains, swift all together, O Soma-pressers, bear the verse and cry to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: ete vadanti śatavat sahasravad abhi krandanti haritebhir āsabhiḥ
children.translated_text: These speak a hundredfold and a thousandfold; they shout with their tawny mouths.

children.text: viṣṭvī grāvāṇaḥ sukṛtaḥ sukṛtyayā hotuś cit pūrve haviradyam āśata ||
children.translated_text: The well-made pressing stones, by their good working, have reached the eating of the oblation even before the Hotṛ.

children.text: ete vadanty avidann anā madhu ny ūṅkhayante adhi pakva āmiṣi
children.translated_text: These speak; they have found the honey. They swing downward over the cooked mixture,

children.text: vṛkṣasya śākhām aruṇasya bapsatas te sūbharvā vṛṣabhāḥ prem arāviṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: eating the branch of the ruddy tree; those well-bearing bulls have roared forth.

children.text: bṛhad vadanti madireṇa mandinendraṃ krośanto 'vidann anā madhu
children.translated_text: They speak loudly, gladdening with the intoxicating drink and crying out to <s>Indra</s>; they have found the honey.

children.text: saṃrabhyā dhīrāḥ svasṛbhir anartiṣur āghoṣayantaḥ pṛthivīm upabdibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise ones, joining with their sisters, have danced, making the earth resound with their noises.

children.text: suparṇā vācam akratopa dyavy ākhare kṛṣṇā iṣirā anartiṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Like fair-winged birds they made speech near the heavenly hollow; black and impetuous, they danced.

children.text: nyaṅ ni yanty uparasya niṣkṛtam purū reto dadhire sūryaśvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Downward they go to the hollowing of the mortar; sun-bright, they have placed much seed.

children.text: ugrā iva pravahantaḥ samāyamuḥ sākaṃ yuktā vṛṣaṇo bibhrato dhuraḥ
children.translated_text: Like powerful streams they came together, yoked together, bulls bearing the yoke,

children.text: yacchvasanto jagrasānā arāviṣuḥ śṛṇva eṣām prothatho arvatām iva ||
children.translated_text: when, snorting and devouring, they roared; their thunder is heard like that of racehorses.

children.text: daśāvanibhyo daśakakṣyebhyo daśayoktrebhyo daśayojanebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: For the ten pressers, the ten bands, the ten yokes, and the ten yokings,

children.text: daśābhīśubhyo arcatājarebhyo daśa dhuro daśa yuktā vahadbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sing to the ageless ones with ten reins, to the ten shafts, and to the ten yoked bearers.

children.text: te adrayo daśayantrāsa āśavas teṣām ādhānam pary eti haryatam
children.translated_text: Those swift stones, furnished with ten mechanisms, are laid down in a lovely circuit.

children.text: ta ū sutasya somyasyāndhaso 'ṃśoḥ pīyūṣam prathamasya bhejire ||
children.translated_text: They have taken the first share of the pressed Soma drink, the nectar of the stalk.

children.text: te somādo harī indrasya niṃsate 'ṃśuṃ duhanto adhy āsate gavi
children.translated_text: Those Soma-drinkers harness <s>Indra</s>'s two bay steeds; milking the stalk, they sit upon the cow.

children.text: tebhir dugdham papivān somyam madhv indro vardhate prathate vṛṣāyate ||
children.translated_text: Having drunk the Soma honey milked by them, <s>Indra</s> grows, spreads out, and acts like a bull.

children.text: vṛṣā vo aṃśur na kilā riṣāthaneḍāvantaḥ sadam it sthanāśitāḥ
children.translated_text: Your stalk is a bull; surely you are not harmed. Rich in refreshment, you always stand at the pressings.

children.text: raivatyeva mahasā cārava sthana yasya grāvāṇo ajuṣadhvam adhvaram ||
children.translated_text: Stand lovely with wealth and greatness, for you pressing stones have favored his sacrifice.

children.text: tṛdilā atṛdilāso adrayo 'śramaṇā aśṛthitā amṛtyavaḥ
children.translated_text: The stones are crushers yet uncrushed, unwearied, unloosened, immortal;

children.text: anāturā ajarā sthāmaviṣṇavaḥ supīvaso atṛṣitā atṛṣṇajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: unafflicted, ageless, firm-spreading, well-nourished, unthirsting, not born of thirst.

children.text: dhruvā eva vaḥ pitaro yuge yuge kṣemakāmāsaḥ sadaso na yuñjate
children.translated_text: Steadfast indeed are your fathers, age after age; desiring security, they do not leave their seat.

children.text: ajuryāso hariṣāco haridrava ā dyāṃ raveṇa pṛthivīm aśuśravuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Unaging, yellow-backed, tawny-flowing, they have made heaven and earth hear with their roar.

children.text: tad id vadanty adrayo vimocane yāmann añjaspā iva ghed upabdibhiḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed the stones say at the release, on their course, as if straight-drinking with their sounds:

children.text: vapanto bījam iva dhānyākṛtaḥ pṛñcanti somaṃ na minanti bapsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: sowing as it were seed, like makers of grain, they mix the <s>Soma</s>; chewing, they do not diminish it.

children.text: sute adhvare adhi vācam akratā krīḍayo na mātaraṃ tudantaḥ
children.translated_text: At the pressed sacrifice they made their voice, nudging like children at their mother.

children.text: vi ṣū muñcā suṣuvuṣo manīṣāṃ vi vartantām adrayaś cāyamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Release now the inspired thought of the good presser; let the stones, being set in motion, roll apart.

children.text: Chapter 932
haye jāye manasā tiṣṭha ghore vacāṃsi miśrā kṛṇavāvahai nu
children.translated_text: O wife, remain here in mind, fierce one; now let us exchange our mingled words.

children.text: na nau mantrā anuditāsa ete mayas karan paratare canāhan ||
children.translated_text: These thoughts of ours, if unspoken, will bring us no delight in the days beyond.

children.text: kim etā vācā kṛṇavā tavāham prākramiṣam uṣasām agriyeva
children.translated_text: What am I to do for you with this speech? I have gone forth like the foremost of the dawns.

children.text: purūravaḥ punar astam parehi durāpanā vāta ivāham asmi ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Purūravas</s>, go back again to your home; I am hard to reach, like the wind.

children.text: iṣur na śriya iṣudher asanā goṣāḥ śatasā na raṃhiḥ
children.translated_text: Like an arrow for splendor from the quiver, like a swift prize-winner for hundreds of cattle,

children.text: avīre kratau vi davidyutan norā na māyuṃ citayanta dhunayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the flashes gleamed in a deed without heroes; the roaring ones did not make known even a bleat to me.

children.text: sā vasu dadhatī śvaśurāya vaya uṣo yadi vaṣṭy antigṛhāt
children.translated_text: She, bringing good things and vigor to her father-in-law, if <s>Uṣas</s> so wished, came from near the house.

children.text: astaṃ nanakṣe yasmiñcākan divā naktaṃ śnathitā vaitasena ||
children.translated_text: She reached the home in which she took pleasure by day, though at night she was struck by the reed-born one.

children.text: triḥ sma māhnaḥ śnathayo vaitasenota sma me 'vyatyai pṛṇāsi
children.translated_text: Three times a day you used to strike me with the reed-born shaft, and even when I was unwilling you filled me.

children.text: purūravo 'nu te ketam āyaṃ rājā me vīra tanvas tad āsīḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Purūravas</s>, I came according to your signal; hero, you were then the king over my body.

children.text: yā sujūrṇiḥ śreṇiḥ sumnaāpir hradecakṣur na granthinī caraṇyuḥ
children.translated_text: Those women, <s>Sujūrṇi</s>, <s>Śreṇi</s>, <s>Sumnaāpi</s>, lake-eyed, knot-bearing, and wandering,

children.text: tā añjayo 'ruṇayo na sasruḥ śriye gāvo na dhenavo 'navanta ||
children.translated_text: those ruddy streams ran like ointments; like milch cows they lowed for beauty.

children.text: sam asmiñ jāyamāna āsata gnā utem avardhan nadyaḥ svagūrtāḥ
children.translated_text: At his birth the divine women sat together around him, and the well-praised rivers increased him,

children.text: mahe yat tvā purūravo raṇāyāvardhayan dasyuhatyāya devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the gods strengthened you, O <s>Purūravas</s>, for the great battle, for the slaying of the <s>Dasyus</s>.

children.text: sacā yad āsu jahatīṣv atkam amānuṣīṣu mānuṣo niṣeve
children.translated_text: When the mortal man took his place among those non-human women as they cast off their garment,

children.text: apa sma mat tarasantī na bhujyus tā atrasan rathaspṛśo nāśvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they fled away from me like those crossing beyond danger; like chariot-touching horses, they were frightened.

children.text: yad āsu marto amṛtāsu nispṛk saṃ kṣoṇībhiḥ kratubhir na pṛṅkte
children.translated_text: When a mortal, touching the immortal women, does not join himself with their counsels as with settled peoples,

children.text: tā ātayo na tanvaḥ śumbhata svā aśvāso na krīḍayo dandaśānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then they adorn their own bodies like swimmers; like playful horses they bite and snap.

children.text: vidyun na yā patantī davidyod bharantī me apyā kāmyāni
children.translated_text: She flashed like falling lightning, bringing me the desirable things that are close to the waters.

children.text: janiṣṭo apo naryaḥ sujātaḥ prorvaśī tirata dīrgham āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: A manly, well-born son was born; <s>Urvaśī</s> has carried him across to long life.

children.text: jajñiṣa itthā gopīthyāya hi dadhātha tat purūravo ma ojaḥ
children.translated_text: You were born thus for protection, and you placed that strength in me, O <s>Purūravas</s>.

children.text: aśāsaṃ tvā viduṣī sasminn ahan na ma āśṛṇoḥ kim abhug vadāsi ||
children.translated_text: Knowing it, I instructed you on that very day; you did not listen to me. Why do you speak uselessly?

children.text: kadā sūnuḥ pitaraṃ jāta icchāc cakran nāśru vartayad vijānan
children.translated_text: When will the son, once born, seek his father, rolling a tear as he recognizes him?

children.text: ko dampatī samanasā vi yūyod adha yad agniḥ śvaśureṣu dīdayat ||
children.translated_text: Who would separate a husband and wife of one mind, when <s>Agni</s> has shone among the in-laws?

children.text: prati bravāṇi vartayate aśru cakran na krandad ādhye śivāyai
children.translated_text: I answer you: he will roll a tear, yet he will not cry out for kindly welfare.

children.text: pra tat te hinavā yat te asme parehy astaṃ nahi mūra māpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall send forth to you what of yours is with us. Go home; foolish one, you have not reached me.

children.text: sudevo adya prapated anāvṛt parāvatam paramāṃ gantavā u
children.translated_text: May the well-favored one today fall away uncovered; surely he is going to the farthest distance.

children.text: adhā śayīta nirṛter upasthe 'dhainaṃ vṛkā rabhasāso adyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then let him lie in the lap of <s>Nirṛti</s>; then let the ravenous wolves devour him.

children.text: purūravo mā mṛthā mā pra papto mā tvā vṛkāso aśivāsa u kṣan
children.translated_text: O <s>Purūravas</s>, do not die, do not fall away; let not the inauspicious wolves eat you.

children.text: na vai straiṇāni sakhyāni santi sālāvṛkāṇāṃ hṛdayāny etā ||
children.translated_text: For friendships with women truly do not exist; these are the hearts of she-wolves.

children.text: yad virūpācaram martyeṣv avasaṃ rātrīḥ śaradaś catasraḥ
children.translated_text: When, changing my form, I moved among mortals and dwelt for four autumn nights,

children.text: ghṛtasya stokaṃ sakṛd ahna āśnāṃ tād evedaṃ tātṛpāṇā carāmi ||
children.translated_text: I ate a single drop of ghee once a day; satisfied with just that, I now wander.

children.text: antarikṣaprāṃ rajaso vimānīm upa śikṣāmy urvaśīṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: I, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, approach <s>Urvaśī</s>, who fills the midspace and measures out the realm of light.

children.text: upa tvā rātiḥ sukṛtasya tiṣṭhān ni vartasva hṛdayaṃ tapyate me ||
children.translated_text: The gift won by good deeds stands near you. Turn back; my heart is burning.

children.text: iti tvā devā ima āhur aiḍa yathem etad bhavasi mṛtyubandhuḥ
children.translated_text: Thus these gods say to you, O <s>Aila</s>: since in this way you are bound to death,

children.text: prajā te devān haviṣā yajāti svarga u tvam api mādayāse ||
children.translated_text: your offspring shall worship the gods with oblation, and you yourself shall rejoice in heaven.

children.text: Chapter 933
pra te mahe vidathe śaṃsiṣaṃ harī pra te vanve vanuṣo haryatam madam
children.translated_text: For you, at the great assembly, I shall praise the two bay horses; for you I seek the desirable exhilaration of the winning one.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ na yo haribhiś cāru secata ā tvā viśantu harivarpasaṃ giraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like ghee, the fair one is poured out with the bay steeds; let the songs enter you, whose form is tawny.

children.text: hariṃ hi yonim abhi ye samasvaran hinvanto harī divyaṃ yathā sadaḥ
children.translated_text: For they have sounded together toward the tawny womb, impelling the two bay horses as toward a heavenly seat.

children.text: ā yam pṛṇanti haribhir na dhenava indrāya śūṣaṃ harivantam arcata ||
children.translated_text: They fill him as cows do with milk by means of the tawny ones; sing the tawny strength for <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: so asya vajro harito ya āyaso harir nikāmo harir ā gabhastyoḥ
children.translated_text: That iron thunderbolt of his is tawny; tawny is his desire, tawny in both his hands.

children.text: dyumnī suśipro harimanyusāyaka indre ni rūpā haritā mimikṣire ||
children.translated_text: Radiant, fair-lipped, with tawny anger as his arrow, the tawny forms have fixed themselves in <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: divi na ketur adhi dhāyi haryato vivyacad vajro harito na raṃhyā
children.translated_text: In heaven the desirable beacon has been set; the tawny thunderbolt spread wide as if with speed.

children.text: tudad ahiṃ hariśipro ya āyasaḥ sahasraśokā abhavaddharimbharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The iron, tawny-lipped one struck the serpent; the bearer of tawny power became thousand-flamed.

children.text: tvaṃ tvam aharyathā upastutaḥ pūrvebhir indra harikeśa yajvabhiḥ
children.translated_text: You, you were delighted when praised by the former sacrificers, O <s>Indra</s> of tawny hair.

children.text: tvaṃ haryasi tava viśvam ukthyam asāmi rādho harijāta haryatam ||
children.translated_text: You take delight; all that is worthy of recitation is yours. O tawny-born one, let the unsurpassed gift be desirable.

children.text: tā vajriṇam mandinaṃ stomyam mada indraṃ rathe vahato haryatā harī
children.translated_text: In exhilaration the two tawny horses carry on the chariot <s>Indra</s>, the thunderbolt-bearer, the rejoicing and praiseworthy one.

children.text: purūṇy asmai savanāni haryata indrāya somā harayo dadhanvire ||
children.translated_text: Many pressings have delighted him; the tawny <s>Somas</s> have streamed forth for <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: araṃ kāmāya harayo dadhanvire sthirāya hinvan harayo harī turā
children.translated_text: For desire the tawny ones have streamed forth; the tawny ones drive on the two swift bay horses for the steadfast one.

children.text: arvadbhir yo haribhir joṣam īyate so asya kāmaṃ harivantam ānaśe ||
children.translated_text: He who gladly comes with the bay coursers, with the racers, he has attained this desire of his, rich in bay steeds.

children.text: hariśmaśārur harikeśa āyasas turaspeye yo haripā avardhata
children.translated_text: The tawny-bearded, tawny-haired, strong one, who as drinker of the tawny draught grew mighty in the swift pressing,

children.text: arvadbhir yo haribhir vājinīvasur ati viśvā duritā pāriṣaddharī ||
children.translated_text: he who, rich in prize-winning strength, with the bay coursers, shall carry the two bay steeds across all hardships.

children.text: sruveva yasya hariṇī vipetatuḥ śipre vājāya hariṇī davidhvataḥ
children.translated_text: His two bay mares fly apart like ladles; his two tawny cheek-pieces shake for the prize.

children.text: pra yat kṛte camase marmṛjaddharī pītvā madasya haryatasyāndhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When, at the prepared bowl, he has rubbed down the two bay steeds after drinking the intoxicating, lovely draught,

children.text: uta sma sadma haryatasya pastyor atyo na vājaṃ harivāṁ acikradat
children.translated_text: and indeed in the dwelling of the lovely home, <s>Indra</s> with the bays cried out like a racehorse for the prize.

children.text: mahī ciddhi dhiṣaṇāharyad ojasā bṛhad vayo dadhiṣe haryataś cid ā ||
children.translated_text: For even the great inspired thought delighted in strength; you have taken to yourself great vital power, even what is lovely.

children.text: ā rodasī haryamāṇo mahitvā navyaṃ navyaṃ haryasi manma nu priyam
children.translated_text: Coming to the two worlds in tawny splendor through your greatness, you delight again and again in the new, dear hymn.

children.text: pra pastyam asura haryataṃ gor āviṣ kṛdhi haraye sūryāya ||
children.translated_text: O mighty lord, make manifest for the tawny one, for the sun, the lovely stall of the cow.

children.text: ā tvā haryantam prayujo janānāṃ rathe vahantu hariśipram indra
children.translated_text: Let the yoked steeds of men carry you here as you are longed for, O <s>Indra</s> of the tawny cheeks, in the chariot.

children.text: pibā yathā pratibhṛtasya madhvo haryan yajñaṃ sadhamāde daśoṇim ||
children.translated_text: Drink of the filled sweet draught, as you desire, delighting in the tenfold sacrifice at the common feast.

children.text: apāḥ pūrveṣāṃ harivaḥ sutānām atho idaṃ savanaṃ kevalaṃ te
children.translated_text: You have drunk the pressed draughts of former men, O <s>Indra</s> with the bay steeds; and now this pressing is solely yours.

children.text: mamaddhi somam madhumantam indra satrā vṛṣañ jaṭhara ā vṛṣasva ||
children.translated_text: Rejoice in the honeyed <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>; at once, O bull, let it pour into your belly.

children.text: Chapter 934
yā oṣadhīḥ pūrvā jātā devebhyas triyugam purā
children.translated_text: The plants that were born of old for the gods, three ages before,

children.text: manai nu babhrūṇām ahaṃ śataṃ dhāmāni sapta ca ||
children.translated_text: of those brown ones I now know a hundred and seven abodes.

children.text: śataṃ vo amba dhāmāni sahasram uta vo ruhaḥ
children.translated_text: A hundred are your abodes, O mothers, and a thousand are your shoots.

children.text: adhā śatakratvo yūyam imam me agadaṃ kṛta ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, O you of a hundred powers, make this remedy for me.

children.text: oṣadhīḥ prati modadhvam puṣpavatīḥ prasūvarīḥ
children.translated_text: Rejoice in response, O plants, flower-bearing, fruitful,

children.text: aśvā iva sajitvarīr vīrudhaḥ pārayiṣṇvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: winning together like mares, O creepers that carry one across.

children.text: oṣadhīr iti mātaras tad vo devīr upa bruve
children.translated_text: I address you as plants, as mothers; this I say to you, O goddesses.

children.text: saneyam aśvaṃ gāṃ vāsa ātmānaṃ tava pūruṣa ||
children.translated_text: May I win horse, cow, garment, and your very self, O person.

children.text: aśvatthe vo niṣadanam parṇe vo vasatiṣ kṛtā
children.translated_text: Your seat is in the aśvattha tree; your dwelling has been made in the leaf.

children.text: gobhāja it kilāsatha yat sanavatha pūruṣam ||
children.translated_text: You are indeed sharers in cattle when you win a person.

children.text: yatrauṣadhīḥ samagmata rājānaḥ samitāv iva
children.translated_text: Where the plants come together like kings in an assembly,

children.text: vipraḥ sa ucyate bhiṣag rakṣohāmīvacātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the inspired one is called a physician, demon-slayer and chaser-away of disease.

children.text: aśvāvatīṃ somāvatīm ūrjayantīm udojasam
children.translated_text: I have found all the plants, possessing horses, possessing <s>Soma</s>, strengthening, and full of force,

children.text: āvitsi sarvā oṣadhīr asmā ariṣṭatātaye ||
children.translated_text: for this man's freedom from injury.

children.text: ucchuṣmā oṣadhīnāṃ gāvo goṣṭhād iverate
children.translated_text: The powers of the plants rise up like cows from the cattle-stall,

children.text: dhanaṃ saniṣyantīnām ātmānaṃ tava pūruṣa ||
children.translated_text: as they seek to win wealth and your very self, O person.

children.text: iṣkṛtir nāma vo mātātho yūyaṃ stha niṣkṛtīḥ
children.translated_text: Your mother is named Cure; therefore you are removers of affliction.

children.text: sīrāḥ patatriṇī sthana yad āmayati niṣ kṛtha ||
children.translated_text: You are streams, winged ones; when someone is sick, you drive it out.

children.text: ati viśvāḥ pariṣṭhā stena iva vrajam akramuḥ
children.translated_text: They have stepped across all enclosures, like a thief across a pen.

children.text: oṣadhīḥ prācucyavur yat kiṃ ca tanvo rapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The plants have driven away whatever is a bodily defect.

children.text: yad imā vājayann aham oṣadhīr hasta ādadhe
children.translated_text: When I take these vigorous plants in my hand,

children.text: ātmā yakṣmasya naśyati purā jīvagṛbho yathā ||
children.translated_text: the spirit of disease perishes beforehand, as if seized by life.

children.text: yasyauṣadhīḥ prasarpathāṅgam aṅgam paruṣ paruḥ
children.translated_text: O plants, for the one through whose limb after limb and joint after joint you creep,

children.text: tato yakṣmaṃ vi bādhadhva ugro madhyamaśīr iva ||
children.translated_text: from him drive away disease, like a fierce middleman.

children.text: sākaṃ yakṣma pra pata cāṣeṇa kikidīvinā
children.translated_text: Fall away together with disease, with the blue jay and the kikidīvi bird.

children.text: sākaṃ vātasya dhrājyā sākaṃ naśya nihākayā ||
children.translated_text: Perish together with the rush of the wind, together with the disappearing mist.

children.text: anyā vo anyām avatv anyānyasyā upāvata
children.translated_text: Let one of you aid another; let each aid each other.

children.text: tāḥ sarvāḥ saṃvidānā idam me prāvatā vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All of you, in agreement, have helped this speech of mine.

children.text: yāḥ phalinīr yā aphalā apuṣpā yāś ca puṣpiṇīḥ
children.translated_text: Those that bear fruit, those that are fruitless, those without flowers, and those that flower,

children.text: bṛhaspatiprasūtās tā no muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those plants, impelled by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, let them release us from distress.

children.text: muñcantu mā śapathyād atho varuṇyād uta
children.translated_text: Let them release me from a curse, and also from what belongs to <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: atho yamasya paḍbīśāt sarvasmād devakilbiṣāt ||
children.translated_text: and also from the fetter of <s>Yama</s>, from every offense against the gods.

children.text: avapatantīr avadan diva oṣadhayas pari
children.translated_text: Flying down, speaking forth from heaven, O plants,

children.text: yaṃ jīvam aśnavāmahai na sa riṣyāti pūruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the living person whom we touch with you does not come to harm.

children.text: yā oṣadhīḥ somarājñīr bahvīḥ śatavicakṣaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Those many plants, ruled by <s>Soma</s>, hundred-eyed,

children.text: tāsāṃ tvam asy uttamāraṃ kāmāya śaṃ hṛde ||
children.translated_text: among them you are the best: bring welfare to the heart for our desire.

children.text: yā oṣadhīḥ somarājñīr viṣṭhitāḥ pṛthivīm anu
children.translated_text: Those plants, ruled by <s>Soma</s>, spread out over the earth,

children.text: bṛhaspatiprasūtā asyai saṃ datta vīryam ||
children.translated_text: impelled by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, grant power to this woman.

children.text: mā vo riṣat khanitā yasmai cāhaṃ khanāmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: May your digger not be harmed, nor the one for whom I dig you.

children.text: dvipac catuṣpad asmākaṃ sarvam astv anāturam ||
children.translated_text: Let every two-footed and four-footed creature of ours be free from sickness.

children.text: yāś cedam upaśṛṇvanti yāś ca dūram parāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Those that hear this, and those that have gone far away,

children.text: sarvāḥ saṃgatya vīrudho 'syai saṃ datta vīryam ||
children.translated_text: let all the plants come together and grant power to this woman.

children.text: oṣadhayaḥ saṃ vadante somena saha rājñā
children.translated_text: The plants converse with <s>Soma</s> the king:

children.text: yasmai kṛṇoti brāhmaṇas taṃ rājan pārayāmasi ||
children.translated_text: For whomever the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> acts, O king, him we carry across.

children.text: tvam uttamāsy oṣadhe tava vṛkṣā upastayaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the highest, O plant; the trees are your attendants.

children.text: upastir astu so 'smākaṃ yo asmāṁ abhidāsati ||
children.translated_text: Let him be our attendant, the one who seeks to attack us.

children.text: Chapter 935
bṛhaspate prati me devatām ihi mitro vā yad varuṇo vāsi pūṣā
children.translated_text: O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, come toward my deity, whether you are <s>Mitra</s> or <s>Varuṇa</s> or <s>Pūṣan</s>,

children.text: ādityair vā yad vasubhir marutvān sa parjanyaṃ śantanave vṛṣāya ||
children.translated_text: or together with the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s>; let him pour rain for <s>Śantanu</s>.

children.text: ā devo dūto ajiraś cikitvān tvad devāpe abhi mām agacchat
children.translated_text: The god, the swift and knowing messenger, has come to me from you, O <s>Devāpi</s>.

children.text: pratīcīnaḥ prati mām ā vavṛtsva dadhāmi te dyumatīṃ vācam āsan ||
children.translated_text: Turn back toward me, facing this way; I place bright speech in your mouth.

children.text: asme dhehi dyumatīṃ vācam āsan bṛhaspate anamīvām iṣirām
children.translated_text: Place bright speech in our mouth, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, free from sickness and impelling,

children.text: yayā vṛṣṭiṃ śantanave vanāva divo drapso madhumāṁ ā viveśa ||
children.translated_text: by which we may win rain for <s>Śantanu</s>; a honeyed drop has entered from heaven.

children.text: ā no drapsā madhumanto viśantv indra dehy adhirathaṃ sahasram
children.translated_text: Let honeyed drops enter us; O <s>Indra</s>, grant a thousand fit for the chariot.

children.text: ni ṣīda hotram ṛtuthā yajasva devān devāpe haviṣā saparya ||
children.translated_text: Sit down as priest; sacrifice in due season; O <s>Devāpi</s>, worship the gods with oblation.

children.text: ārṣṭiṣeṇo hotram ṛṣir niṣīdan devāpir devasumatiṃ cikitvān
children.translated_text: The seer <s>Devāpi Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, knowing the favor of the gods, sat down as priest.

children.text: sa uttarasmād adharaṃ samudram apo divyā asṛjad varṣyā abhi ||
children.translated_text: He released the heavenly waters, the rain-bearing streams, from the upper ocean down to the lower.

children.text: asmin samudre adhy uttarasminn āpo devebhir nivṛtā atiṣṭhan
children.translated_text: In this ocean, in the upper one, the waters, held back by the gods, stood still.

children.text: tā adravann ārṣṭiṣeṇena sṛṣṭā devāpinā preṣitā mṛkṣiṇīṣu ||
children.translated_text: They ran forth, released by <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, sent by <s>Devāpi</s> among the cleansing streams.

children.text: yad devāpiḥ śantanave purohito hotrāya vṛtaḥ kṛpayann adīdhet
children.translated_text: When <s>Devāpi</s>, priest for <s>Śantanu</s>, chosen for the office of <s>hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), kindling with compassion, made the fire blaze,

children.text: devaśrutaṃ vṛṣṭivaniṃ rarāṇo bṛhaspatir vācam asmā ayacchat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, bestowing god-heard, rain-winning speech, granted speech to him.

children.text: yaṃ tvā devāpiḥ śuśucāno agna ārṣṭiṣeṇo manuṣyaḥ samīdhe
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, you whom <s>Devāpi Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, the shining mortal, kindled,

children.text: viśvebhir devair anumadyamānaḥ pra parjanyam īrayā vṛṣṭimantam ||
children.translated_text: approved by all the gods, send forth rain-bearing <s>Parjanya</s>.

children.text: tvām pūrva ṛṣayo gīrbhir āyan tvām adhvareṣu puruhūta viśve
children.translated_text: The former seers came to you with songs; to you all come in the sacrifices, O much-invoked one.

children.text: sahasrāṇy adhirathāny asme ā no yajñaṃ rohidaśvopa yāhi ||
children.translated_text: Bring thousands fit for the chariot to us; come near to our sacrifice, O red-horsed one.

children.text: etāny agne navatir nava tve āhutāny adhirathā sahasrā
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, these ninety-nine thousand chariot-loads have been offered into you.

children.text: tebhir vardhasva tanvaḥ śūra pūrvīr divo no vṛṣṭim iṣito rirīhi ||
children.translated_text: With them grow in your many bodies, O hero; impelled, pour rain from heaven for us.

children.text: etāny agne navatiṃ sahasrā sam pra yaccha vṛṣṇa indrāya bhāgam
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, hand over these ninety thousand to mighty <s>Indra</s> as his share.

children.text: vidvān patha ṛtuśo devayānān apy aulānaṃ divi deveṣu dhehi ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the paths, the divine ways according to season, place also <s>Aulāna</s> among the gods in heaven.

children.text: agne bādhasva vi mṛdho vi durgahāpāmīvām apa rakṣāṃsi sedha
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, drive away hostilities, drive away hardships; drive away disease and repel the demons.

children.text: asmāt samudrād bṛhato divo no 'pām bhūmānam upa naḥ sṛjeha ||
children.translated_text: From this great ocean of heaven, release here to us the abundance of waters.

children.text: Chapter 936
kaṃ naś citram iṣaṇyasi cikitvān pṛthugmānaṃ vāśraṃ vāvṛdhadhyai
children.translated_text: Whom, O knowing one, do you urge on as wondrous, wide-striding and bellowing, so that he may grow?

children.text: kat tasya dātu śavaso vyuṣṭau takṣad vajraṃ vṛtraturam apinvat ||
children.translated_text: What gift of his might, at daybreak, fashioned the thunderbolt that overcomes <s>Vṛtra</s> and made it swell?

children.text: sa hi dyutā vidyutā veti sāma pṛthuṃ yonim asuratvā sasāda
children.translated_text: He indeed moves with flashing lightning and knows the chant; by his divine power he has sat in the broad womb.

children.text: sa sanīḍebhiḥ prasahāno asya bhrātur na ṛte saptathasya māyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: With those of one nest he overpowers; not without the devices of this seventh brother does he prevail.

children.text: sa vājaṃ yātāpaduṣpadā yan svarṣātā pari ṣadat saniṣyan
children.translated_text: He goes toward the prize by a trackless path; when winning the sun, he sits around it, seeking to gain it.

children.text: anarvā yacchatadurasya vedo ghnañchiśnadevāṁ abhi varpasā bhūt ||
children.translated_text: He held the treasure of the four-cornered one without horses; striking the phallus-worshippers, he became manifest in his form.

children.text: sa yahvyo 'vanīr goṣv arvā juhoti pradhanyāsu sasriḥ
children.translated_text: He pours the mighty streams among the cows, a ready helper in the foremost contests.

children.text: apādo yatra yujyāso 'rathā droṇyaśvāsa īrate ghṛtaṃ vāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where the footless are yoked, where the chariotless and trough-horsed ones move, they carry ghee.

children.text: sa rudrebhir aśastavāra ṛbhvā hitvī gayam āreavadya āgāt
children.translated_text: He, with the <s>Rudras</s>, warding off the unpraised, strong, leaving the household, came far away from blame.

children.text: vamrasya manye mithunā vivavrī annam abhītyārodayan muṣāyan ||
children.translated_text: I think of <s>Vamra</s>'s uncovered pair: attacking and stealing, they made the food cry out.

children.text: sa id dāsaṃ tuvīravam patir dan ṣaḍakṣaṃ triśīrṣāṇaṃ damanyat
children.translated_text: He, as lord, subdued the loudly roaring <s>Dāsa</s>, six-eyed and three-headed.

children.text: asya trito nv ojasā vṛdhāno vipā varāham ayoagrayā han ||
children.translated_text: <s>Trita</s>, growing now by this one's power, struck the boar with an iron-tipped weapon.

children.text: sa druhvaṇe manuṣa ūrdhvasāna ā sāviṣad arśasānāya śarum
children.translated_text: For <s>Druhvaṇa</s>, the man rising upright, he shot an arrow at <s>Arśasāna</s>.

children.text: sa nṛtamo nahuṣo 'smat sujātaḥ puro 'bhinad arhan dasyuhatye ||
children.translated_text: Most manly, well-born among the <s>Nahuṣas</s>, he broke forts for us when worthy in the slaying of the <s>Dasyus</s>.

children.text: so abhriyo na yavasa udanyan kṣayāya gātuṃ vidan no asme
children.translated_text: Like one of the cloud seeking water for grass, he found for us a path to dwelling and settlement.

children.text: upa yat sīdad induṃ śarīraiḥ śyeno 'yopāṣṭir hanti dasyūn ||
children.translated_text: When the eagle, with his bodies, sat near the pressed <s>Soma</s>, the iron-beaked one struck the <s>Dasyus</s>.

children.text: sa vrādhataḥ śavasānebhir asya kutsāya śuṣṇaṃ kṛpaṇe parādāt
children.translated_text: With overpowering powers, for <s>Kutsa</s> he handed <s>Śuṣṇa</s> over in distress.

children.text: ayaṃ kavim anayacchasyamānam atkaṃ yo asya sanitota nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: This one led the poet who was being praised, the garment that was his, and also the winner of men.

children.text: ayaṃ daśasyan naryebhir asya dasmo devebhir varuṇo na māyī
children.translated_text: This wondrous one, granting gifts with his manly helpers, is like <s>Varuṇa</s>, a maker of divine powers among the gods.

children.text: ayaṃ kanīna ṛtupā avedy amimītāraruṃ yaś catuṣpāt ||
children.translated_text: This young guardian of order was recognized; he measured out the hostile four-footed one.

children.text: asya stomebhir auśija ṛjiśvā vrajaṃ darayad vṛṣabheṇa piproḥ
children.translated_text: By his praises, <s>Auśija Ṛjiśvan</s> split open <s>Pipru</s>'s enclosure with the bull.

children.text: sutvā yad yajato dīdayad gīḥ pura iyāno abhi varpasā bhūt ||
children.translated_text: When, having pressed <s>Soma</s>, the worshipful song shone out, going before the forts, he became manifest in form.

children.text: evā maho asura vakṣathāya vamrakaḥ paḍbhir upa sarpad indram
children.translated_text: Thus, for the growth of the great <s>Asura</s>, <s>Vamraka</s> crawled up to <s>Indra</s> with his feet.

children.text: sa iyānaḥ karati svastim asmā iṣam ūrjaṃ sukṣitiṃ viśvam ābhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he comes on, may he bring us welfare, food, strength, good dwelling, and every blessing.

children.text: Chapter 937
indra dṛhya maghavan tvāvad id bhuja iha stutaḥ sutapā bodhi no vṛdhe
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>, stand firm; O bountiful one, such aid as yours is here. Praised here, drinker of the pressed <s>Soma</s>, be awake for our increase.

children.text: devebhir naḥ savitā prāvatu śrutam ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Savitṛ</s> with the gods protect our fame; we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: bharāya su bharata bhāgam ṛtviyam pra vāyave śucipe krandadiṣṭaye
children.translated_text: Bring well, O <s>Bharatas</s>, the timely share for the pure-drinking <s>Vāyu</s>, for the loudly rejoicing one.

children.text: gaurasya yaḥ payasaḥ pītim ānaśa ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: He has attained the drinking of the cow's milk; we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: ā no devaḥ savitā sāviṣad vaya ṛjūyate yajamānāya sunvate
children.translated_text: May the god <s>Savitṛ</s> impel aid for us, for the straight-moving sacrificer who presses <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: yathā devān pratibhūṣema pākavad ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: So that we may fitly adorn the gods, like a cooked offering, we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: indro asme sumanā astu viśvahā rājā somaḥ suvitasyādhy etu naḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> be well-disposed toward us every day; may King <s>Soma</s> come over us for good guidance.

children.text: yathā yathā mitradhitāni saṃdadhur ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: As they have established the bonds of friendship one by one, we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: indra ukthena śavasā parur dadhe bṛhaspate pratarītāsy āyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, with hymn and might, has set down many supports; O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, you are the carrier across of life.

children.text: yajño manuḥ pramatir naḥ pitā hi kam ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice, and <s>Manu</s>, and wise thought are indeed our father; we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: indrasya nu sukṛtaṃ daivyaṃ saho 'gnir gṛhe jaritā medhiraḥ kaviḥ
children.translated_text: Now the divine good deed and strength of <s>Indra</s>: <s>Agni</s> in the house is the singer, the wise poet.

children.text: yajñaś ca bhūd vidathe cārur antama ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: And the sacrifice has become lovely and nearest in the assembly; we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: na vo guhā cakṛma bhūri duṣkṛtaṃ nāviṣṭyaṃ vasavo devaheḍanam
children.translated_text: We have not committed much hidden evil against you, nor the worst god-offending act, O <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: mākir no devā anṛtasya varpasa ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: Let not the form of falsehood be ours, O gods; we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: apāmīvāṃ savitā sāviṣan nyag varīya id apa sedhantv adrayaḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Savitṛ</s> drive disease downward; may the broad stones drive it away from us.

children.text: grāvā yatra madhuṣud ucyate bṛhad ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: Where the pressing-stone is loudly called honey-sweet and great, we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: ūrdhvo grāvā vasavo 'stu sotari viśvā dveṣāṃsi sanutar yuyota
children.translated_text: Let the pressing-stone stand upright for the presser, O <s>Vasus</s>; keep all hatreds far away.

children.text: sa no devaḥ savitā pāyur īḍya ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: May that praiseworthy god <s>Savitṛ</s> be our protector; we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: ūrjaṃ gāvo yavase pīvo attana ṛtasya yāḥ sadane kośe aṅgdhve
children.translated_text: O cows, eat rich pasture for strength, you who lick at the seat of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), in the vessel.

children.text: tanūr eva tanvo astu bheṣajam ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: Let the body itself be medicine for the body; we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: kratuprāvā jaritā śaśvatāṁ ava indra id bhadrā pramatiḥ sutāvatām
children.translated_text: O protector of inspired power, aid the singer forever; <s>Indra</s> indeed is the gracious favor of those who have pressed <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: pūrṇam ūdhar divyaṃ yasya siktaya ā sarvatātim aditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ||
children.translated_text: His heavenly udder is full, with its outpourings; we choose <s>Aditi</s> for complete wholeness.

children.text: citras te bhānuḥ kratuprā abhiṣṭiḥ santi spṛdho jaraṇiprā adhṛṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Bright is your radiance, O protector of inspired power; your help is wondrous. Rival powers exist, protected by praise and hard to assail.

children.text: rajiṣṭhayā rajyā paśva ā gos tūtūrṣati pary agraṃ duvasyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the straightest line the worshipper strives to pass beyond the foremost point, toward the cattle and the cow.

children.text: Chapter 938
ud budhyadhvaṃ samanasaḥ sakhāyaḥ sam agnim indhvam bahavaḥ sanīḍāḥ
children.translated_text: Awaken with one mind, friends; kindle <s>Agni</s> together, many of you sharing one dwelling.

children.text: dadhikrām agnim uṣasaṃ ca devīm indrāvato 'vase ni hvaye vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I call <s>Dadhikrā</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and the divine <s>Uṣas</s>, and I call you, accompanied by <s>Indra</s>, for help.

children.text: mandrā kṛṇudhvaṃ dhiya ā tanudhvaṃ nāvam aritraparaṇīṃ kṛṇudhvam
children.translated_text: Make your thoughts pleasing; stretch them out. Make a boat that crosses with oars.

children.text: iṣkṛṇudhvam āyudhāraṃ kṛṇudhvam prāñcaṃ yajñam pra ṇayatā sakhāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Make it ready; make the holder of weapons. Lead the sacrifice forward, friends.

children.text: yunakta sīrā vi yugā tanudhvaṃ kṛte yonau vapateha bījam
children.translated_text: Yoke the ploughs; spread out the yokes. Sow the seed here in the prepared womb.

children.text: girā ca śruṣṭiḥ sabharā asan no nedīya it sṛṇyaḥ pakvam eyāt ||
children.translated_text: Let praise and willing hearing be richly laden for us; may the sickles come nearer to the ripe crop.

children.text: sīrā yuñjanti kavayo yugā vi tanvate pṛthak
children.translated_text: The inspired poets yoke the ploughs; they stretch the yokes apart, each separately.

children.text: dhīrā deveṣu sumnayā ||
children.translated_text: The wise men do so among the gods, seeking their good favor.

children.text: nir āhāvān kṛṇotana saṃ varatrā dadhātana
children.translated_text: Make the troughs; fasten the straps together.

children.text: siñcāmahā avatam udriṇaṃ vayaṃ suṣekam anupakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: Let us pour into the raised well, easy to pour from and not failing.

children.text: iṣkṛtāhāvam avataṃ suvaratraṃ suṣecanam
children.translated_text: Prepare the trough, the well with good straps and good pouring.

children.text: udriṇaṃ siñce akṣitam ||
children.translated_text: I pour into the raised, inexhaustible well.

children.text: prīṇītāśvān hitaṃ jayātha svastivāhaṃ ratham it kṛṇudhvam
children.translated_text: Satisfy the horses; win the prize that has been set. Make the chariot a bearer of welfare.

children.text: droṇāhāvam avatam aśmacakram aṃsatrakośaṃ siñcatā nṛpāṇam ||
children.translated_text: Sprinkle the trough-vessel, the stone-wheeled well, the shoulder-boxed protector of men.

children.text: vrajaṃ kṛṇudhvaṃ sa hi vo nṛpāṇo varma sīvyadhvam bahulā pṛthūni
children.translated_text: Make a cattle-pen, for he is your protector of men; sew broad and thick armor.

children.text: puraḥ kṛṇudhvam āyasīr adhṛṣṭā mā vaḥ susroc camaso dṛṃhatā tam ||
children.translated_text: Make iron strongholds, unassailable. Let not your cup leak; make it firm.

children.text: ā vo dhiyaṃ yajñiyāṃ varta ūtaye devā devīṃ yajatāṃ yajñiyām iha
children.translated_text: I turn your sacrificial thought here for aid; O gods, worship here the divine, sacrificial goddess of the worshippers.

children.text: sā no duhīyad yavaseva gatvī sahasradhārā payasā mahī gauḥ ||
children.translated_text: May that great cow, going as if to pasture, milk for us with a thousand streams of milk.

children.text: ā tū ṣiñca harim īṃ dror upasthe vāśībhis takṣatāśmanmayībhiḥ
children.translated_text: Pour the tawny one here into the lap of the wooden vessel; shape it with stone axes.

children.text: pari ṣvajadhvaṃ daśa kakṣyābhir ubhe dhurau prati vahniṃ yunakta ||
children.translated_text: Embrace it all around with ten girths; yoke the bearer to both shafts.

children.text: ubhe dhurau vahnir āpibdamāno 'ntar yoneva carati dvijāniḥ
children.translated_text: The bearer, drinking at both shafts, moves between them like one twice-born in a womb.

children.text: vanaspatiṃ vana āsthāpayadhvaṃ ni ṣū dadhidhvam akhananta utsam ||
children.translated_text: Set the forest-tree in the wood; lay it down well, after digging out the spring.

children.text: kapṛn naraḥ kapṛtham ud dadhātana codayata khudata vājasātaye
children.translated_text: Men, raise up the kapṛn and the kapṛtha; drive it on, dig, for the winning of strength.

children.text: niṣṭigryaḥ putram ā cyāvayotaya indraṃ sabādha iha somapītaye ||
children.translated_text: Bring down the son of <s>Niṣṭigrya</s>; bring <s>Indra</s> here under pressure for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: Chapter 939
pra te ratham mithūkṛtam indro 'vatu dhṛṣṇuyā
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> boldly protect your chariot, made together.

children.text: asminn ājau puruhūta śravāyye dhanabhakṣeṣu no 'va ||
children.translated_text: In this contest, O much-invoked one, in the winning of wealth, aid us for fame.

children.text: ut sma vāto vahati vāso 'syā adhirathaṃ yad ajayat sahasram
children.translated_text: And indeed the wind carries her garment, when she won a thousand upon the chariot.

children.text: rathīr abhūn mudgalānī gaviṣṭau bhare kṛtaṃ vy aced indrasenā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mudgalānī</s> became the charioteer in the quest for cattle; in the contest <s>Indra</s>'s army accomplished the deed and made it clear.

children.text: antar yaccha jighāṃsato vajram indrābhidāsataḥ
children.translated_text: Hold back the thunderbolt of the one who wishes to slay, O <s>Indra</s>, of the one who attacks.

children.text: dāsasya vā maghavann āryasya vā sanutar yavayā vadham ||
children.translated_text: Whether it is the weapon of a <s>Dāsa</s> or of an <s>Ārya</s>, O bountiful one, drive it far away.

children.text: udno hradam apibaj jarhṛṣāṇaḥ kūṭaṃ sma tṛṃhad abhimātim eti
children.translated_text: Exulting, he drank the water of the lake; he broke the peak and goes against the hostile force.

children.text: pra muṣkabhāraḥ śrava icchamāno 'jiram bāhū abharat siṣāsan ||
children.translated_text: The heavy-scrotumed one, seeking fame and wishing to win, carried his swift forelegs forward.

children.text: ny akrandayann upayanta enam amehayan vṛṣabham madhya ājeḥ
children.translated_text: As they came up, they made this bull bellow; they made him urinate in the middle of the contest.

children.text: tena sūbharvaṃ śatavat sahasraṃ gavām mudgalaḥ pradhane jigāya ||
children.translated_text: With him <s>Mudgala</s> won the well-bearing prize, a hundred and a thousand cows, in the battle for spoil.

children.text: kakardave vṛṣabho yukta āsīd avāvacīt sārathir asya keśī
children.translated_text: At <s>Kakardava</s> the bull was yoked; his hairy charioteer called out downward.

children.text: dudher yuktasya dravataḥ sahānasa ṛcchanti ṣmā niṣpado mudgalānīm ||
children.translated_text: As the yoked one ran together with the wagon, the tracks of its feet reached <s>Mudgalānī</s>.

children.text: uta pradhim ud ahann asya vidvān upāyunag vaṃsagam atra śikṣan
children.translated_text: And, knowing how, he struck up its rim; there, learning the way, he yoked the vaṃsaga.

children.text: indra ud āvat patim aghnyānām araṃhata padyābhiḥ kakudmān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> aided the lord of the inviolable cows; the humped one sped onward with his feet.

children.text: śunam aṣṭrāvy acarat kapardī varatrāyāṃ dārv ānahyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: The top-knotted one moved auspiciously under the goad, tied with a wooden piece to the strap.

children.text: nṛmṇāni kṛṇvan bahave janāya gāḥ paspaśānas taviṣīr adhatta ||
children.translated_text: Doing heroic deeds for many people, touching the cows, he assumed mighty powers.

children.text: imaṃ tam paśya vṛṣabhasya yuñjaṃ kāṣṭhāyā madhye drughaṇaṃ śayānam
children.translated_text: Look at this yoking of the bull, the wooden implement lying in the middle of the course,

children.text: yena jigāya śatavat sahasraṃ gavām mudgalaḥ pṛtanājyeṣu ||
children.translated_text: by which <s>Mudgala</s> won a hundred and a thousand cows in contests of battle.

children.text: āre aghā ko nv itthā dadarśa yaṃ yuñjanti tam v ā sthāpayanti
children.translated_text: Evil is far away. Who has seen such a thing? The one whom they yoke, they also set in place.

children.text: nāsmai tṛṇaṃ nodakam ā bharanty uttaro dhuro vahati pradediśat ||
children.translated_text: They bring him neither grass nor water; set foremost, he carries the upper shaft.

children.text: parivṛkteva patividyam ānaṭ pīpyānā kūcakreṇeva siñcan
children.translated_text: Like a rejected wife finding a husband, swollen and sprinkling as if with a little wheel,

children.text: eṣaiṣyā cid rathyā jayema sumaṅgalaṃ sinavad astu sātam ||
children.translated_text: may this very chariot-course come to us; may we win. Let the acquisition be auspicious and well-flowing.

children.text: tvaṃ viśvasya jagataś cakṣur indrāsi cakṣuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Indra</s>, are the eye of the whole moving world, the eye of sight itself.

children.text: vṛṣā yad ājiṃ vṛṣaṇā siṣāsasi codayan vadhriṇā yujā ||
children.translated_text: When, as a bull with bull companions, you seek to win the contest, driving on with a gelded yoke-mate.

children.text: Chapter 940
āśuḥ śiśāno vṛṣabho na bhīmo ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaś carṣaṇīnām
children.translated_text: Swift, sharpening himself, terrible like a bull, striking again and again, shaker of peoples,

children.text: saṃkrandano 'nimiṣa ekavīraḥ śataṃ senā ajayat sākam indraḥ ||
children.translated_text: shouting, unwinking, sole hero, <s>Indra</s> conquered a hundred armies together.

children.text: saṃkrandanenānimiṣeṇa jiṣṇunā yutkāreṇa duścyavanena dhṛṣṇunā
children.translated_text: With the shouter, the unwinking victor, with the battle-cry, hard to dislodge and bold,

children.text: tad indreṇa jayata tat sahadhvaṃ yudho nara iṣuhastena vṛṣṇā ||
children.translated_text: win that with <s>Indra</s>; stand firm in that, men of battle, with the virile archer.

children.text: sa iṣuhastaiḥ sa niṣaṅgibhir vaśī saṃsraṣṭā sa yudha indro gaṇena
children.translated_text: He is with bowmen, he is with quiver-bearers, masterful; <s>Indra</s> with the troop is the one who joins battle.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭajit somapā bāhuśardhy ugradhanvā pratihitābhir astā ||
children.translated_text: Winner in the clash, drinker of <s>Soma</s>, strong in his arms, fierce-bowed, he shoots with arrows set in place.

children.text: bṛhaspate pari dīyā rathena rakṣohāmitrāṁ apabādhamānaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, drive around with your chariot, slayer of demons, driving enemies away.

children.text: prabhañjan senāḥ pramṛṇo yudhā jayann asmākam edhy avitā rathānām ||
children.translated_text: Shatter the armies; crush them in battle, winning the fight. Become the protector of our chariots.

children.text: balavijñāya sthaviraḥ pravīraḥ sahasvān vājī sahamāna ugraḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing strength, ancient, foremost in valor, powerful, prize-winning, overpowering, fierce,

children.text: abhivīro abhisatvā sahojā jaitram indra ratham ā tiṣṭha govit ||
children.translated_text: heroic over heroes, true in assault, born of might: O <s>Indra</s>, mount the victorious, cow-winning chariot.

children.text: gotrabhidaṃ govidaṃ vajrabāhuṃ jayantam ajma pramṛṇantam ojasā
children.translated_text: This breaker of cattle-pens, finder of cows, thunderbolt-armed, conquering the course and crushing by force,

children.text: imaṃ sajātā anu vīrayadhvam indraṃ sakhāyo anu saṃ rabhadhvam ||
children.translated_text: follow him, O kinsmen, in heroic power; take hold of <s>Indra</s>, O friends, together.

children.text: abhi gotrāṇi sahasā gāhamāno 'dayo vīraḥ śatamanyur indraḥ
children.translated_text: Forcing his way by might into the cattle-pens, pitiless, heroic, a hundredfold in fury, <s>Indra</s>

children.text: duścyavanaḥ pṛtanāṣāḍ ayudhyo 'smākaṃ senā avatu pra yutsu ||
children.translated_text: hard to dislodge, conqueror of battle-lines, not to be fought against, let him protect our armies in the combats.

children.text: indra āsāṃ netā bṛhaspatir dakṣiṇā yajñaḥ pura etu somaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> is their leader; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the reward; let Sacrifice and <s>Soma</s> go in front.

children.text: devasenānām abhibhañjatīnāṃ jayantīnām maruto yantv agram ||
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Maruts</s> go at the head of the divine armies that break through, that win the victory.

children.text: indrasya vṛṣṇo varuṇasya rājña ādityānām marutāṃ śardha ugram
children.translated_text: Of mighty <s>Indra</s>, of king <s>Varuṇa</s>, of the <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>, the fierce troop,

children.text: mahāmanasām bhuvanacyavānāṃ ghoṣo devānāṃ jayatām ud asthāt ||
children.translated_text: of the great-minded ones who shake the worlds, the victory-shout of the gods has risen.

children.text: ud dharṣaya maghavann āyudhāny ut satvanām māmakānām manāṃsi
children.translated_text: Raise up, O <s>Maghavan</s>, the weapons; raise up the spirits of my warriors.

children.text: ud vṛtrahan vājināṃ vājināny ud rathānāṃ jayatāṃ yantu ghoṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Raise up, O <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer, the vigor of the prize-winners; let the shouts of the conquering chariots rise up.

children.text: asmākam indraḥ samṛteṣu dhvajeṣv asmākaṃ yā iṣavas tā jayantu
children.translated_text: Let <s>Indra</s> be ours amid encounters and standards; let the arrows that are ours be victorious.

children.text: asmākaṃ vīrā uttare bhavantv asmāṁ u devā avatā haveṣu ||
children.translated_text: Let our heroes become superior; and you gods, protect us in our invocations.
